title: Chart engine core (scene, axes, interaction, LOD)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer renders every high-value surface in the product - candles, footprint cells with per-cell text, volume/delta profiles, a 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap at 100 ms cadence, big-trade bubbles, draggable order/position lines and the whole drawing kit - through a **fully custom WebGL2 chart engine** (owner decision #1, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`). No surveyed charting library provides those natively.

This Epic is the engine **chassis**: milestones **M1 (chassis parity)** and **M2 (data plane)** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` 15, plus the DOM-mirror accessibility layer that `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 makes a binding engine-design constraint rather than a later bolt-on. Everything else in R1 and R2 renders through what is built here: E12 bar builders and series, E13 indicators, E14 drawing tools, E15 layouts, E18 footprint, E21 DOM + heatmap. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` 13 names E11 as a single point of failure on the critical path `E02 -> E06 -> E11 -> E12 -> E18 -> E26 -> E38 -> E44 -> E46 -> GA`.

The research warning this Epic exists to honour: **parity work on the "boring things"** (pan/zoom momentum, axis decimation, multi-pane sync, crosshair, DPI correctness, transform math) costs 4-8 weeks and must finish *before* any order-flow feature can pay off. It is scheduled first, deliberately.

The package is **framework-free** (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16): `packages/chart-engine` contains no React, no application state, no `fetch` and no Bybit knowledge. React bindings are a thin layer in `apps/web`.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Engineering (91 pts across Sprint 05 - Sprint 07)**

- **Package and API** - `packages/chart-engine` with the public surface of `26-chart-engine-design.md` 8 (`Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`), thin React bindings in `apps/web` (E11-T01).
- **Worker plane** - OffscreenCanvas render worker, main-to-worker message protocol ( 6), `RunMode.inline` fallback, transferable typed-array data path (E11-T02); columnar stores with an append/patch/prepend mutation API returning affected index ranges (E11-T03).
- **Scene and loop** - fixed-depth scene graph `Chart -> Pane -> Layer -> Series` with `DATA|LAYOUT|STYLE|TRANSFORM` dirty flags; `FrameScheduler` with a 16.7 ms budget, bounded 4 ms/frame data-mutation drain, time-based animation, render-on-demand parking (E11-S01).
- **GL backend** - WebGL2 context management, capability probe selecting `RenderProfile` (`full`/`reduced`/`degraded-2d`), program/VAO/buffer lifecycle, context-loss recovery within 2 s with no data loss wired to **SCR-048** (E11-S02, E11-T05).
- **Transform and scales** - bar-index vs time space, `indexToScreen`/`timeToScreen`/`screenToIndex`/`screenToPrice`, tick-integer price precision with a `priceOrigin` uniform (E11-S03); price scale linear / log / percent / inverted with autoscale, manual lock and the **SCR-043** context menus (E11-S05, `US-CHART-007`).
- **Interaction** - pan/zoom with cursor-anchored zoom, kinetic momentum honouring reduced-motion, wheel/pointer coalescing to <= 1 batch per frame, full keyboard equivalents (E11-S04, `US-CHART-006`).
- **Axes** - `CMP-188 PriceAxis`, `CMP-189 TimeAxis` with label decimation, device-pixel snapping, drag-to-rescale plus a keyboard rescale path (E11-S06).
- **Crosshair and readout** - `CMP-190 Crosshair`, `CMP-197 ChartTooltip`, `CMP-226 BarCountdown`, magnet modes, sync-group broadcast (E11-S07, `US-CHART-008`).
- **Hit-testing** - analytic structural index plus a 64 px uniform-grid object index, edge-triggered pick messages, <= 1 ms budget (E11-S08).
- **Multi-pane** - pane stacking with a shared time axis, height ratios, `CMP-196 MultiChartLinker` sync groups for time range / crosshair / price level (E11-S09).
- **DPI** - backing store at `devicePixelRatio` (heatmap layer capped at 2), hairline snapping, resize and DPR-change handling (E11-S10).
- **Text** - SDF glyph atlas pipeline, two-pass EDT generation, shelf packing, IndexedDB caching, instanced glyph batching, outline variant for legibility over saturated fills (E11-S11, spike E11-K01 closing open item **O2**).
- **LOD** - candle L0/L1/L2 ladder with **min/max-preserving** decimation, 15 % hysteresis dead band, automatic step-down after 3 consecutive over-budget frames, the degradation ladder of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` 4.4 (E11-S12).
- **Accessibility layer** - windowed DOM mirror, keyboard data cursor, throttled live regions, canvas `role="img"` rolling label (E11-S13); the **SCR-045** data-table alternative (E11-S14, `US-CHART-014`).
- **Memory and paging** - `MemoryGovernor` (600 MB budget, 5 s sampling, step-down over 70 %), `visibleRangeNeedsData` paging, days-to-load memory estimate feeding **SCR-044** and **SCR-047** (E11-S15, `US-CHART-010`).
- **Quality infrastructure** - theme/LUT/density ingestion (E11-T04), golden-image harness on SwiftShader (E11-T08), benchmark harness promoted to a **required CI check** with B1/B2/B5/B6/B9/B10 baselines (E11-T06), the **SCR-046** diagnostics feed (E11-T07), engine API freeze plus ADR amendment (E11-T09).

**User stories covered:** `US-CHART-006` (pan/zoom/autoscale, Must), `US-CHART-007` (log and percentage scales, Must/Should), `US-CHART-008` (crosshair, OHLCV readout, countdown, Must), `US-CHART-010` (days-to-load control, Must), `US-CHART-014` (accessible chart data alternative, Must). `US-CHART-001` (candlestick rendering, Must) is **jointly owned**: E11 provides the render loop, the LOD ladder, the empty/error states and the frame budget it is measured against; the candle series itself ships in E12.

**Screens:** SCR-030 (chart panel chassis), SCR-031 (chart settings - scale section), SCR-043 (price/time-scale context menus), SCR-044 (Go to date), SCR-045 (data-table alternative), SCR-046 (diagnostics overlay), SCR-047 (empty / no-data), SCR-048 (error state).

**Components:** CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-198 ChartWatermark / PaneBackground, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-226 BarCountdown, CMP-228 PreviewTile (settings previews), CMP-004 FocusRing (mirror-node focus ring).

**Engineering 102 pts** across E11-K01, E11-S01..S15 and E11-T01..T09 (of which E11-T06 and E11-T08 carry the `qa` label because they are test infrastructure, and are counted on the QA capacity line). **Design 32 pts** (E11-D01..D09), **QA 33 pts** (E11-Q01..Q07 plus T06/T08), **Security 8 pts** (E11-X01..X03) are tracked against their own capacity lines, per the planning brief's separate design/QA/security capacity rule.

## Out of scope
- **Series rendering** of candles / bars / line / area / baseline / Heikin-Ashi and all bar builders - E12 (`US-CHART-001`..`005`, `US-CHART-011`). E11 ships the plugin seam they register against, not the plugins.
- Indicators and indicator plugin implementations - E13. Footprint series, profiles, heatmap, bubbles, Deep-Stats - E18/E19/E20/E21/E22. Drawing tools - E14. Layouts, workspaces and chart templates (`US-CHART-012`) - E15. Order and position line overlays (`US-CHART-013`) - E31.
- Session / day-boundary configuration (`US-CHART-009`) - owned by E12 alongside the bar builders that consume it.
- Backend data supply: `GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `GET /api/v1/market/footprint`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and the `bars.*` / `trades.*` / `ticker.*` WS topics - E17 and E12. The engine consumes typed arrays handed to it; it never performs I/O.
- WebGPU backend (explicit future seam only), SVG output, server-side rendering, third-party distribution of the package.
- Android and any mobile client (owner decision 2026-09-14). No separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Frame budget met and enforced
  Given the CI benchmark harness runs scenario B5 on the reference machine in Electron
  When 100k bars plus all R1 overlays render through the engine chassis
  Then p95 frame time is <= 16.6 ms and p50 frame rate is >= 60 fps
  And a change regressing any hard-budget p95 by more than 5 % fails the required check

Scenario: 30 fps floor holds under worst case
  Given a 6-chart layout with every R1 overlay enabled (benchmark B6)
  When the frame budget is exceeded for 3 consecutive frames
  Then the engine steps down one LOD level per the degradation ladder and logs the step
  And frame rate never falls below 30 fps and no trading-critical overlay is shed

Scenario: Context loss recovers without data loss
  Given a chart with 100k bars, 3 panes and an active crosshair
  When WEBGL_lose_context is forced
  Then SCR-048 announces "Graphics context lost - restoring..." through a role="alert" region
  And a fully correct scene is restored from the DataModel within 2 s with zero data loss

Scenario: The chart is fully operable without a mouse
  Given a chart pane has keyboard focus
  When the user navigates with arrow keys, Home/End, +/- and Alt+T
  Then the data cursor steps bar by bar and the OHLCV readout is announced in a throttled live region
  And the SCR-045 data table exposes the same data at the same fidelity as the canvas

Scenario: The engine package stays framework-free
  Given packages/chart-engine is built
  When its dependency graph is inspected in CI
  Then it imports no React, no application store, no fetch/XHR/WS client and no Bybit-specific type
  And a PR introducing any of those fails the boundary check

Scenario: Engine degrades rather than fails without WebGL2
  Given a machine whose capability probe reports no WebGL2
  When a chart is mounted
  Then RenderProfile degraded-2d is selected and candles, axes and lines render through Canvas 2D
  And the user is told which capabilities are reduced and why, never shown a blank canvas
```

## Technical notes / design

M1 exits on benchmarks **B1** and **B2** green plus golden images for candles/axes/crosshair; M2 exits on **B7** and **B9** green plus integration tests against fixtures.

**Risks carried by this Epic.**

| Risk | Exposure | Mitigation inside this Epic |
|---|---|---|
| R2 Render performance | The whole product renders through this chassis | Benchmark harness becomes a required CI check in E11-T06 during Sprint 07; B1/B2 gate M1 exit; per-stage attribution makes regressions same-day diagnosable |
| R8 Browser/GPU compat | WebGL2 availability, driver quirks, WebView2 behaviour | Capability probe plus `degraded-2d` (E11-T05), GPU matrix exploratory (E11-Q07), golden images on SwiftShader (E11-T08) |
| R10 Key-person | One graphics-capable engineer carries the subsystem | Pairing rule on S01/S02/S11; every subsystem documented in `26-chart-engine-design.md`; no undocumented shader tricks |
| R5 Scope | Chassis parity expanding into series work | The Out-of-scope boundary above; series plugins live in E12 and register through the seam |

**Exit criteria (Epic level, verified end-to-end, not per child).**
1. Benchmarks B1, B2, B5, B6, B9 and B10 green on the reference machine in Electron, recorded as artefacts and enforced as a required check.
2. The 30 fps floor holds under the B6 worst case using the documented degradation ladder.
3. Forced `WEBGL_lose_context` restores a correct scene within 2 s with no data loss (R1 exit criterion 8).
4. Every chart is operable without a mouse; NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist (R1 exit criterion 9).
5. `packages/chart-engine` at >= 85 % line coverage; property tests hold over 10k cases for transform round-trips, LOD selection and decimation extreme-preservation.
6. Golden images exist per layer and per theme including `degraded-2d`, at <= 0.1 % pixel diff.
7. Public engine API frozen and documented; `26-chart-engine-design.md` matches the shipped implementation; open item **O2** closed by an ADR amendment.
8. Zero open P0/P1 bugs against E11 scope; STRIDE findings triaged; QA and design sign-off recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Test plan
Epic-level rollup; per-child plans live on the children.
- **Unit / property** (Vitest + fast-check, >= 85 % lines): transform round-trips, log/percent projection, LOD thresholds with hysteresis, min/max decimation preservation, ring-buffer wrap, prefix-sum indexing, momentum integration, viewport clamping, colour-LUT generation.
- **Golden image** (Playwright + SwiftShader, <= 0.1 % diff): axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD, `degraded-2d`, per theme.
- **Contract**: engine consumes only `packages/protocol` types; `tsd` / `tsc --noEmit` compile-time assertion; framework-free boundary check.
- **Integration**: engine plus a fake WS server against a recorded fixture session - snapshot, deltas, sequence-gap resync, paging.
- **Interaction** (Playwright, web and Electron): pan, zoom, crosshair, axis drag, keyboard cursor, multi-pane sync.
- **Accessibility**: axe-core zero violations on all chart routes; live-region announcement assertions; reduced-motion behaviour; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes.
- **Performance**: B1, B2, B5, B6, B7, B9, B10 at 3 repetitions, medians of p95 compared to baseline.
- **Fuzz / robustness**: malformed frames, out-of-order sequences, NaN/Infinity prices, zero-size canvas, mid-flight DPR change, injected context loss.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data only** (public, non-PII, no financial credentials). The engine holds no secrets, no API keys and no account identifiers beyond opaque ids passed for overlay labels in later Epics.

STRIDE surface (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** - malicious or corrupt binary frames reaching the decoder, shader/asset supply chain, IndexedDB-cached SDF atlas poisoning. **Denial of service** - unbounded data volume exhausting GPU/JS memory, pathological zoom or LOD causing allocation storms, worker starvation. **Information disclosure** - the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and error correlation ids leaking internals into screenshots. **Repudiation** - not applicable (no state mutation). **Spoofing / elevation of privilege** - not applicable at engine level; topic authorization belongs to E17.

Controls: strict typed-array bounds validation at every ingest point; NaN/Infinity rejection; hard `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings enforced by the `MemoryGovernor`; no `eval` and no dynamic shader source derived from data; pinned dependencies under npm-audit/Dependabot gates; CSP-compatible worker construction. The `security` label is required on E11-S02, E11-T02, E11-T03 and E11-S15.

## Accessibility notes
Binding, not advisory: `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 makes the three-layer canvas strategy an engine-design constraint. This Epic ships all three layers - the windowed DOM mirror ( 6.1, E11-S13), throttled live regions ( 6.2, E11-S13) and the data-table alternative ( 6.3, E11-S14, SCR-045) - plus `role="img"` with a rolling `aria-label` on the canvas (CMP-180), keyboard rescale on both axes (CMP-188/189), a keyboard-driven crosshair as the *primary* path with hover as the pointer convenience layer (CMP-190), reduced-motion-respecting momentum, and non-colour-only encodings throughout. WCAG 2.2 AA; axe-core zero violations on all R1 chart routes; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist (E11-Q05, E11-D07).

## Performance notes
Hard gates: budget **#1** (16.6 ms p95 frame with 100k bars plus a 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms) and budget **#2** (30 fps floor under worst case). Budget **#14** (100 ms heatmap cadence) is prepared by this Epic's texture-streaming seam and gated in E21. The per-stage allocation of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` 4.3 is instrumented stage by stage, not just totalled. Memory <= 600 MB per chart instance (requirement R7), with the modelled chassis footprint about 116 MB for the 100k-bar case. Steady state <= 18 draw calls per pane and <= 40 for a 3-pane chart. Zero GC-triggering allocations in the frame path, asserted by an allocation-counter test. Regression gate: a p95 regression above 5 % on any hard budget fails the build.

## Observability
- `frame` stats message (fps, p50/p95 frame time, draw calls, triangles, uploaded bytes/s, LOD levels, GPU memory estimate, render profile) sampled at 1 Hz in production and fully in bench mode, surfaced by **SCR-046** and copied into bug reports.
- Structured `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` spans at all nine 4.3 stage boundaries, correlated with the backend span id carried on the WS envelope.
- Engine error events with stable codes: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN`, `ENGINE_FRAME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, each with a `recoverable` flag and surfaced on SCR-048 with a copyable correlation id.
- Analytics events emitted from engine hooks but owned by the app layer: `chart.error_shown`, `diagnostics.overlay_toggled`, `diagnostics.snapshot_copied`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child Stories/Tasks/Spikes Done (100 % rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria verified end-to-end on the reference machine with evidence attached.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % on `packages/chart-engine` and >= 80 % on the `apps/web` binding layer; no baseline regression.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated to shipped behaviour; ADR amendment recorded for open item **O2**; engine API documented in the package README and Storybook.
- [ ] Storybook stories exist for CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199 and CMP-226 per their catalogue entries.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on all chart routes; NVDA and VoiceOver manual passes signed off (E11-Q05, E11-D07).
- [ ] perf: B1/B2/B5/B6/B9/B10 recorded against budgets; the benchmark required check is live in CI.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged with Owner sign-off on any accepted risk, Security engineer sign-off comment (E11-X03).
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded (E11-Q06).
- [ ] design: D02-D07 signed off >= 2 sprints before their consuming stories; design-QA pass complete (E11-D08).
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review against **staging (demo)**; retro notes filed as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- **E06** - chart-engine spike and ADR. The custom-engine decision must be confirmed (or the Lightweight-Charts fallback adopted and R1 re-cut) before this Epic starts; the M0 benchmark harness and seeded fixture generator built there are extended here.
- **E10** - app shell and Electron host. The engine needs a mount point, a theme provider and the Electron runtime it is benchmarked in.
- **E17** - market-data WS protocol and binary framing. The worker data plane decodes frames in that wire format; `packages/protocol` types are the contract the engine compiles against.
- **E05** (design system v0) - tokens, font and density scales consumed by E11-T04 and every design ticket.
- **E02** (monorepo scaffold) - transitively via E06.

**Blocks:** E12 (bars and series), E13 (indicators), E14 (drawings), E15 (layouts), E21 (DOM and heatmap), and through them E18/E19/E20/E22/E23/E25/E26.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-*` per child (for example `feat/chart-engine-core-scene-graph`). No long-lived Epic branch: every child merges to `main` independently behind the `chart.engine.v2` feature flag, default **on** in dev/staging and **off** in prod until the R1 PRR. PR size guidance <= 400 LOC diff; shader files and generated atlases are excluded from the count but reviewed by the code owner.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Run UX research on chart navigation, scale control and keyboard-first charting
body:
## Context
Everything else in E11 is parity work against a category norm the owner already has strong opinions about, formed over years in TradingView and DeepCharts. Designing the chart chassis from first principles would be both slower and worse than designing it from **observed** expectations — and getting pan/zoom feel, scale-lock behaviour or crosshair magnet wrong is the kind of defect that is felt on every single interaction but rarely reported as a bug ("it just feels off").

This research ticket exists because E11 introduces **two genuinely new interaction models** that have no obvious prior art to copy, and guessing at them would be expensive: (1) the **keyboard-first charting path** — a data cursor, keyboard rescale and keyboard crosshair that must be a *primary* path rather than a compliance afterthought (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6, CMP-190); and (2) the **equal-status data table** (SCR-045, `US-CHART-014`), which the standard insists is "not a stripped-down compliance minimum".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Participants**: the owner plus 2–3 account managers (the actual user population — `10-personas.md` Pavel/Marta/Viewer), plus **at least one screen-reader user** and one low-vision user recruited for the keyboard-first and table sessions. A11y sessions are not optional and not merged into the trader sessions.
- **Method**: 60-minute moderated sessions, split competitive walkthrough (TradingView, DeepCharts, Bookmap on the owner's own setup) + task-based think-aloud on a clickable prototype.
- **Research questions**, each with a decision attached so the study cannot end inconclusively:
  1. Which pan/zoom gesture bindings are expected, and which are *muscle memory* (wheel = zoom time vs scroll time is the highest-cost thing to get wrong)? -> fixes E11-S04's default bindings.
  2. What should happen to autoscale when the price axis is dragged — disengage silently, disengage with a badge, or ask? -> fixes `US-CHART-006`'s lock-badge behaviour and E11-S05.
  3. Is the crosshair magnet expected on by default, and snapping to OHLC or to the nearest price level? -> fixes E11-S07's default magnet mode.
  4. What does a keyboard-first user actually need to *do* on a chart, in priority order, and what is the minimum cursor-stepping vocabulary (bar, price level, page, extreme)? -> fixes E11-S13's key map.
  5. Is the data table a reading surface, a verification surface, or a working surface — and what column set makes it equal-status rather than a fallback? -> fixes E11-S14's default columns and its row actions.
  6. What does "aggregated" need to communicate so a trader trusts a zoomed-out chart? -> fixes E11-S12's disclosure wording.
- **Deliverables**: a findings report with a per-question decision, a prioritised issues list, session recordings/notes, and a one-page "chart interaction principles" summary pinned in the Figma file.
- **Competitive teardown** of scale menus and go-to-date flows in the three reference products, captured as annotated screenshots.

## Out of scope
- Visual design and hi-fi screens — **E11-D02**/**D03**/**D04**.
- Order-flow surfaces (footprint, heatmap, DOM) — researched in E18/E21's own design tracks.
- Quantitative A/B testing — the user population is single digits; this is qualitative research and an A/B test would be statistically meaningless.
- Usability testing of the *built* product — **E11-Q06**'s exploratory pass and the design-QA in E11-D08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every research question ends in a decision, not a summary
  Given the six research questions above
  When the findings report is delivered
  Then each question has an explicit recommended decision, the evidence behind it and the E11 ticket it feeds
  And any question that could not be resolved is escalated with a named owner and a date, never left open

Scenario: Accessibility is researched with real users, not simulated
  Given the keyboard-first and data-table research questions
  When the sessions are conducted
  Then at least one screen-reader user and one low-vision user participated
  And their findings are reported as first-class results, not an appendix

Scenario: Findings reach the tickets that need them
  Given the findings report is signed off
  When E11-S04, E11-S05, E11-S07, E11-S12, E11-S13 and E11-S14 are inspected
  Then each carries the relevant decision and a link to the report
  And no engineering ticket is left guessing at a default that was researched

Scenario: Research lands before design needs it
  Given design work E11-D02 starts in Sprint 04
  Then this research is Done by the end of Sprint 03
  And a delay here is escalated immediately, because it pushes every downstream design and the design-ahead rule with it
```

## Technical notes / design
**Prototype fidelity is deliberately low** for gesture questions and deliberately high for the keyboard/table questions. Gesture feel cannot be tested in a clickable prototype at all — questions 1 and 3 are tested on the **E06 spike build** (a real engine prototype with real inertia), because asking someone how zoom should feel while looking at a static mock produces confident answers that do not survive contact with a scroll wheel. Questions 4 and 5 are tested on a semi-functional HTML prototype with real screen-reader output, since the only thing that matters there is what NVDA actually says.

**Session structure**: 10 min context, 20 min competitive walkthrough (their own tools, their own symbols — the owner's real workspace, not a demo account), 25 min task-based think-aloud, 5 min wrap. Tasks phrased as goals ("find where price rejected this level yesterday"), never as instructions ("click the go-to-date button"), so the navigation strategy is observed rather than dictated.

**Analysis**: thematic coding of session notes, with any finding that contradicts an existing planned behaviour flagged explicitly in the report — the contradictions are the valuable part and are easy to lose in a tidy summary.

## Test plan
Research validity rather than software testing:
- Task success/failure and time-on-task recorded per participant per task.
- Findings triangulated across at least two participants before becoming a recommendation; single-source findings are reported as such and marked lower confidence.
- The competitive teardown is verified against the live products at session time, not from memory or documentation.
- The report is reviewed by the CDO and the accessibility specialist before sign-off.

## Security notes
Research data handling: session recordings and notes contain participant identity and, for the owner's sessions, **live account context on screen** (balances, positions, symbols). Controls: recordings stored in the private research drive with access limited to the design and product leads; **the owner's sessions are conducted on the demo environment wherever possible**, and any accidental live-account capture is redacted before the recording is stored. No recording leaves the organisation. Consent captured in writing before each session, including consent for a11y participants to be recorded using their own assistive technology configuration.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is partly *about* accessibility, and the method has to match:
- At least one screen-reader user and one low-vision participant, recruited as participants rather than as reviewers.
- Sessions run with the participant's **own** AT setup and configuration, because the defaults people actually run with differ substantially from a clean install.
- Findings feed E11-S13 (keyboard cursor, live-region cadence) and E11-S14 (table as an equal-status surface) directly.
- Research materials themselves are accessible: the prototype is keyboard-operable, and consent forms and task sheets are provided in an accessible format.

## Performance notes
N/A — no runtime performance implications. One research-side note: the gesture-feel sessions must run on the **reference machine** (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §1), because inertia and zoom feel are inseparable from frame rate, and a finding gathered on a laggy laptop would be a finding about the laptop.

## Observability
N/A. The findings report itself is the artefact, linked from E11 and from each consuming ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.

## Dependencies
- **E05** — design-system v0 provides the prototype's visual vocabulary.
- **E06** — the engine spike build is the only surface on which gesture feel can honestly be tested.
- Blocks **E11-D02** (and through it D03/D04/D06), and directly informs E11-S04, S05, S07, S12, S13, S14.

## Branch
`design/chart-engine-ux-research` (artefacts in Figma + the research drive; repo branch only for the findings summary committed to `docs/research/`).

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-043, SCR-044, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-049 (each entry's states, a11y, performance and design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7 — CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226, CMP-228, CMP-004
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` — tokens, theming, motion, density, a11y
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom), §6 (canvas a11y), §7 (reduced motion)
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`, `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 (visual encoding rules, density modes)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 (design-ready gate)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-006, 007, 008, 010, 014
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md` (owner, account manager, viewer)
- `docs/research/24-owner-decisions.md` (owner decision #1: custom engine)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-004, CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226, CMP-228, SCR-030
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/chart-engine-ux-research`
- PR title: `E11-D01: Run UX research on chart navigation, scale control and keyboard-first charting`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E11-D01)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, design, ux-research

**Done means**
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E11-D01 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

title: Design the chart chassis: pane chrome, axes, crosshair, legend, diagnostics
body:
## Context
This is the visual foundation every other chart surface is built on. **SCR-030** is described in `14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the spine of the product", and its chrome — axes, crosshair, legend, pane backgrounds, the bar countdown — is what E12's series, E13's indicators, E14's drawings, E18's footprint and E21's heatmap all render *inside*. A chassis decision made loosely here is re-litigated in six Epics.

SCR-030 carries a hard gate that this ticket must respect: the **mandatory WebGL engine spike gate** (owner decision #2.2.1) — the screen "may not be signed off until the custom-engine spike demonstrates, on the reference machine and recorded as evidence attached to the sign-off," 100k bars with footprint text at >=60 fps, sustained 100 ms-cadence updates with no dropped frames over 10 minutes, and the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2. **E06** produces that evidence; this ticket attaches it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-030 chassis** (chrome only, not order-flow content): panel header, pane stack, gutters, the time-axis strip, the price-axis gutter, the Deep Stats strip slot, the sub-pane divider treatment.
- **CMP-188 PriceAxis** — tick density, label typography (`font.mono`), the drag-to-rescale affordance **and its keyboard equivalent**, the scale-lock badge, and the log/percent/inverted mode indicators.
- **CMP-189 TimeAxis** — label decimation rules at each zoom level (what is dropped first, and what is never dropped), session/day-boundary markers, maintenance-window markers, the auto/fit control cluster.
- **CMP-190 Crosshair** + **CMP-197 ChartTooltip** — line treatment, axis label pills, magnet-mode affordance, tooltip content layout and its collision/flip rules near pane edges.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown** — normal, warning (amber in the final 10 s per `US-CHART-008`) and closed states; the warn state **adds a word, not just a colour**.
- **CMP-199 ChartLegend** — per-pane legend with swatch, value, visibility toggle; the "many indicators" overflow behaviour.
- **CMP-198 ChartWatermark / PaneBackground** — grid line hierarchy (major/minor), watermark treatment, pane background per theme.
- **Multi-pane chrome** — splitters (with their keyboard-resize affordance), collapsed-pane stubs, pane focus indication, per-pane labelling (feeds E11-S09).
- **SCR-046 diagnostics overlay** — layout, the threshold treatment **paired with text**, the sparkline row, the copy-diagnostics control.
- All of the above in **dark, light and high-contrast** themes and in **comfortable, compact and dense** density modes — the density triple is one coherent switch (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 5), so the three density variants must be drawn, not described.
- **States** per SCR-030: loading (skeleton grid), streaming, **stale** (canvas dims 15 %, "Stale 4 s" chip), disconnected, replay-mode border, demo/live badge, low-GPU degraded ("Reduced detail…").
- The **aggregation indicator** treatment for E11-S12's LOD disclosure.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells, profiles, heatmap, bubbles, Deep Stats *content* — E18/E19/E20/E21/E22 design tracks; this ticket defines the chrome they sit in and the slots they occupy.
- Order/position line overlays — E31's design track.
- Drawing tools and their toolbar — E14.
- Scale/time context menus and go-to-date — **E11-D03**. Data table, empty and error states — **E11-D04**.
- Chart settings dialog beyond the Scales section — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The engine spike gate is satisfied before sign-off
  Given SCR-030's mandatory WebGL engine spike gate
  When this design is submitted for sign-off
  Then the E06 spike evidence is attached: 100k bars with footprint text at >= 60 fps, a 10-minute sustained 100 ms-cadence run with no dropped frames, and the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2
  And sign-off is withheld if that evidence is absent or fails its targets

Scenario: Every chrome element is specified at all three densities
  Given comfortable, compact and dense density modes
  When the axis, crosshair, legend and pane chrome specs are inspected
  Then each is drawn at all three densities with explicit spacing, type scale and tick-density values
  And the three change together as one switch, with no density-specific one-off

Scenario: Axis labels decimate predictably
  Given the time axis at 0.5, 3, 12 and 50 pixels per bar
  When label decimation is specified
  Then the rule states what is dropped first and what is never dropped at each level
  And an implementer can derive the visible label set at any zoom without asking

Scenario: No state is conveyed by colour alone
  Given every state of SCR-030: loading, streaming, stale, disconnected, replay, demo/live, degraded
  When each is reviewed against the colour-only rule
  Then each carries a text or shape equivalent
  And the bar-countdown warn state adds a word, not only an amber colour

Scenario: Keyboard equivalents are designed, not assumed
  Given drag-to-rescale on the price axis and drag-to-resize on pane splitters
  When the specs are reviewed
  Then each drag affordance has a designed keyboard equivalent with its focus treatment and its announcement
  And no functionality exists that is reachable only by dragging or only by hovering

Scenario: Contrast holds in all three themes
  Given dark, light and high-contrast themes
  When every foreground/background pair in the chassis is measured
  Then text pairs meet 4.5:1 and non-text UI pairs meet 3:1
  And the measurements are recorded in the sign-off, not asserted
```

## Technical notes / design
**Gridline hierarchy** is the single highest-leverage decision in this ticket. Chart grids either recede and let price dominate, or they compete with it and the chart reads as noise. The spec must fix: major/minor line opacity per theme, the rule for *which* price levels get a major line (round numbers scaled to the instrument's tick size, not every nth pixel), and the interaction with the crosshair line so the two are distinguishable when they coincide.

**Axis label decimation** is specified as a rule, not as a picture, because it must hold at continuous zoom: labels are placed at "nice" intervals (1/2/5 × 10^n) with a minimum pixel gap, and the *last* things dropped are the boundary labels (session start, day start) — dropping a day boundary at low zoom loses the user's place entirely.

**Density coupling.** Each density mode fixes a triple: `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` (E11-T04). The design must supply the actual numbers for all three modes, since a density mode that exists only as an adjective becomes three engineers' three interpretations.

**Tooltip collision.** The crosshair tooltip must flip rather than clip near pane edges, and must never cover the last-price line — SCR-030's constraint that labels "never obscure the last price" is a layout rule with a defined priority order, specified here.

## Test plan
Design verification rather than software testing:
- **Contrast audit** across every pair, in all three themes, recorded numerically.
- **Density walkthrough**: the full chassis rendered at all three densities, checked for collision, truncation and illegible type.
- **Edge-density check**: axis labels at the most extreme zoom in and out; legend with 12 indicators; tooltip at every pane edge.
- **Colour-blind simulation** (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) over every state, confirming each remains distinguishable — feeds open item **O5**.
- **Prototype review** against the E06 spike build so the specs are checked against what the engine can actually draw, not only against what looks good in Figma.
- Design QA of the built result is **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No direct security surface. One relevant constraint carried from SCR-046: the diagnostics overlay is designed to be **screenshotted into bug reports**, so its layout must not include account identifiers, balances, order data or user identity — the design fixes what fields exist, and therefore fixes what a screenshot can leak. The demo/live badge is the inverse case and is a **safety-critical** design element: it must be unmistakable at a glance, because the cost of a trader misreading which environment they are in is a real order on a live account.

- **Focus treatment** for every focusable chrome element, using CMP-004 FocusRing; focus order follows visual order across panes.
- **Keyboard equivalents designed for every pointer gesture**: axis rescale, splitter resize, crosshair movement, legend toggles (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6).
- **Target sizes** meet the §4 minimum, including splitters and axis drag zones, which are the easiest to draw too thin.
- **Contrast** measured, not eyeballed; the high-contrast theme is drawn as a first-class theme rather than derived.
- **No colour-only encoding** anywhere, including the stale, degraded, replay and demo/live states.
- **Reduced motion**: every animated affordance (crosshair, countdown, stale dimming) has a specified reduced-motion variant — see E11-D06 for the motion spec proper.
- **DOM-mirror alignment**: the canvas-control-surrogate pattern (§6.1) means invisible focusable elements are **sized to match their visual targets**, so the visual target sizes designed here *are* the a11y target sizes.
- Reviewed and signed off by the accessibility specialist; deeper review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
Design decisions with direct frame-budget consequences, which is why this ticket is reviewed against the E06 build:
- Gridline count per pane and label count per axis feed the draw-call budget (<=18 per pane, <=40 for a 3-pane chart).
- Text quantity on screen drives the SDF batching budget (<=2.0 ms, <=6 text draw calls per pane).
- Effects that would require an extra render pass (blurs, shadows, translucent overlays) must be flagged at design time, because each one is a measurable slice of a 16.6 ms budget. Where such an effect is wanted, the design states the cheaper alternative it will fall back to under the degradation ladder.

N/A for the design artefact. The diagnostics overlay design fixes which metrics are surfaced, which in turn fixes E11-T07's data contract — so the observability *surface* is decided here even though the instrumentation is not.

title: Design the price/time scale menus, scale settings and the go-to-date dialog
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007` makes log and linear scales **Must** and percentage **Should**, and `US-CHART-006` makes the manual scale-lock behaviour explicit: dragging the price axis disengages autoscale, a lock badge appears, and double-clicking restores auto-fit. Those behaviours are exposed through two small but heavily-used surfaces — the scale context menus (**SCR-043**) and the Scales section of the chart settings dialog (**SCR-031**) — plus the go-to-date dialog (**SCR-044**) that `US-CHART-010` and the recorded-history boundary make non-trivial.

These are small surfaces with sharp edges. `US-CHART-007` requires that on a series containing non-positive values, **log scale is disabled with an explanation rather than rendering incorrectly**; SCR-044 requires a clear failure when the target **precedes recorded history**. Both are error states that must be designed, not discovered.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-043 price-scale menu**: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100, invert, lock, merge indicator scales, reset. Checkable menu items with state announced; reachable via `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus.
- **SCR-043 time-scale menu**: auto-fit, go to date (opens SCR-044), spacing presets, show/hide session dividers and maintenance-window markers, timezone.
- **Disabled-with-explanation** treatment: the log option on a series with non-positive values must show *why* it is unavailable, inline, not as a silent grey item (`US-CHART-007` scenario 3).
- **SCR-031 Scales tab**: the section of the chart settings dialog covering scale mode, precision, autoscale-includes-drawings, countdown toggle, and the **CMP-228 PreviewTile** live preview against a real chart.
- **SCR-044 go-to-date dialog**: date+time entry with **UTC and local shown side by side**, quick jumps (session open, yesterday, last swing, last journal entry, last alert), and the **"before recorded history" error state drawn with the recording-start timestamp**.
- The **scale-lock badge** treatment on the price axis (its resting, hover and focus states) and the double-click-to-reset affordance.
- "Applies to this panel / all panels / as new default" scope control for settings (SCR-031's checklist item).
- All states in dark, light and high-contrast.

## Out of scope
- The rest of the chart settings dialog (General, Appearance, Trading, Performance tabs) — E15.
- Footprint settings (SCR-032) — E18.
- The underlying scale projection maths — E11-S05.
- Session/day-boundary *semantics* (`US-CHART-009`) — owned by E12; this ticket designs the toggle that surfaces the markers.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An unavailable scale mode explains itself
  Given a series containing non-positive values
  When the price-scale menu is opened
  Then the logarithmic option is shown as unavailable with an inline explanation of why
  And it is never silently greyed out, and never allowed to render incorrectly

Scenario: Go-to-date fails fast and usefully before recorded history
  Given recorded history for the symbol starts on 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC
  When the user requests 2026-08-15
  Then an error state names the recording-start timestamp in text
  And it fails immediately rather than showing a spinner, and Esc cancels without moving the chart

Scenario: Both timezones are visible at entry time
  Given the go-to-date dialog is open
  Then UTC and local time are shown side by side with the active timezone stated next to the field
  And the format hint is explicit, so there is no ambiguity about what was entered

Scenario: Scale menus are real menus with announced state
  Given the price scale has keyboard focus
  When the user presses Shift+F10
  Then the context menu opens with menu semantics
  And auto, logarithmic, percent, invert and lock are checkable items whose state is announced

Scenario: The scale-lock badge is unmistakable and reversible
  Given the user drags the price axis
  Then autoscale disengages and a lock badge appears with a text label, not an icon alone
  And the design specifies double-click-to-reset and its keyboard equivalent
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why the disabled-log case gets its own design attention.** The naive implementation greys the item out, the user tries three times, and then files a bug. The design specifies an inline reason ("Log scale needs all-positive values; this series contains a value <= 0") attached to the item itself, because a tooltip on a disabled control is famously unreliable across platforms and assistive technology.

**Menu item state.** Checkable items use `aria-checked` with `role="menuitemradio"` for the mutually-exclusive scale modes and `role="menuitemcheckbox"` for the independent toggles (invert, lock, dividers). Drawing these as two visually distinct groups makes the mutual exclusivity readable without trial and error.

**Preview tile.** CMP-228 renders a live miniature of the actual chart, not a generic sample — SCR-031's requirement for a "live preview against a real chart". The design must specify what the tile shows when the chart is empty or errored, which is the case everyone forgets.

## Test plan
- Contrast audit across all three themes for menus, dialog and badge.
- Keyboard walkthrough: `Shift+F10` open, arrow navigation, `Esc` close and focus restoration, tab order within the dialog.
- Error-state review: every failure path in SCR-044 drawn (before history, invalid format, no data at target).
- Screen-reader review of menu semantics with the accessibility specialist.
- Design QA of the built result in **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No security surface. One data-handling note for SCR-044's quick jumps: "last journal entry" and "last alert" reference user-owned records, so the design must account for the `viewer` role, where those quick jumps may be absent or empty — an RBAC-dependent menu that is designed only in its fully-populated state produces a broken layout for the least-privileged user, who is precisely the one least able to work around it.

## Accessibility notes
- Menus use real menu semantics (WAI-ARIA APG menu pattern), reachable by `Shift+F10` from the focused scale, with checkable items whose state is announced.
- The scale-lock badge carries a **text label**; the lock state is never icon-or-colour-only.
- The date field has an explicit **format hint** and a keyboard-operable calendar; the active timezone is stated next to the field, not implied.
- Errors are described in **text**, including the recording-start timestamp.
- `Esc` cancels the dialog without moving the chart, and focus returns to the invoking control.
- Every numeric field in SCR-031 carries its **units in the label**; Reset requires confirmation.
- Design source reviewed with the accessibility specialist; deeper review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
SCR-043's constraint is a design constraint too: a scale-mode change is a **projection change only — no data refetch, redraw within one frame**. The design must therefore not imply a loading state for a scale change; showing a spinner for something that takes one frame teaches users the app is slower than it is. SCR-044's budget: a jump inside recorded history renders the target window in <=800 ms; out-of-history requests fail fast.

## Observability
Design fixes the analytics surface: `chart.price_scale_changed`, `chart.time_scale_changed` (SCR-043), `chart.go_to_date` with `{target, found}` (SCR-044), `chart.settings_changed` with `{section, key}` (SCR-031).
