title: Design the data-table alternative and the chart empty and error states
body:
## Context
Three surfaces, one shared property: they are what the user sees when the canvas is not enough.

**SCR-045** is the data-table alternative, and `US-CHART-014`'s NFR is unusually forceful — "this view is treated as an **equal-status alternative, not a degraded fallback**" — with `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 adding that it "is not a stripped-down compliance minimum". SCR-045's own sign-off checklist makes the point structural: it must be "reachable from the chart panel header, **not hidden in settings** — equal status verified". Designing this as a utility panel tucked behind a settings toggle would fail the ticket regardless of how it looks.

**SCR-047** (empty / no-data) and **SCR-048** (error) are the states most likely to be encountered by a new user on day one, and both carry explicit "no infinite spinner" and "never a blank canvas" requirements.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-045 data table**: the full table layout with columns time, open, high, low, close, volume, delta, CVD; the **expandable per-bar footprint cell row** (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag); the filter toolbar; tri-state sort affordance with `aria-sort`; the row-action menu (create alert here, replay from here, add note); the TSV-copy affordance; and the **stale banner** ("Data is for bar X, no longer in view — press Alt+T to refresh to current").
- The **equal-status entry point**: a control in the chart panel header, designed at equal visual weight to other primary chart controls — plus `Alt+T`.
- Empty, loading and filtered-to-zero states of the table.
- **SCR-047 empty / no-data**: the three distinct reasons drawn separately — never recorded (with the "history starts when you record" explanation and the owner CTA to SCR-140), no data in this range, instrument not trading/delisted — plus the non-owner explanatory copy variant and the "live data is still streaming" note where true.
- **SCR-048 error**: distinct copy for engine/WebGL failure, data-feed failure and backend failure; the **WebGL-unavailable message naming the fallback path** (E11-T05's `degraded-2d`); the "Graphics context lost — restoring…" auto-retry treatment with attempt count and next-attempt time; a **copyable correlation id**; retry and "open diagnostics" actions; and the requirement that the rest of the workspace remains usable.
- All states in dark, light and high-contrast.

## Out of scope
- Footprint sub-row **content** semantics — E18 (this ticket designs the expandable mechanism and the column contract).
- The profile and DOM-ladder table variants of §6.3 — E19 and E21, which reuse this table shell.
- The recorder settings screen (SCR-140) the empty-state CTA links to — E16.
- Alert/replay/note flows behind the row actions — E40/E26/E41.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The table is designed as an equal-status view
  Given the SCR-045 design
  When the entry point is reviewed
  Then a control exists in the chart panel header at equal visual weight to other primary chart controls
  And the table is not reachable only from settings, and is not styled as a secondary or fallback surface

Scenario: The table carries the same information as the canvas
  Given the canvas shows bars with OHLCV, delta and per-bar footprint cells
  When the table columns are reviewed
  Then every one of those values has a column or an expandable sub-row
  And no information available on the canvas is missing from the table

Scenario: Every empty reason is drawn separately
  Given the three empty reasons: never recorded, no data in this range, instrument not trading
  When SCR-047 is reviewed
  Then each is drawn with its own copy and its own action
  And the owner CTA and the non-owner explanatory variant are both present, with no infinite-spinner path anywhere

Scenario: The error state names the fallback and is actionable
  Given WebGL2 is unavailable
  When SCR-048 is reviewed
  Then the copy names the degraded-2d fallback and what is reduced
  And a copyable correlation id, a retry action and an open-diagnostics action are present, and the rest of the workspace remains usable

Scenario: Context-loss recovery is communicated, not hidden
  Given the engine is auto-retrying after a lost graphics context
  Then the design shows "restoring", the attempt count and the next-attempt time
  And after three failed attempts a manual retry and a link to renderer settings are offered

Scenario: The stale banner prevents silent staleness
  Given the table's focused bar scrolls out of the chart's visible range
  Then a banner states which bar the data is for and how to refresh
  And the stale values are never presented as though they were current
```

## Technical notes / design
**Equal status is a layout decision, not a copy decision.** The table's entry point sits in the panel header alongside the chart-type and indicator controls, at the same size and weight. A "view as table" item buried in an overflow menu would satisfy the letter of the requirement and fail its intent, which is why SCR-045's checklist calls it out explicitly.

**Table density.** The table is the surface a low-vision user will zoom to 200 %, so the design must hold at that zoom without horizontal scrolling of the primary columns (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.10 reflow). The column-picker (CMP-056) is how a user drops columns they do not need, and the default column set must already fit comfortably.

**Error copy discipline.** Three distinct causes, three distinct messages, each naming what the user can do. "Something went wrong" is not acceptable copy for any of the three; the correlation id exists so the user can hand over something actionable, and it must be selectable text, not an image or a truncated ellipsis.

**Empty-state honesty.** The never-recorded case is the most common first-run experience, and the copy must be honest about the product's model: history exists because *you recorded it*. SCR-047's example copy — "No recorded history for BTCUSDT before 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC. Live data is streaming now." — is the tone to match.

## Test plan
- **Parity review**: canvas information inventory vs table column inventory, item by item, recorded in the sign-off.
- **Zoom review**: table at 200 % browser zoom, confirming reflow without horizontal scrolling of primary columns.
- **Screen-reader review** with the accessibility specialist over table semantics, sort announcement and filter announcement.
- **Copy review** for all empty and error variants, including the non-owner RBAC variants.
- **Colour-blind simulation** over delta signs and imbalance flags, confirming the text encodings carry the meaning.
- Design QA of the built result in **E11-D08**; the built table is audited in **E11-Q05**.

## Security notes
The error state is the security-relevant surface here. SCR-048 requires a **correlation id as selectable text**, which is deliberately opaque — it identifies a trace, not a user, an account or a session. The design must not surface internal exception messages, stack traces, hostnames or query strings, because this screen is screenshotted into issues by design. Plain-language copy plus an opaque id is the whole contract.

For SCR-047, the owner CTA ("Record this symbol") is a privileged action: the **non-owner variant is explanatory copy, not a disabled button**, so a `viewer` is not shown an action they can never take.

## Accessibility notes
This is the ticket where the accessibility standard's §6.3 becomes a drawn artefact:
- Real `<table>` semantics with column and row headers; tri-state sort with `aria-sort`; filter state announced with counts ("Showing 6 of 40 rows, filtered by: Bid-stacked").
- Keyboard navigation designed explicitly: arrows to move, `Enter` to expand, `Ctrl+C` to copy, `Alt+T` to open/close, with focus placement and restoration specified.
- **Equal status** is itself an accessibility requirement — this is the normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030.
- Delta signs as text `+`/`-`; imbalance flags as text labels; `(estimated)` carries the literal word (CMP-227) — never colour or icon alone.
- SCR-048 is a `role="alert"` region with plain-language copy and a focusable, non-colour-only retry.
- SCR-047 is a heading + paragraph + action, never an icon alone; the recording-start timestamp is text.
- Reviewed by the accessibility specialist; this ticket is a primary input to **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
SCR-045's budget shapes the design: the table is **virtualised**, renders 100k rows without jank (<=8 ms scripting per scroll frame), and **reads the same in-memory series as the canvas so no extra fetch is issued** — meaning the design must not include anything that would require a separate query (a full-series aggregate footer, for instance, would). SCR-047 requires the empty state to render **without initialising the GL context**, so an empty chart costs no GPU budget — the design must therefore not depend on any canvas-rendered element. SCR-048's retry uses exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, capped 30s) with the next attempt time shown.

## Observability
Design fixes the analytics surface: `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (SCR-045); `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}` (SCR-047); `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}` (SCR-048).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 design sign-off acceptance checklists ticked item by item.
- [ ] Equal-status verification recorded explicitly in the sign-off comment (entry point placement and visual weight).

## Dependencies
- **E11-D02** — the chassis and panel header the table's entry point lives in.
- **E05** — CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-027 ErrorState, CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback.
- Blocks **E11-S14** (design-ahead) and informs **E11-S13** and **E11-T05**.

## Branch
`design/chart-engine-table-and-states` (Figma).

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-043, SCR-044, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-049 (each entry's states, a11y, performance and design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7 — CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226, CMP-228, CMP-004
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` — tokens, theming, motion, density, a11y
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom), §6 (canvas a11y), §7 (reduced motion)
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`, `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 (visual encoding rules, density modes)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 (design-ready gate)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-014 (equal-status NFR)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 (table alternative, column sets, sort/filter/live-sync)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-004, CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-049, CMP-053, CMP-056, CMP-091, CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/chart-engine-table-and-states`
- PR title: `E11-D04: Design the data-table alternative and the chart empty and error states`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E11-D04)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, design, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E11-D04 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Contribute chart primitives, tokens and density modes to the design system
body:
## Context
E11 introduces a band of components that exist nowhere else in the product: **CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-198 ChartWatermark/PaneBackground, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-226 BarCountdown**. `15-component-catalogue.md` classifies these as **chart primitives** — "engine-level render objects with no DOM" — which makes them a genuinely unusual design-system contribution: most of them have no CSS, no DOM node and no Storybook story in the conventional sense.

The reason to route them through the design system anyway is that **E12, E13, E14, E18, E19 and E21 all draw inside them**. If the chart token set is invented ad hoc in E11 and then extended ad hoc in each of those Epics, the chart ends up with six palettes. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 makes this a gate: "Component(s) used are in `15-component-catalogue.md`; any new component has a design-system entry, **not an ad hoc one-off**."

This ticket also ships the **density-mode triple** that `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 5 requires to move as one switch.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Chart token slots** added to the design-system token set: `color.chart.axis`, `color.chart.grid.major`, `color.chart.grid.minor`, `color.chart.crosshair`, `color.chart.watermark`, `color.chart.pane.bg`, `color.chart.pane.bg.focused`, plus the up/down/neutral series slots and the delta-ramp endpoints — each defined for **dark, light and high-contrast**.
- **Colour ramps** (the source values E11-T04 turns into LUTs): the diverging delta ramp and the sequential intensity ramp, specified in **OkLab** stops so the engine's interpolation and the design's intent agree.
- **Density scale** for chart surfaces: `comfortable` | `compact` | `dense`, each fixing the triple `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` with concrete numbers — the single switch of §5 rule 5.
- **Pattern/hatch registry** entries for the non-colour-only encodings: the `(estimated)` hatch (CMP-227's engine counterpart), the imbalance outline pattern, and the reduced-detail indicator — so later Epics attach a registered pattern id rather than inventing a new visual language.
- **Catalogue entries** for the nine chart primitives above: tier, purpose, props, a11y contract, tokens, Storybook plan and test requirements, matching the existing `15-component-catalogue.md` §7 format.
- **Storybook strategy for canvas components**: each primitive gets a story that mounts a real engine instance with a fixed fixture, so "Storybook coverage" for a no-DOM component means a rendered, inspectable canvas rather than a placeholder — the stories named in the catalogue (PriceAxis: Linear/Log/Dragging(keyboard demo); TimeAxis: Default/ZoomedIn/ZoomedOut; Crosshair: Default/SyncedAcrossPanes/KeyboardDriven).
- **CMP-004 FocusRing** usage contract for canvas-surrogate elements, since focus rings on invisible mirror nodes are a case the base component was not designed for.
- Updates committed to `15-component-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md`.

## Out of scope
- Building the components — engineering, across E11's stories.
- Footprint, profile, heatmap and bubble primitives (CMP-181..187, CMP-192..195) — contributed by E18/E19/E21 against the foundation laid here.
- The design-system's own infrastructure (token pipeline, Storybook setup, visual-regression baseline) — **E05**.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection — open item **O5**, validated in the M8 a11y pass.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Chart colours come from tokens, not from code
  Given the engine's rendering code after this contribution lands
  When it is searched for colour literals
  Then no hard-coded colour exists outside the theme ingestion layer
  And every chart colour resolves to a named design-system token in all three themes

Scenario: Density is one switch with real numbers
  Given the comfortable, compact and dense modes
  When the density scale is inspected
  Then each fixes cellPadPx, font size class and lodBias with concrete values
  And no surface can adopt one of the three without the other two

Scenario: Every primitive has a catalogue entry before it is built
  Given CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199 and CMP-226
  When 15-component-catalogue.md is read
  Then each has tier, purpose, props, a11y contract, tokens, Storybook stories and test requirements
  And the engineering story that builds it references that entry rather than inventing a contract

Scenario: Non-colour encodings are registered, not improvised
  Given a later Epic needs to encode "estimated" or "imbalanced"
  When it consults the pattern registry
  Then a registered hatch or outline pattern exists with its usage rule
  And introducing a new encoding requires a design-system contribution, not a local decision

Scenario: Canvas components have real Storybook coverage
  Given a chart-primitive story is opened in Storybook
  Then a live engine instance renders with a fixed fixture
  And the story is inspectable and covered by the visual-regression baseline, not a static placeholder
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why OkLab stops.** A diverging ramp interpolated in sRGB passes through a desaturated grey-brown mid-band and has visibly uneven perceptual steps — on a delta ramp that means two meaningfully different delta values look identical. Specifying stops in OkLab and letting E11-T04 interpolate there keeps steps perceptually even. The design supplies stops; the engine supplies interpolation; neither reinvents the other's half.

**The density triple is the interesting constraint.** Density is usually a spacing token. Here it also changes *how much data is drawn*, because font size class determines the minimum legible cell-text height, which determines the LOD threshold at which text is dropped (§3.6). Splitting them would let a user select "dense" spacing with "comfortable" LOD thresholds and get unreadable overlapping text — which is exactly why §5 rule 5 requires them to move together, and why this ticket ships them as one object rather than three tokens.

**Storybook for no-DOM components.** The catalogue already demands stories and visual tests for these primitives. The approach: a `<ChartStoryHarness>` that mounts a real engine with a deterministic fixture and a fixed viewport, so a story is a real render. This also makes the stories usable as golden-image sources (E11-T08), which is why the harness is worth building once here rather than per component.

## Test plan
- **Token-coverage check**: every token slot defined for all three themes; a missing theme value fails the token build.
- **Contrast audit** over every chart token pair in every theme, recorded numerically (the design-side counterpart of E11-T04's automated CI test).
- **Ramp evaluation**: the delta ramp sampled at 16 stops and reviewed for perceptual evenness and for distinguishability under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulation.
- **Catalogue completeness check**: each of the nine primitives has every required field.
- **Storybook review**: each named story renders and is captured in the visual-regression baseline.
- Design QA of the built components in **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No security surface — tokens, ramps and catalogue entries.

One durable consequence worth recording: the **pattern registry is a safety mechanism, not a styling one**. The `(estimated)` hatch is how the product keeps its promise (principle P10 in `20-architecture.md`) that heuristic-derived data is never presented as measured fact. A later Epic that encodes estimated data without a registered pattern is making a truthfulness error, not a visual one, and routing the encoding through the design system is what makes that error reviewable.

## Accessibility notes
- Every token pair carries a **recorded contrast measurement**; the high-contrast theme is authored as a first-class theme, not derived by a filter.
- The **pattern/hatch registry exists so that colour is never the sole carrier of meaning** — it is the design-system enforcement of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rules 1–4 and of WCAG 1.4.1.
- Each primitive's catalogue entry states its **a11y contract** explicitly, as the existing entries do: PriceAxis's keyboard rescale, TimeAxis's keyboard pan/zoom, Crosshair's keyboard-primary path, ChartTooltip's `aria-hidden` (to prevent duplicate announcement alongside the DOM mirror), MultiChartLinker's once-only sync announcement.
- **CMP-004 FocusRing** on canvas-surrogate nodes: the ring must be visible against the canvas content behind it in all three themes, which is a harder case than a ring on a solid surface and is specified here.
- Colour-blind simulation over the ramps feeds open item **O5**.

## Performance notes
Token and density decisions have frame-budget consequences, so they are made with the budget in view: the number of distinct colours in a ramp determines LUT size (256 entries is the fixed budget), and the density mode's `lodBias` directly shifts how much is drawn at a given zoom. A density mode that retains too much detail would push B5 over budget — so the `dense` mode's `lodBias` is validated against the benchmark rather than chosen by eye.

## Observability
N/A for the artefacts. The density mode and theme name are reported in `frame` stats (E11-T04), so a performance report always states which density produced it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md` updated and merged.
- [ ] Token set builds cleanly for all three themes with no missing values.
- [ ] Storybook stories exist and are captured in the visual-regression baseline for all nine primitives.
- [ ] Design-system team sign-off (this is a contribution to their surface, not a local addition).

## Dependencies
- **E05** — the design system this contributes to: token pipeline, Storybook, visual-regression baseline.
- **E11-D02** — the chassis design whose decisions are generalised into tokens here.
- Blocks **E11-T04** (theme ingestion consumes these tokens) and is the foundation E18/E19/E21's own primitive contributions extend.

## Branch
`design/chart-engine-design-system` (Figma + PRs to `15-component-catalogue.md`, `16-design-system-brief.md` and the token package).

## References

title: Specify chart motion: momentum, transitions and reduced-motion variants
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-006` requires pan and zoom "with inertia that **respects reduced-motion settings**", and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 makes `prefers-reduced-motion` a binding requirement rather than a nicety. Momentum is also the single most "feel"-dependent thing in the engine: the difference between a chart that feels responsive and one that feels slippery is a time constant, and it is not a number an engineer should have to guess.

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 already proposes the model — velocity-based with exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)`, tau = 120 ms, terminated below 0.02 px/ms, cancelled on any new pointer-down. This ticket validates that against the E06 build with real users (E11-D01's findings), fixes the remaining motion in the chassis, and specifies every reduced-motion variant so the fallback is designed rather than improvised as "turn the animation off".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pan/zoom momentum**: decay constant tau, termination threshold, cancel-on-pointer-down behaviour, and the maximum fling distance — validated by feel against the E06 build, not chosen from the document alone.
- **Zoom transitions**: cursor-anchored zoom is instantaneous by design (it tracks the wheel), but double-click-to-reset and go-to-date jumps are **animated transitions**; their duration, easing and the rule for when a jump is too far to animate (beyond which it cuts, because a 3-second pan across 30,000 bars is disorienting, not elegant).
- **Crosshair**: no easing on position (it must track the pointer exactly — a lagging crosshair is a correctness problem in a trading tool), but the fade in/out and the magnet snap have specified timings.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: the 1 Hz tick treatment and the transition into the warn state in the final 10 seconds — specified so the warn state is a **change of word and weight**, not a flash.
- **Stale-state dimming** (SCR-030: canvas dims 15 %): the fade duration and the recovery transition.
- **LOD step-down / step-up**: whether the transition is instantaneous or crossfaded, and the aggregation-indicator's appearance animation.
- **Pane splitter drag** and collapsed-pane expand/collapse timings.
- **Context-loss recovery** (SCR-048): the "restoring…" treatment's motion, if any.
- **A reduced-motion variant for every one of the above**, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 — stated individually rather than as a blanket "disable animation", because some of these (the countdown warn state, the stale dimming) carry information and must survive in a non-animated form.
- Output as a motion spec table: element, trigger, property, duration, easing curve, reduced-motion variant.

## Out of scope
- Drawing-tool and order-ticket motion — E14 and E31.
- Application-shell transitions (panel open/close, dialogs) — E05/E10.
- The motion implementation — E11-S04 and the consuming stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animated element has a designed reduced-motion variant
  Given the motion spec table
  When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is assumed
  Then every row states its reduced-motion variant explicitly
  And no row's variant is simply "no animation" where the animation carried information

Scenario: Momentum feel is validated on the real engine, not on paper
  Given the proposed decay constant of 120 ms
  When it is tested against the E06 build on the reference machine with the owner
  Then the final constant is recorded with the evidence behind it
  And any deviation from the 26-chart-engine-design.md proposal is noted with its reason

Scenario: The crosshair never lags the pointer
  Given the crosshair motion spec
  Then crosshair position has no easing and no interpolation
  And only its fade in/out and magnet snap carry timings

Scenario: Long jumps cut rather than animate
  Given a go-to-date jump spanning 30,000 bars
  When the transition rule is applied
  Then the distance exceeds the animate threshold and the view cuts to the target
  And the threshold is stated as a number, not as a judgement call

Scenario: Information-carrying states survive reduced motion
  Given the countdown warn state and the stale dimming
  When reduced motion is active
  Then each remains distinguishable through a non-animated means: a word change and a static dimmed treatment
  And no information is lost by disabling animation
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why tau is worth a ticket.** Exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)` is framerate-independent, which matters because a momentum implementation that multiplies per frame behaves differently at 30 fps and 60 fps — the chart would come to rest in a different place depending on how busy the machine was. The design fixes tau; the implementation (E11-S04) must integrate against elapsed time, not frame count, and the spec says so explicitly because this is a mistake that is easy to make and hard to notice.

**The "too far to animate" threshold.** Animated navigation is a spatial cue — it tells the user which direction they moved and how far. Beyond a certain distance that cue becomes useless and the animation is just a delay. The spec fixes a threshold in viewport-widths (proposed: 3), beyond which the transition cuts and the user is oriented by the axis labels instead.

**Reduced motion is not motion removal.** `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7's requirement is that motion not be *vestibularly triggering*, not that state changes become invisible. Where an animation conveys information — the countdown entering its warn state, the chart going stale — the reduced-motion variant substitutes an instant, non-animated change of the same information, which is why each row's variant is specified individually.

## Test plan
- **Feel validation** against the E06 build on the reference machine, with the owner, for momentum and zoom transitions specifically.
- **Reduced-motion walkthrough**: every specified element reviewed with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, confirming no information loss.
- **Vestibular review** with the accessibility specialist: no parallax, no large-area movement, no motion exceeding the standard's thresholds.
- **Frame-budget sanity**: any proposed transition that would require an extra render pass is flagged and re-specified.
- Implementation conformance is verified in **E11-D08** (design QA) and **E11-Q05** (a11y audit).

## Security notes
No security surface.

One safety note with a motion dimension: the **demo/live badge** and the replay-mode border are environment indicators where misreading has real financial consequence. Their motion spec must not include anything that could make the indicator momentarily ambiguous — no cross-fade between demo and live treatments, no transitional state where neither reads clearly. The change is instant, in both the normal and reduced-motion variants.

## Accessibility notes
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is honoured for **every** animated element, with a designed variant per element rather than a global switch (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §7).
- The engine reads the preference through `theme.reducedMotion` (E11-T04), giving one source of truth rather than per-component media queries.
- Information-carrying animations have non-animated equivalents, so reduced motion never costs a user information.
- No animation is the sole indicator of any state change.
- Motion durations stay within the standard's thresholds; nothing flashes more than three times per second (WCAG 2.3.1).
- The **keyboard** pan/zoom path (E11-S04) uses discrete steps rather than momentum, which is both the accessible path and the reduced-motion path — the spec notes that these coincide deliberately.

## Performance notes
Momentum is integrated by the scheduler's time-based animation loop, so dropped frames change nothing about where the chart comes to rest — a correctness property as much as a performance one, and specified here so it is not treated as an implementation detail. Transitions must not require an additional render pass; any that would are re-specified. Under the degradation ladder, animated transitions are among the first things shed, and the spec states which ones, so the shedding order is a design decision rather than an engineering convenience.

## Observability
N/A for the artefact. `theme.reducedMotion` is reported in `frame` stats so a perf or behaviour report states whether momentum was active.

- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.

- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.

- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.

- [ ] Vestibular review signed off by the accessibility specialist.

title: Run an accessibility design review of the chart engine's canvas strategy
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 opens by naming this "the **highest-risk area**" of the product: WebGL canvases are opaque to assistive technology, and the mitigation is a three-layer strategy that must be designed into the engine rather than retrofitted. §6.1 is explicit that the engine's visible-window/focused-unit query surface is "an **explicit chart-engine-design requirement, not an afterthought bolted on later**".

Retrofitting accessibility into a render engine is close to impossible — by the time the canvas is drawing, the information needed to describe it has already been discarded. This review exists to catch that class of problem while it is still a design change, and it is scheduled **before** E11-S13 and E11-S14 are built precisely so its findings are cheap.

It is also the ticket that verifies the **equal-status** claim for SCR-045, which is the product's main accessibility promise and the one most easily eroded in implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layer-by-layer review** against `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6:
  - §6.1 DOM mirror — windowing strategy, the canvas-control-surrogate pattern, `clip-path` hiding (**not** `display:none`), surrogate sizing matching visual targets, focus ring visibility over canvas content, node-count cap.
  - §6.2 Live regions — politeness routing per event class, throttle cadence (default 1 update / 2 s, `US-CHART-008`'s <=2/s cap), region hygiene (pre-rendered containers, text-content-only swaps), the "reduce announcements" master toggle, and which events are `role="alert"` and therefore never throttled.
  - §6.3 Table alternative — equal-status verification, column-set completeness against the canvas, sort/filter announcements, live-patching without focus loss, the stale banner.
  - §6.4 Canvas semantics — `role="img"` with a rolling label that updates on data change.
- **Keyboard vocabulary review**: the complete key map across chart, axes, panes, crosshair, table and menus — checked for conflicts with the global hotkey table, with screen-reader reserved keys, and with browser defaults. A key map with a conflict is discovered in testing at ten times the cost of discovering it here.
- **No hover-only / no drag-only audit** (§3.1.6): every pointer gesture in E11 enumerated with its keyboard equivalent — pan, zoom, axis rescale, splitter resize, crosshair, magnet, legend toggles, table sort.
- **Focus-order review** across panes, axes, legend, table and overlay.
- **Target-size review** (§4) for splitters, axis drag zones and legend toggles.
- **Contrast and colour-independence re-check** across D02/D03/D04/D05 as a set, rather than per ticket — encodings that are individually fine can collide when composed.
- **Reduced-motion review** of D06's spec.
- Findings logged with severity and an owner, each routed to the specific engineering or design ticket that must change.

## Out of scope
- Auditing the **built** product — **E11-Q05** (the a11y audit with NVDA/VoiceOver passes on real code).
- Accessibility of order-flow surfaces — E18/E19/E21's own reviews against this same standard.
- The design system's base component accessibility — E05.
- Writing the DOM mirror — E11-S13.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four layers are reviewed against the standard, clause by clause
  Given 05-accessibility-standard.md sections 6.1 through 6.4
  When the review is complete
  Then each clause has a verdict of compliant, at risk or non-compliant with evidence
  And every non-compliant and at-risk item has an owner and a target ticket

Scenario: Equal status is verified, not asserted
  Given SCR-045's equal-status requirement
  When the table design is compared against the canvas information inventory
  Then every value available on the canvas has a table equivalent
  And the entry point is confirmed to be in the panel header at equal visual weight, not in settings

Scenario: No functionality is pointer-only
  Given every pointer gesture E11 introduces
  When the audit table is inspected
  Then each has a keyboard equivalent of equal capability
  And any gesture without one is raised as a blocking finding

Scenario: The key map has no conflicts
  Given the complete E11 key map
  When it is checked against the global hotkey table, screen-reader reserved keys and browser defaults
  Then no conflict exists
  And any conflict found is resolved before the review is signed off, not deferred to implementation

Scenario: Findings land before the code is written
  Given E11-S13 starts in Sprint 07 and E11-S14 in Sprint 08
  Then this review is Done by the end of Sprint 05
  And its findings are reflected in those tickets before they start
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method.** Structured walkthrough against the standard's clauses, with the accessibility specialist, the chart-engine lead and the designer of record present. Each clause gets a verdict rather than a discussion, so the output is actionable rather than a set of notes.

**The highest-value check is the desync question.** The DOM mirror and the canvas can disagree — at an LOD step-down, mid-pan, or during a live update — and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4 states plainly that desync is **never acceptable**. The review's job is to interrogate the design for every path where the two could diverge and confirm each is structurally prevented rather than merely unlikely. E11-S13's property test exists because of this review.

**Key-map conflicts worth checking specifically**, since they are the ones that actually bite: NVDA's browse-mode keys, JAWS's virtual cursor, VoiceOver's `VO`-prefixed combinations, and browser defaults (`Ctrl+F`, `Ctrl+D`, `Alt+arrow` for history). `Alt+T` for the table is chosen because it is clear in all four, and the review confirms that the rest of the map is too.

- The pointer-gesture audit table is complete — enumerated from the design, not from memory.

- Findings are triaged with severity, owner and target ticket; blocking findings prevent sign-off of the design tickets they affect.
- A prototype walkthrough with a screen reader is performed where the design's behaviour is ambiguous on paper — which, for live regions, it usually is.

## Security notes
No security surface.

One intersection worth recording: the DOM mirror is real DOM containing formatted market data, and the review confirms the design specifies `textContent` writes rather than `innerHTML`, so a malformed symbol name or number string cannot become markup. This is an accessibility ticket noticing a security property because the mirror is the one place where engine-rendered values become DOM — it is fed to E11-X01's threat model rather than handled here.

This ticket **is** the accessibility work. Its authority: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 is binding on the engine's design, WCAG 2.2 AA is the conformance target, and the accessibility specialist's sign-off is a gate on E11-S13 and E11-S14 entering Ready.

Accessibility and performance intersect in two specific places the review must confirm rather than assume: the mirror's node cap (500) and per-frame cost (<=1 ms) must be achievable given the designed surrogate density, and the announcement throttle must be slow enough for a screen reader to keep up at a 20 Hz tick rate. title: Run design QA on the built chart engine surfaces against the specs
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA **default-on for net-new UI Stories**: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set."

E11 ships the chassis that six further Epics build on, which changes the stakes of this pass. A 2 px gutter error or a token wired to the wrong slot does not stay a 2 px error — it becomes the baseline that E12's series, E13's indicators and E18's footprint are all aligned to, and correcting it later means touching all of them. This is the cheapest moment to catch it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Surface-by-surface comparison** of the built engine against E11-D02/D03/D04/D05/D06:
  - SCR-030 chassis: pane chrome, gutters, axis rendering, gridline hierarchy, legend, watermark, countdown.
  - CMP-188/189 axes: tick density, label decimation at each zoom level, drag and keyboard rescale affordances, the scale-lock badge.
  - CMP-190/197 crosshair and tooltip: line treatment, axis pills, tooltip layout, edge-flip behaviour, the never-obscure-last-price rule.
  - SCR-043/044/031 scale menus, go-to-date and the Scales tab.
  - SCR-045 data table, including the **equal-status entry point placement**.
  - SCR-046 diagnostics, SCR-047 empty, SCR-048 error.
  - Multi-pane chrome: splitters, collapsed stubs, pane focus indication.
- **All three themes** (dark, light, high-contrast) and **all three densities** (comfortable, compact, dense) — the full 9-cell matrix for the chassis, since a density/theme combination is exactly where a token error hides.
- **Every state** from SCR-030: loading, streaming, stale, disconnected, replay, demo/live, degraded.
- **Motion conformance** against E11-D06: momentum feel, transition durations, countdown warn, stale dimming, and each reduced-motion variant.
- **Token conformance**: confirm no hard-coded colours and that every surface resolves to the design-system token specified.
- **Discrepancy log**: each item classified as fix-now or file-as-Bug with a `priority/*` label, per the DoD.

## Out of scope
- Functional testing — **E11-Q01**/**Q02**/**Q06**.
- Accessibility auditing — **E11-Q05** (this pass checks *designed* focus and contrast treatments are implemented, not full conformance).
- Performance — **E11-Q03**.
- Surfaces owned by other Epics (footprint cells, heatmap, drawings) — their own design QA.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every designed surface is compared against its spec
  Given the E11 design specs and the built engine
  When design QA completes
  Then every surface in scope has a recorded comparison result
  And no surface is marked "looks fine" without a spec-by-spec check of spacing, tokens, type, colour and states

Scenario: The full theme and density matrix is covered
  Given three themes and three density modes
  When the chassis is reviewed
  Then all nine combinations are checked
  And discrepancies that appear only in a specific combination are logged with that combination named

Scenario: Discrepancies are dispositioned, never merely noted
  Given the discrepancy log
  Then each item is either fixed within this pass or filed as a Bug with a priority label and an owner
  And no item is left as an unowned observation

Scenario: Equal status survives implementation
  Given SCR-045's equal-status requirement
  When the built product is inspected
  Then the table's entry point is in the chart panel header at the designed visual weight
  And any regression toward hiding it in a menu or settings is a blocking finding

Scenario: Reduced-motion variants are implemented as designed
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When each animated element is exercised
  Then it behaves per its designed reduced-motion variant
  And no information-carrying state change is lost
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method.** Side-by-side comparison at 1:1 scale using the Figma overlay workflow, plus browser DevTools for computed values — measuring rather than eyeballing spacing and colour, since a 2 px error is invisible to the eye and obvious to a measurement.

For canvas-rendered surfaces the comparison uses **screenshots at a fixed DPR against the golden images** (E11-T08), which conveniently means a discrepancy found here can usually be turned into a golden test so it cannot recur — design QA findings that become regression tests are worth more than findings that become fixes.

**Order of attack**: themes first (token errors are systematic and cheap to find in one theme, then confirm across all three), then densities (spacing errors), then states (coverage gaps), then motion. Going state-first would mean re-checking every state after each token fix.

## Test plan
- Comparison results recorded per surface per theme per density.
- Discrepancy log with classification, priority and owner.
- Findings converted into golden-image cases (E11-T08) wherever they are visual and reproducible.
- Re-check after fixes, with the re-check result recorded — a design QA pass that does not verify its own fixes is half a pass.

## Security notes
No security surface. One check with a safety dimension: the **demo/live badge** and the replay-mode border are verified to be unmistakable in every theme and density, because an environment indicator that is legible in dark/comfortable and washed out in high-contrast/dense is a real trading hazard, not a cosmetic defect.

## Accessibility notes
This pass verifies that **designed** accessibility treatments were implemented: focus ring visibility over canvas content in all three themes, target sizes for splitters and axis drag zones, contrast conformance of the shipped tokens, the presence of text equivalents on every state, and the reduced-motion variants. Full accessibility conformance — axe-core, NVDA and VoiceOver passes — is **E11-Q05**, and this ticket does not substitute for it.

## Performance notes
Not a performance pass, but visual discrepancies with performance causes are flagged for E11-Q03: text that looks wrong because it fell back to the 2D path, gridlines missing because a draw-call budget was hit, a density mode that silently dropped detail. A visual bug with a performance root cause is mis-triaged more often than not, so noting the possibility here saves a round trip.

title: Produce the chart-engine design handoff pack and run the engineering walkthrough
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule exists so engineering never waits on design, but a signed-off Figma file is not the same as a usable specification. The chart chassis is unusually hard to hand off because most of it has **no DOM**: an engineer cannot inspect a canvas-rendered axis in a browser to find out what the tick spacing should be, and cannot derive label decimation behaviour from a static frame. Everything that would normally be discoverable has to be written down.

This ticket produces the pack that makes E11's design specs actionable without a conversation, and runs the walkthrough where the remaining ambiguities surface while both sides are in the room.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Redline specs** for every E11 surface: spacing, type scale, token names (not hex values), border radii, opacity, and the numeric values for all three density modes.
- **Behaviour specs** for what a static frame cannot express — the things most likely to be guessed at otherwise:
  - Axis label decimation as a **rule** (nice-interval selection, minimum pixel gap, drop order, what is never dropped).
  - Gridline major/minor selection rule relative to instrument tick size.

- **The motion spec table** from E11-D06 (element, trigger, property, duration, easing, reduced-motion variant).
- **Token mapping table**: every visual element -> its design-system token slot, so implementation is a lookup rather than an interpretation.
- **State matrix**: every surface × every state × every theme, with the expected treatment per cell.
- **Asset export**: any icons, the pattern/hatch definitions, and the font subset E11-K01 needs for the SDF atlas.

- The designs themselves — D02/D03/D04/D05/D06.
- Ongoing design support during implementation — normal sprint activity, not a deliverable here.

```gherkin
Scenario: An engineer can build from the pack without asking a question
  Given a frontend engineer assigned to E11-S06 with no prior involvement in the design
  When they build the axes from the handoff pack alone
  Then every value they need (spacing, tokens, type, decimation rule, keyboard behaviour) is in the pack
  And this is verified during the walkthrough by having them attempt exactly that

Scenario: Behaviour that a static frame cannot express is written as a rule
  Given axis label decimation, gridline selection, tooltip collision and magnet snapping
  When the pack is reviewed
  Then each is specified as a rule that produces a deterministic result at any zoom level
  And none is left as a set of example frames to interpolate between

  Given the token mapping table
  Then every element maps to a design-system token slot
  And no hex value appears as an implementation instruction anywhere in the pack
```

**Why rules rather than frames.** A chart is continuous: there is no "the" zoom level, so a design expressed as three example frames leaves the engineer to invent the behaviour between them — and they will invent something reasonable and different from what was intended.
```
timeAxisLabels(range, widthPx):
  candidates = niceIntervals(range)            // 1/2/5 x 10^n in time units
  interval   = smallest candidate whose label spacing >= minGapPx
  labels     = ticks at that interval
  always keep: session boundaries, day boundaries      // never dropped
  drop order when crowded: minor, then hour, then day  // day is last
```

**Tokens, not values.** Handing over hex values guarantees drift the first time a token changes. The mapping table gives slot names, which is also what makes E11-T04's "no hard-coded colours" check pass.

**The walkthrough's real purpose** is to surface the questions nobody knew they had. title: Spike: fix the SDF glyph set and atlas size for the design font (O2)
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §16 tracks **open item O2 — "Exact SDF atlas size/glyph set for the chosen design-system font"** — owned by the chart-engine lead plus the design-system team, due at engine milestone M3. §3.7 assumes a 1024×1024 single-channel atlas costing ~40 ms to generate once per font/size-class, cached in IndexedDB. Both the size and the generation cost are *assumptions carried from research*, not measurements against the font E05 actually ships.

Getting this wrong is expensive in two directions: an atlas too small silently drops glyphs (footprint numbers render as blanks at the densest zoom, the exact place the product is most valuable), and an atlas too large costs GPU memory against the 600 MB per-instance budget and slows cold start against B9 (<=900 ms to first frame).

The spike answers it with numbers before E11-S11 implements the pipeline.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Take the final design-system font family/weights from `16-design-system-brief.md` as shipped by E05.
- Enumerate the required glyph set from real product surfaces, not guesses: digits, `.`, `,`, `-`, `+`, `%`, `×`, `K`, `M`, `B` (compact number formatting), `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z` for axis/legend labels, plus the currency/unit glyphs actually used by `CMP-188`/`CMP-189` tick formatters and the `(estimated)` label.
- Generate the SDF atlas at 512², 1024² and 2048² for each size class (`comfortable`/`compact`/`dense` per §5 rule 5) using the two-pass EDT (Felzenszwalb) described in §3.7.
- Measure per variant: generation wall time (cold), IndexedDB read time (warm), atlas bytes, glyph coverage (any dropped glyph is a hard fail), and rendered legibility at 11 px and at the LOD text-hiding threshold.
- Compare shelf packing against a skyline packer if 1024² overflows — only if it overflows.
- Produce a decision table and an amendment to **ADR-0002** recording the chosen atlas size, glyph set, size classes and packer.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the production pipeline, batching, or the outline shader variant — E11-S11.
- Multi-language/CJK glyph coverage: the product is English-only (`locale` default `'en-GB'`, §8) and CJK would change the strategy entirely; if that ever changes, a new spike is required.
- MSDF (multi-channel) — evaluate only if single-channel SDF fails legibility at 11 px; record the finding either way.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The question is answered with measurements
  Given the shipped design-system font and the enumerated glyph set
  When the atlas is generated at 512, 1024 and 2048 for all three density size classes
  Then a table records generation time, warm-load time, bytes and glyph coverage for each
  And a single (size, glyph set, packer) combination is recommended with its rationale

Scenario: Coverage is a hard gate
  Given a candidate atlas size
  When any required glyph fails to pack
  Then that size is rejected outright regardless of its timing numbers
  And the rejection is recorded in the table rather than silently dropped

Scenario: The decision is recorded where implementers will find it
  Given the spike concludes
  Then ADR-0002 carries an amendment naming the chosen atlas configuration
  And open item O2 in 26-chart-engine-design.md §16 is marked closed with a link to it
  And E11-S11 is updated with the chosen values before it enters a sprint
```

## Technical notes / design
**Timebox: 3 working days**, agreed with the Architect; not extendable without an Architect note on the ticket.

**Decision rule, stated up front:** choose the smallest atlas size that achieves 100 % glyph coverage for all three size classes with cold generation <=60 ms and warm IndexedDB load <=5 ms (the B9 secondary gate). If 1024² meets it, 1024² is chosen and no further work is done. If 1024² fails coverage, split into per-size-class atlases before going to 2048² — two 1024² atlases beat one 2048² on both memory and generation time. If single-channel SDF fails legibility at 11 px in a blind A/B with two designers, escalate to MSDF and record the memory cost (3× bytes).

Explicitly **not** production code: the prototype lives on `spike/chart-engine-sdf-atlas` and is left unmerged; only the measurements and the ADR amendment are the deliverables.

## Test plan
Not a test-bearing ticket. Evidence required for DoD: the measurement table, screenshots of rendered numbers at 11 px and at the LOD threshold for each candidate, and the raw benchmark script committed on the spike branch so the numbers are reproducible.

## Security notes
No security surface: fonts are bundled first-party assets, generation is local and deterministic. One note carried forward to E11-S11: the IndexedDB atlas cache is keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))` — the hash must cover the glyph set so a changed set cannot silently load a stale atlas (a correctness issue that would look like a rendering bug, not a security one, but is fixed by the same control).

## Accessibility notes
Legibility is an accessibility outcome, not only an aesthetic one. The blind A/B legibility check includes a low-vision reviewer from the accessibility team, and the recommendation must state the minimum cell height at which per-cell text remains legible — that number becomes the LOD text-hiding threshold in E11-S12 and is quoted in `05-accessibility-standard.md`'s chart section.

## Performance notes
Feeds B9 (cold init to first frame <=900 ms, with "SDF atlas from cache <=5 ms" as the secondary gate) and the §7 memory line "SDF atlas 1024×1024×1 B = 1.0 MB". Any recommendation above 1024² must state the new memory figure against the 600 MB per-instance budget.

## Observability
None (spike). The production pipeline in E11-S11 adds `engine.text.atlas_generate_ms` and `engine.text.atlas_cache_hit`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Question answered with recorded evidence: the measurement table and legibility screenshots are attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Decision recorded as an amendment to `27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`; open item O2 marked closed in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.
- [ ] E11-S11's Scope updated with the chosen atlas size, glyph set and packer before it enters Sprint 06.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review and at the design-system sync (the glyph set is a shared artefact with E05).

title: Write the black-box test plan for chart navigation, scales, crosshair and axes
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a black-box test plan executed by QA/SDET for every Story, with a sign-off comment carrying pass/fail per scenario. E11's interaction stories — pan/zoom (S04), scale modes (S05), axes (S06), crosshair (S07) — are where a black-box view earns its keep: the unit tests verify that `zoomAt` returns the right transform, and a user discovers that zooming near the right edge with autoscale on and a locked price axis does something surprising.

This plan covers the **interaction group**. Multi-pane, LOD, a11y and memory are covered by Q02, Q03, Q05 and Q06 respectively, so the four plans together cover the Epic without overlapping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan covering **E11-S04** (pan/zoom/momentum), **E11-S05** (linear/log/percent/inverted, autoscale, manual lock), **E11-S06** (axes, decimation, keyboard rescale) and **E11-S07** (crosshair, OHLCV readout, countdown).
- Scenarios derived from `US-CHART-006`, `US-CHART-007` and `US-CHART-008`, including every Gherkin scenario in those stories as a named, executable test case.
- **Combination coverage** — the part unit tests cannot reach: log scale + autoscale + manual lock; percent scale + a reference bar scrolled out of view; inverted + log together; zoom at the extreme right edge with the forming bar; momentum interrupted by a scale change; crosshair magnet across a gap in data.
- **Boundary cases**: single bar loaded; two bars; all bars identical price (zero range — a classic division-by-zero in autoscale); a series containing a non-positive value with log requested (`US-CHART-007` scenario 3); bar spacing at its minimum and maximum; the first and last bar of the series.
- **Failure cases**: scale change during an in-flight momentum decay; rapid repeated mode switching; keyboard and pointer input arriving in the same frame; interaction during a data update storm.
- **Reduced-motion path** exercised as a first-class case, not an afterthought.
- Exploratory charter for the interaction group (90 minutes, time-boxed, with a stated mission).
- Plan committed to `packages/chart-engine/test/plans/` so it lives beside the code it tests.

## Out of scope
- Multi-pane and sync — **E11-Q02**. Performance numbers — **E11-Q03**. Chaos and robustness — **E11-Q04**. Accessibility conformance — **E11-Q05**. Epic-level regression — **E11-Q06**. GPU matrix — **E11-Q07**.
- Series rendering behaviour (candles, Heikin-Ashi) — E12's QA.
- Writing the automated E2E implementations — **E11-Q02** owns the suite; this plan defines what it must cover.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every user-story scenario is an executable test case
  Given US-CHART-006, US-CHART-007 and US-CHART-008
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then every Gherkin scenario in those stories appears as a named test case with explicit steps and expected results
  And each case states which E11 ticket it verifies

Scenario: Combinations are covered, not just individual features
  Given the scale modes, autoscale, manual lock and zoom behaviours
  When the plan's combination matrix is inspected
  Then log + autoscale + lock, percent with an off-screen reference, and inverted + log are all covered
  And each combination states the expected behaviour precisely enough to fail a test on

Scenario: Degenerate data is covered
  Given a series where every bar has an identical price, giving a zero price range
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then a case exists asserting autoscale produces a sane range rather than a division by zero or a collapsed axis

Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with the engine
  When they execute the plan
  Then every case has steps, expected results and the fixture to use
  And no case requires asking the author what "correct" means

Scenario: Execution produces a sign-off with per-scenario results
  When the plan is executed against a build
  Then a sign-off comment records pass or fail for every scenario with evidence
  And failures are filed as defects with priority and owner
```

## Technical notes / design
**Fixtures.** Cases reference named fixtures from `packages/fixtures` so results are reproducible: `btcusdt-1m-100k` (the volume case), `btcusdt-1m-spike` (decimation and autoscale extremes), `btcusdt-1m-gap` (missing data, for magnet and decimation), `synthetic-flat` (zero price range), `synthetic-nonpositive` (the log-disable case). Ad hoc "load some data and have a look" cases are not acceptable, because they cannot be re-run against a later build.

**Why combinations get their own matrix.** Each of scale mode, autoscale state, lock state and zoom anchor is individually simple; the defects live in their interaction. The matrix is explicit rather than left to exploratory testing because these combinations are all reachable in normal use, not obscure — a trader on a log-scaled chart who drags the price axis has entered a three-way combination without trying.

**Exploratory charter format** per `03-testing-strategy.md`: mission, areas, timebox, and a session sheet recording what was tried, what was found and what was not covered.

## Test plan
The deliverable is itself a test plan; its own verification is:
- Traceability check: every Gherkin scenario from the three user stories is present.
- Peer review by the chart-engine lead, to reconcile the black-box view with known implementation edges.
- A dry run against the current build to confirm every case is executable as written.
- Fixture existence check — a plan referencing a fixture that does not exist is not executable.

## Security notes
No security surface; the plan exercises market-data rendering with synthetic fixtures only. Any defect with a security or safety implication found during execution is routed to **E11-X03** and labelled `security` per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, rather than being filed as an ordinary rendering bug.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the **keyboard equivalents** for every pointer interaction it covers, because `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 makes them functional requirements rather than accessibility extras: keyboard pan/zoom/reset (`US-CHART-006`'s NFR), keyboard axis rescale (CMP-188/189), keyboard crosshair stepping (`US-CHART-008`). Conformance auditing — axe-core, screen readers, contrast — is **E11-Q05**; this plan simply verifies the keyboard paths work as functionality.

## Performance notes
Not a performance plan, but every interaction case is executed against the 100k-bar fixture so that a case which is functionally correct and unusably slow is caught here rather than being assumed to be someone else's problem. Measured budgets are **E11-Q03**.

## Observability
Execution results and the exploratory session sheets attached to the ticket. Defects link back to the plan case that found them, so the plan's yield is measurable and the weak areas of the next plan are informed by it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S07** — the last story in the interaction group; planning before it lands would mean re-planning.
- **E11-S04**, **S05**, **S06** — the stories under test.
- Feeds **E11-Q02** (E2E automation) and **E11-Q06** (regression pack).

## Branch
`test/chart-engine-interaction-plan` · plan committed to `packages/chart-engine/test/plans/`.

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` — test pyramid, coverage floors, fixture conventions, flake policy
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budgets, measurement method, regression gate
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` — WCAG 2.2 AA target, canvas strategy, manual pass requirements
