title: Build the WebGL2 backend with capability probing and context-loss recovery
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4 owns the GL backend: program/VAO/buffer/texture lifecycle, the atlas, and the state sorting that keeps draw calls at the §4 target of **<=18 per pane and <=40 for a 3-pane chart**. §1 requirement R9 mandates that the engine still runs when WebGL2 is unavailable, and requirement R8 (`32-risk-register.md` R8 Browser/GPU compat) is the risk this story carries: driver quirks, WebView2 differences, and GPU resets in the middle of a trading session.

Context loss is not hypothetical — a driver reset, a laptop switching GPUs, or a browser reclaiming memory all trigger it, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 makes recovery an **R1 exit criterion (#8)**: "forcing `WEBGL_lose_context` restores a fully correct scene within 2 s with no data loss". Because the `DataModel` lives in the worker and is independent of GL, recovery is a rebuild of GPU state from CPU state — which is only true if nothing in the engine treats a GL object as the source of truth. This story enforces that.

The user-visible half is **SCR-048**: "Graphics context lost — restoring…", auto-retry ×3 then a manual Retry plus a link to SCR-118 renderer settings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/gl/GLBackend.ts`: context acquisition with the E10-tuned attributes (`{ alpha: false, antialias: false, depth: false, stencil: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance', preserveDrawingBuffer: false, desynchronized: true }`), program compilation/caching, VAO and buffer lifecycle, texture and LUT management, draw-list submission sorted by program then texture.
- Shader programs required by §4 for this Epic's layers: `line` (grid, sessions, crosshair, indicator lines — thick-line expansion in the vertex shader from per-instance `p0`,`p1`,`width`, dash pattern index), `quad`, `sdf-text` (E11-S11 supplies the atlas), and a `bar`/`cell` program stub registered for E18/E19 to implement against.
- **Capability probe** run at `init`, producing the `ready` capability report and selecting `RenderProfile`: `full` (WebGL2 + required extensions + adequate `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`), `reduced` (WebGL2 but constrained limits — smaller atlas, fewer instanced attributes), `degraded-2d` (no WebGL2 — handled by E11-T05).
- Context-loss handling: listen for `webglcontextlost` (call `preventDefault()`), tear down GPU-side state only, emit `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST` with `recoverable: true`, and on `webglcontextrestored` rebuild programs, buffers, VAOs, textures and the atlas from CPU state within 2 s. Auto-retry ×3 with 1/2/4 s backoff, then `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED` and the manual-retry path of SCR-048.
- A **GL-object ownership rule** enforced by review and by a test: no subsystem may hold a GL handle across frames except via the backend's registry, so recovery can invalidate and recreate everything centrally.
- Draw-call trace recorder (`§14` determinism aid): an opt-in mode recording the ordered draw list for structural test assertions.
- Error code table owned here: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED`.

## Out of scope
- The Canvas-2D rendering path itself — E11-T05 (this story selects the profile and hands off).
- The SDF atlas generation pipeline — E11-S11 (this story consumes an atlas texture).
- Heatmap texture streaming (`texSubImage2D` rolling ring) — E21; the texture-management seam is provided here.
- WebGPU backend — explicit future seam only, per §3.4 non-goals.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Context loss recovers within the R1 exit budget
  Given a chart with 100 000 bars, 3 panes and an active crosshair
  When WEBGL_lose_context is forced
  Then SCR-048 shows "Graphics context lost — restoring…" in a role="alert" region
  And a fully correct scene is restored within 2 s, verified by a golden image matching the pre-loss frame at <=0.1 % pixel diff
  And no bar, cell or drawing is lost from the DataModel

Scenario: Repeated loss gives up gracefully rather than looping
  Given context restoration fails three consecutive times
  When the third retry completes
  Then ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED is emitted and SCR-048 shows a manual Retry plus a link to SCR-118
  And the render loop is parked rather than spinning

Scenario: Capability probing selects a profile instead of crashing
  Given a runtime reporting WebGL2 with MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE below the atlas requirement
  When the chart initialises
  Then RenderProfile "reduced" is selected, reported in the ready message, and shown in SCR-046
  And the user is told which capabilities are reduced and why — never shown a blank canvas

Scenario: Draw calls stay within the architectural budget
  Given a 3-pane chart rendering grid, candles, indicator lines and a crosshair
  When the draw-call trace for one frame is inspected
  Then there are <=18 draw calls for any single pane and <=40 for the chart
  And the list is ordered so that program switches are minimised

Scenario: A shader that fails to compile is a handled error
  Given a shader source that fails to compile on a specific driver
  When the backend initialises
  Then ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED is emitted with the driver info string and the program name
  And the engine falls back to degraded-2d rather than rendering a blank canvas
```

## Technical notes / design
Context attributes are tuned deliberately: `antialias: false` because candle geometry is device-pixel-snapped (E11-S10) and MSAA costs fill rate for no benefit here; `depth: false`/`stencil: false` because ordering is done by layer and draw order; `desynchronized: true` to shave a frame of latency for budget #6 (input-to-photon <=2 frames).

Thick-line expansion in the vertex shader (§3.10): per-instance `p0`, `p1`, `width`, `dashPatternIdx`; the quad is expanded along the segment normal in clip space with a per-vertex sign attribute. No geometry shader (WebGL2 has none) and no CPU-side triangulation.

Precision: prices arrive as integer ticks; `priceOrigin` is a **uniform** subtracted in the vertex shader before the float conversion (E11-S03 owns the maths). Passing absolute BTC-magnitude prices as `float` attributes is the classic precision bug this avoids.

Recovery algorithm: on `webglcontextrestored`, walk the backend's resource registry and recreate in dependency order — programs -> LUT textures -> SDF atlas (from IndexedDB cache, <=5 ms) -> static buffers -> per-series dynamic buffers repopulated from the `DataModel` by marking every node `DATA`-dirty. The scene graph is untouched; only GPU mirrors are rebuilt.

State sorting: batches carry `(programId, textureId, layerIndex)`; submission sorts by `layerIndex` first (correctness — layers must composite in order) then by `programId`, then `textureId` within the layer.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: resource registry lifecycle (create/invalidate/recreate); draw-list sort stability; capability-probe decision matrix over synthetic `getParameter` responses (WebGL2 absent / limits low / all good / extension missing).
- **Robustness** (§14 fuzz layer, required check): injected context loss at 50 random points in a scripted session — including mid-`bufferSubData`, mid-atlas-upload and during a resize — must always recover or report, never hang; zero-size canvas; DPR change mid-flight.
- **Golden image** (Playwright + SwiftShader, <=0.1 % diff): pre-loss vs post-restore frame equality; grid + crosshair + line rendering per theme.
- **Contract**: draw-call trace assertions for the <=18/pane and <=40/chart budgets.
- **Cross-shell** (§14): the loss/recovery test runs in browser Chromium, Electron, and (while ADR-0011 is open) Tauri/WebView2; results reported per release.
- **E2E**: SCR-048 alert copy, correlation id selectability, retry button focusability.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. Threats handled here:
- **Tampering / supply chain**: shader sources are static, bundled, first-party strings. There is **no dynamic shader construction from data** and no `eval` — a data-driven shader string would be a code-injection vector through the market feed. A lint rule forbids template-literal shader sources containing interpolation of non-constant values.
- **Denial of service**: a driver-level GPU hang cannot be prevented from JS, but the retry policy is bounded (3 attempts, exponential backoff) so a failing GPU degrades to `degraded-2d` instead of spinning the render loop and heating the machine — `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-048 states explicitly that "failures never spin the render loop".
- **Information disclosure**: the capability report includes `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` (GPU vendor/model) for diagnostics. This is fingerprinting-adjacent data; it is shown only in SCR-046 (owner/developer overlay, hidden by default per its catalogue entry) and included in copied diagnostics with an explicit note, never sent to any third party.
Requires the `security` label; covered by E11-X01's STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-048's contract is implemented against here: `role="alert"` region with plain-language text ("Graphics context lost — restoring…"), a **selectable** correlation id as text, and a focusable Retry button that is not colour-only. The reduced/degraded profile must be communicated in words ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells" per SCR-030's low-GPU state), never by appearance alone. During recovery, focus must not be stolen from wherever the user had it; the alert announces without moving focus.

## Performance notes
Owns the "composite + present" (<=1.6 ms) and draw-submission slices of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, and the §4 draw-call targets. Benchmarks: B1 (draw calls <=8 for pure candles), B5 (total <=40), B9 (cold init to first frame <=900 ms — program compilation is the dominant term, so programs are compiled lazily per layer actually used, and compilation time is recorded). Recovery must complete <=2 s (R1 exit criterion 8), measured as an explicit benchmark, not by eye.

## Observability
Codes: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED`, each with `recoverable`. `FrameStats` gains `drawCalls`, `triangles`, `gpuMemoryMbEstimate`, `renderProfile`. Counters: `engine.gl.context_losses`, `engine.gl.restore_ms`, `engine.gl.program_compile_ms{program}`. `chart.error_shown {code, correlationId}` is emitted by the app layer from these events (SCR-048 analytics).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.

- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S01** — the ordered draw list and the layer model.
- **E10** — Electron GPU flags and CSP; the renderer must already be launched with the flag set chosen in E06.
- Blocks **E11-S03** (uniforms), **E11-S10** (DPI/backing store), **E11-S11** (atlas texture), **E11-T05** (degraded-2d), **E21** (heatmap texture streaming).

title: Project time and price to screen through one shared, tick-precise transform
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007`'s NFR states the rule this story exists to enforce: **"projection is a single shared function used by every renderer, covered by unit tests"**. Every candle, cell, drawing, order line, profile row and axis tick must agree on where a price is, or overlays drift against the data they annotate — a class of bug that is invisible in code review and obvious to a trader.

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 specifies the maths: viewport state `{timeStart, timeEnd}` in µs float64 plus per-pane `{priceLow, priceHigh}` and a scale mode; screen mapping computed on the CPU into uniforms once per pane per frame. It also fixes the **bar-space vs time-space** distinction that every trading chart needs: panning and bar spacing operate in bar-index space (`barSpacing` px/bar, `rightOffset` in bars) while overlays needing true time (heatmap columns, session shading) map through `time`, with `BarStore` keeping a monotone index->time map.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/viewport/Viewport.ts` — state `{ timeStart, timeEnd }` (µs, float64), per-pane `{ priceLow, priceHigh, scaleMode }`, `barSpacing`, `rightOffset`.
- The single projection module `src/viewport/transform.ts` exporting `indexToScreen`, `timeToScreen`, `priceToScreen`, `screenToIndex`, `screenToPrice`, `screenToTime` — used by **every** renderer and by hit-testing, with no second implementation anywhere in the codebase (enforced by a lint rule forbidding arithmetic on `priceLow`/`priceHigh` outside this module).
- Linear mapping per §3.5: `sx = (t - timeOrigin) * kx + bx` with `kx = plotWidth / (timeEnd - timeStart)`; `sy = (p - priceOrigin) * ky + by` with `ky = -plotHeight / (priceHigh - priceLow)`.
- Tick-integer precision: prices are integer ticks; `priceOrigin` is subtracted before the float conversion and passed to shaders as a uniform, so GPU-side floats never carry BTC-magnitude values.
- Uniform block assembly: one CPU-side computation per pane per frame feeding the GL uniforms, so a pan is a uniform update and not a buffer update (the §3.1 dirty-flag contract).
- `barSpacing` clamped to `[0.05, 200]` px; `rightOffset` clamped so the last bar cannot be panned entirely off-screen.
- Cursor-anchored zoom primitive: `zoomAt(anchorPx, factor)` keeping the world coordinate under the anchor invariant (used by E11-S04 for wheel and pinch).

## Out of scope
- Log/percent/inverted scale modes and autoscale — E11-S05 (they plug into this module as alternative `priceToScreen` implementations).
- Input handling, momentum and gesture recognition — E11-S04.
- Axis tick generation and label formatting — E11-S06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round-trips are exact
  Given any viewport and any bar index within the loaded range
  When screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) is evaluated
  Then the result equals i for all 10 000 property-test cases
  And the same holds for screenToPrice(priceToScreen(p)) within half a tick

Scenario: One projection serves every renderer
  Given the codebase is scanned by the projection lint rule
  When any module other than viewport/transform.ts performs arithmetic on priceLow/priceHigh
  Then the build fails naming the offending module and the US-CHART-007 NFR

Scenario: Zoom keeps the point under the cursor fixed
  Given the cursor is over the bar at 2026-11-24T12:00:00Z at x = 640 px
  When zoomAt(640, 1.25) is applied
  Then that bar's time still maps to x = 640 px (±0.5 px)
  And barSpacing is clamped into [0.05, 200]

Scenario: Prices keep sub-tick precision at BTC magnitudes
  Given a symbol with tickSize 0.5 and prices around 64 000
  When a bar's high and a drawing anchored to it are both projected
  Then their screen y values differ by less than 0.5 px
  And no float32 value in the pipeline ever holds the absolute price

Scenario: Panning does not touch GPU buffers
  Given a viewport change of 200 px
  When the next frame is built
  Then only uniforms are updated and bufferSubData is not called
```

## Technical notes / design
Keep `time` in float64 microseconds everywhere on the CPU (float32 µs epoch loses ~minutes of precision). Only the *relative* values reach the GPU.

Bar-space is authoritative for panning: `timeStart/timeEnd` are derived from `(firstVisibleIndex, barSpacing, plotWidth)` via the store's index->time map, not the other way round — this is why bar spacing stays exact while time gaps (maintenance windows, thin liquidity) do not stretch bars. Overlays that are genuinely time-anchored (heatmap columns, session bands) use `timeToScreen`, which interpolates through the same monotone map.

`screenToIndex` is O(1) analytic (`floor((x - bx) / barSpacing) + firstVisibleIndex`); `screenToTime` is O(log n) through the index->time binary search. Hit-testing (E11-S08) relies on the O(1) path for its budget.

Clamping is applied in the setter, not the getter, so the viewport never holds an out-of-range value that a renderer could observe.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: mapping against hand-computed values for a fixed viewport; clamping at both `barSpacing` bounds; `rightOffset` limit; `zoomAt` anchor invariance at the left edge, centre and right edge; degenerate cases (`priceHigh === priceLow`, zero-width plot, single bar).
- **Property** (fast-check, must hold over 10 000 cases per §14): `screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) === i`; `priceToScreen` monotone decreasing in price; projecting then unprojecting a price is within half a tick; zoom anchor invariance for random anchors and factors in `[0.1, 10]`.
- **Integration**: a candle, a drawing anchored to its high, and an axis tick at the same price all render within 0.5 px in a golden image.
- **Perf**: transform computation <=0.05 ms per pane per frame; part of the <=2 ms "data-window recompute" stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.
- Coverage >=90 % (pure maths; cheap to cover, catastrophic to get wrong).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
The transform is what lets the DOM mirror place surrogate nodes exactly over the canvas region they represent — `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires the surrogate to be "sized to match the visual target for pointer users using it too", which simultaneously satisfies target-size and focus-visible rules. E11-S13 calls `indexToScreen`/`priceToScreen` for that placement, so a transform bug is an a11y bug; the golden-image test above includes a mirror-node bounding-box assertion.

## Performance notes
Serves budget #1. Because a pan is a uniform update rather than a buffer update, this story is the single largest contributor to B1 (100k candles, continuous pan at 1000 px/s, p95 <=12 ms, draw calls <=8). A regression here shows up as `bufferSubData` traffic during pan, which the B1 secondary gate catches directly.

## Observability
`viewport` worker->main message (<=1/frame) carrying `{ timeStart, timeEnd, priceLow, priceHigh, barSpacing }` — consumed by sync groups (E11-S09), the a11y layer and SCR-046. No new error codes.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies

- **E11-T03** — the monotone index->time map lives on `BarStore`.
- Blocks **E11-S04**, **E11-S05**, **E11-S06**, **E11-S08**, **E11-S12**, and every renderer in E12+.

title: Pan and zoom with cursor-anchored zoom, momentum and keyboard equivalents
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-006` (Must) — *"As a trader, I want fluid pan/zoom with auto-fit and manual scale lock, so that navigation never fights me"* — with the NFR **"input-to-pixel latency <=1 frame; keyboard equivalents for pan/zoom/reset (arrow keys, +/-, Home)"**. This is the interaction a trader performs thousands of times a day; it is also the canonical "boring parity" item that `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 warns costs 4–8 weeks and must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

§3.11 fixes the gesture table and §3.5 the momentum model. The a11y standard makes the keyboard path mandatory rather than a nicety: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids hover-only and drag-only functionality, so every pointer gesture here needs a keyboard equivalent of equal capability, and momentum must honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

This story covers **time-axis and plot-area navigation**. Price-scale modes, autoscale and the lock badge are E11-S05 (`US-CHART-007` and the autoscale/lock scenarios of `US-CHART-006`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/interaction/InputRouter.ts` (main thread): `setPointerCapture`, `getCoalescedEvents()` for pointers, wheel accumulation, and forwarding **at most one batch per frame** to the worker as the packed `input` message from E11-T02.
- Gestures per §3.11: drag on plot = pan time (and price when the price scale is unlocked); wheel = zoom time at cursor; `Shift+wheel` = horizontal pan; `Ctrl+wheel` = zoom price; drag on time axis = compress/expand `barSpacing`; double-click plot = reset to auto-scale + latest bar; pinch (touch/trackpad) = zoom at centroid, two-finger drag pans.
- Cursor-anchored zoom through `Viewport.zoomAt` (E11-S03) so the world coordinate under the cursor is invariant.
- Momentum per §3.5: velocity-based with exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)`, tau = 120 ms, terminated below 0.02 px/ms, **cancelled on any new pointer-down**; integrated by the scheduler's time-based animation so dropped frames do not change the resting position.
- **Reduced motion**: when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set (or the app-level setting from SCR-117 is on), momentum is disabled — the pan stops on pointer-up — and this is stated in the chart's keyboard-help text, not silently different.
- Keyboard equivalents (`US-CHART-006` NFR + §3.11): `<-/->` move the data cursor by a bar, `Shift+<-/->` by 10, `Home/End` jump to first/last bar, `+/-` zoom in/out about the cursor bar, `Space` as a pan-drag modifier, double-tap equivalent `Ctrl+Home` resets to auto-scale + latest bar.
- Kinetic scroll on touch with the same tau and the same reduced-motion rule.

## Out of scope
- Price-scale modes (log/percent/inverted), autoscale and the manual-lock badge — E11-S05.
- Crosshair rendering and the OHLCV readout — E11-S07.
- Cross-chart sync of the resulting viewport — E11-S09.
- `Alt+<-/->` replay tick stepping (§3.11) — E26.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pan and zoom stay above the frame floor
  Given BTCUSDT 1m with 100 000 bars loaded
  When the chart is panned horizontally at 1000 px/s for 5 s and then wheel-zoomed from 0.1 to 50 px/bar
  Then the measured frame rate stays at or above 55 fps throughout (benchmarks B1 and B2)
  And input-to-pixel latency is at most 1 frame

Scenario: Zoom is anchored to the cursor
  Given the cursor rests over the 14:00 bar
  When the wheel is scrolled to zoom in three notches
  Then the 14:00 bar remains under the cursor within 0.5 px at every step

Scenario: Inertia respects reduced-motion settings
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the user flicks the chart and releases
  Then the chart stops immediately at the release position with no glide
  And the keyboard-help text states that inertia is disabled

Scenario: Every pointer gesture has a keyboard equivalent
  Given the chart pane has keyboard focus and no mouse is used
  When the user presses <-, ->, Shift+->, Home, End, + and -
  Then the view pans by one bar, ten bars, jumps to the first and last bar, and zooms in and out about the cursor bar
  And Ctrl+Home resets to auto-scale with the latest bar visible

Scenario: A high-rate trackpad cannot flood the worker
  Given a trackpad emitting 240 wheel events per second
  When the events are routed
  Then at most one input batch per frame is posted to the worker with the deltas accumulated
  And no zoom step is lost — the accumulated delta equals the sum of the raw deltas

Scenario: A new touch cancels momentum immediately
  Given a momentum glide is in progress
  When the user puts a finger or pointer down on the plot
  Then the glide stops on that frame and the new drag begins from the current position
```

## Technical notes / design
Wheel handling is the subtle part: trackpads emit far more than 60 events/s and mix pixel/line/page delta modes. Accumulate `deltaY` normalised to pixels (`deltaMode` 0/1/2 -> ×1/×16/×plotHeight) into a per-frame accumulator, apply once in the worker, then clear. Never apply per-event — that is the classic cause of zoom "racing" on macOS trackpads.

Pointer events use `getCoalescedEvents()` so a 240 Hz stylus/trackpad still yields one batch per frame carrying every sample (needed for accurate velocity), packed into the `Float32Array` layout defined in E11-T02.

Velocity estimate for momentum: exponentially weighted over the last 50 ms of coalesced samples, not a two-point difference (two-point is noisy at high sample rates and makes flicks feel inconsistent).

`Space` as a pan-drag modifier follows the design-tool convention and must not conflict with the global shortcut registry from E10 — register through it rather than attaching a raw listener, so a conflict is detected at registration time.

Reduced-motion resolution order: OS media query -> app accessibility setting (SCR-117) -> chart option. Any of them being "reduce" disables momentum; the engine never overrides a user preference in the other direction.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: wheel delta-mode normalisation; per-frame accumulation and clearing; velocity estimation over synthetic sample trains; momentum integration with `TestClock` (including dropped-frame equivalence); clamp behaviour at `barSpacing` bounds; reduced-motion resolution matrix.
- **Interaction/E2E** (Playwright web + Electron, §14 interaction layer): drag-pan, wheel-zoom, `Shift+wheel`, `Ctrl+wheel`, time-axis drag, double-click reset, pinch, and the full keyboard set — each asserted against the resulting viewport, not against pixels.
- **Perf**: B1 (pan, p95 <=12 ms, draw calls <=8) and B2 (zoom sweep 0.1->50 px/bar, p95 <=14 ms, **no LOD flicker — LOD changes <=6 over the sweep**).
- **A11y**: keyboard-only traversal of the whole gesture set with axe-core clean; reduced-motion assertion; announcement throttling verified with E11-S13's live region.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
This story is where the "no drag-only, no hover-only" rule of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 is either honoured or lost. Requirements verified in QA, not just implemented:
- Every gesture in §3.11 has a keyboard equivalent of equal capability, documented in the global hotkey table (E10) and discoverable from the chart's keyboard-help affordance.
- The chart pane is a single tab stop with a visible focus ring (CMP-004 FocusRing); arrow keys move the data cursor rather than scrolling the page, and the pane does not trap focus — `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` leave it.
- Momentum honours `prefers-reduced-motion` (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions).
- Viewport changes are announced through the throttled polite live region at <=2/s (E11-S13), summarised ("showing 09:00 to 13:00, 240 bars") rather than per-frame.
- Motion spec and easing come from **E11-D06**, which must be signed off before this story starts (design-ahead rule).

## Performance notes
Budget #1 plus the <=1 ms input stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 and budget #6's input-to-photon <=2 frames (requirement R6). Hard gates: B1 and B2. The "no LOD flicker" secondary gate on B2 is what the ±15 % hysteresis dead band in E11-S12 exists for — if B2 reports more than 6 LOD changes across the sweep, this story is not done.

## Observability
Analytics emitted by the app layer from engine events: `chart.time_scale_changed` (SCR-043). Counters: `engine.input.batches_per_frame`, `engine.input.coalesced_ratio`, `engine.momentum.cancelled`. Frame stats already carry LOD level so a zoom sweep's LOD history is reconstructable from the SCR-046 feed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S03** — `zoomAt` and the viewport clamps.
- **E11-D06** — the motion spec (easing curves, momentum feel, reduced-motion variants) must be Done >=2 sprints earlier.
- **E10** — global keyboard-shortcut registry (conflict detection).
- Blocks **E11-S07** (crosshair follows the cursor this routes), **E11-S09** (sync broadcasts the viewport this changes).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-pan-zoom` · 2 PRs (pointer/wheel routing + zoom anchoring; momentum + keyboard equivalents), each <=400 LOC.

## References

title: Support linear, log, percent and inverted scales with autoscale and lock
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007` (Must/Should) — log (Must), linear (Must) and percentage (Should) price scales — plus the autoscale and manual-lock scenarios of `US-CHART-006`. **SCR-043** (price-scale context menu) fixes the exact item set: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100, invert, lock, merge indicator scales, reset.

The NFR that makes or breaks this story is `US-CHART-007`'s: *"projection is a single shared function used by every renderer, covered by unit tests"*. A log scale that only the candle renderer knows about produces drawings, profiles and order lines floating away from the price they annotate. Every scale mode is therefore implemented **inside** the E11-S03 transform module as an alternative `priceToScreen`/`screenToPrice` pair, never as a per-renderer adjustment.

The failure case is explicit in the story: a series containing non-positive values must **disable** log with an explanation rather than rendering incorrectly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scale modes in `src/viewport/scales.ts`, all four plugged into the shared transform: `linear`, `log` (`sy = (log(p) - log(priceLow)) / (log(priceHigh) - log(priceLow)) × -plotHeight + plotBottom`, §3.5), `percent` (computed against an anchor bar's close — the left-edge bar by default), `indexed-to-100` (percent normalised so the anchor reads 100).
- `invert` flag (flips the y mapping) and `lock` flag (disables autoscale), both orthogonal to the mode.
- **Autoscale** per §3.5: computed from the visible range's min/max with a configurable margin, optionally including visible drawings and overlays ("include drawings" option from `US-CHART-006`), recomputed only when the visible bar range changes and throttled to once per frame.
- **Manual lock**: dragging the price axis disengages autoscale, a lock badge appears on the axis, and double-clicking the axis restores auto-fit (`US-CHART-006` third scenario).
- **SCR-043 price-scale context menu**: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100 / invert / lock / merge indicator scales / reset — real menu semantics (CMP-041 Menu), reachable by `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus, checkable items with state announced.
- Log-mode guard: when the visible series contains a value <=0, the log item is disabled with an explanatory tooltip ("Log scale needs positive prices; this series contains 0 or negative values") and the scale stays on its previous mode.
- Persistence of the per-pane scale mode into the chart options object handed back to the app (E15 persists it into workspaces).

## Out of scope
- Axis tick generation, label formatting and decimation — E11-S06.
- The chart settings dialog surface (SCR-031 scale section) — built by E15/E13's settings work; this story exposes the options it binds to.
- Merging *indicator* scales across panes — the menu item is present and wired, but indicator scale objects arrive with E13; until then the item is disabled with "No indicators on this pane".
- Price-axis drag-to-rescale gesture plumbing — E11-S06 owns the axis component's gesture surface; this story owns what a rescale *means* for the scale state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Log scale re-projects everything, not just candles
  Given a chart with candles, a trend-line drawing, a horizontal level and a visible-range volume profile
  When the price scale is switched to logarithmic
  Then gridlines, candles, the drawing, the level and the profile all re-project through the shared transform
  And a golden image shows the drawing still anchored to the same two bar/price pairs

Scenario: Percent scale reads as change from the reference bar
  Given percentage mode with the left-edge bar as the reference
  When the crosshair moves across the visible range
  Then the axis and the readout display values as % change from that reference bar's close
  And switching the visible range re-anchors the reference to the new left-edge bar

Scenario: Log is refused, not faked, on non-positive data
  Given a series whose visible range contains a value of 0
  When the user opens the price-scale menu
  Then the "Logarithmic" item is disabled with an explanation of why
  And the scale remains on its previous mode with no rendering artefacts

Scenario: Manual drag disengages autoscale and is reversible
  Given autoscale is on
  When the user drags the price axis
  Then autoscale disengages and a lock badge appears on the axis with an accessible name "Price scale locked"
  And double-clicking the axis restores auto-fit and removes the badge

Scenario: Autoscale includes drawings only when asked
  Given a drawing extends 20 % above the visible price range and "include drawings" is off
  When the visible range changes
  Then the price range fits the bars only
  And enabling "include drawings" re-fits to include the drawing within one frame

Scenario: A scale change costs a projection change only
  Given a chart with 100 000 bars loaded
  When the scale mode is changed from linear to log
  Then no data refetch is issued and the redraw completes within one frame (SCR-043 performance note)
```

## Technical notes / design
All four modes are implemented as `{ toScreen(p, ctx), fromScreen(y, ctx), tickCandidates(range) }` triples registered in the transform module, so adding a mode never touches a renderer. `tickCandidates` is consumed by E11-S06 — log ticks are decade-anchored (1, 2, 5 × 10^n), percent ticks are round percentages, not linear price steps.

Percent/indexed anchor: the anchor is the **close of the left-most fully visible bar**, recomputed when the visible bar range changes (not every frame). Storing an absolute anchor price instead would make the percent scale drift as the user pans, which is not what traders expect.

Log guard: evaluated over the *visible* range only, re-evaluated when the range changes; a non-positive value scrolling into view while log is active switches the pane to linear with a polite announcement rather than producing `NaN` geometry — silently rendering `log(0)` is the failure `US-CHART-007` calls out.

Autoscale margin default 5 % top and bottom, configurable; computation is a single pass over the visible slice of `BarStore` (already bounded by the visible window, so it is O(visible bars) not O(100k)) and is throttled to once per frame per §3.5.

Inverted mode multiplies the mapping by -1 after the mode's own projection, so it composes with log and percent without special cases.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: each mode's `toScreen`/`fromScreen` against hand-computed values; round-trip within half a tick in all four modes; inverted composition with each mode; autoscale margin maths; anchor re-selection on range change; log guard triggering on 0 and on negative values.
- **Property** (fast-check, 10 000 cases): in every mode, `fromScreen(toScreen(p)) ~ p`; `toScreen` is strictly monotone in price (decreasing, or increasing when inverted); no mode ever returns `NaN` or `Infinity` for in-range input.
- **Golden image**: candles + drawing + level + profile rendered in linear and in log, per theme, asserting co-anchoring at <=0.1 % pixel diff.
- **E2E**: SCR-043 menu opened by right-click and by `Shift+F10`, every item toggled, checked state announced; axis drag then double-click restore; lock badge presence.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the menu; `aria-checked` state on each mode item; the lock badge has a text name, not colour alone.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-043's a11y contract is the acceptance bar: real menu semantics (`role="menu"`/`menuitemradio`/`menuitemcheckbox`), reachable via `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus, with each option's checked state announced. Additional requirements:
- The lock badge carries a text accessible name ("Price scale locked") — it may not be conveyed by an icon or colour alone.
- A mode change is announced once through the polite live region ("Price scale: logarithmic"), not on every subsequent frame.
- The disabled log item exposes its reason via `aria-describedby` so a screen-reader user learns *why* it is disabled, rather than finding an inert item.
- Design source: **E11-D03** (scale menus hi-fi) must be Done >=2 sprints before this story.

## Performance notes
SCR-043's performance note is a hard behaviour: "scale-mode changes are a projection change only — no data refetch, redraw within one frame". Autoscale recomputation is bounded to the visible window and throttled to once per frame (§3.5), contributing to the <=2 ms data-window recompute stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3. `Math.log` per vertex is avoided — the log mapping is applied CPU-side into the same uniform form, so the shader is unchanged across modes.

## Observability
Analytics: `chart.price_scale_changed` with `{mode, inverted, locked}` (SCR-043). Counters: `engine.scale.autoscale_recomputes`, `engine.scale.log_guard_trips`. A log-guard trip also emits a polite announcement and is visible in SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.

title: Render price and time axes with label decimation and keyboard rescale
body:
## Context
`CMP-188 PriceAxis` and `CMP-189 TimeAxis` are the chart's frame of reference — the components every other surface is read against. They are also a classic parity trap: naive tick generation produces labels that collide at one zoom level, disappear at another, and jitter by a sub-pixel as the user pans. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 names axis decimation and DPI correctness among the "boring things" that must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

The catalogue fixes the contracts. CMP-188: shared across panes bound to the same scale, supports linear/log, props `min/max`, `scaleType`, `tickFormatter`, `onDragScale`, and **"draggable-to-rescale has a keyboard equivalent (focus axis, arrow keys nudge scale)"**. CMP-189: horizontal time axis, "shared master clock across all panes in a chart (synced pan/zoom)", props `range`, `tickFormatter`, `onPan/onZoom`, with keyboard pan (`<-/->`) and zoom (`+/-`) documented in the global hotkey table.

Both expose their tick labels into the DOM mirror: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires "a real, if visually-hidden-when-redundant, list of tick values".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/axes/PriceAxis.ts` (**CMP-188**): tick generation per scale mode using the `tickCandidates` from E11-S05 (linear: 1/2/5 × 10^n; log: decade-anchored; percent: round percentages), label formatting to the instrument's `tickSize` precision, last-price label pinned and never overlapped by a tick label, drag-to-rescale, double-click to auto-fit.
- `src/axes/TimeAxis.ts` (**CMP-189**): time tick generation at the appropriate granularity for the visible span (seconds -> minutes -> hours -> days -> months), **session and day-boundary markers** rendered from the boundary setting, drag to compress/expand `barSpacing`, and the master-clock role for all panes in the chart.
- **Label decimation**: a greedy pass that keeps the highest-priority ticks (round hours before round minutes, decades before intermediates) and drops any label whose bounding box would overlap an already-placed one, with a minimum gap of 1.5× the label height. Priority ordering is stable across frames so labels do not flicker in and out while panning.
- **Device-pixel snapping**: gridlines and axis rules are snapped to device pixels (`Math.round(x * dpr) / dpr + 0.5/dpr`) so hairlines are crisp at any DPR rather than being blurred across two pixels.
- Axis gutters computed by the layout engine from the widest formatted label, re-measured only when the formatter, font or price magnitude class changes — not per frame.
- Keyboard rescale (CMP-188 contract): focusing the price axis and pressing `Up/Down` compresses/expands the price scale by one step; `Home` restores auto-fit. Focusing the time axis and pressing `<-/->` pans, `+/-` zooms.
- Timezone: labels rendered in UTC by default (`ChartOptions.timeZone`, default `'UTC'`), with the active timezone stated in the SCR-043 time-scale menu.
- Text is drawn through the SDF pipeline (E11-S11) as a single batched draw call per axis (§4 draw-call table).

## Out of scope
- The scale *modes* themselves and the SCR-043 menu — E11-S05.
- Session/day-boundary **configuration** (`US-CHART-009`, which anchor, funding-time resets) — E12; this story renders the markers from whatever boundary setting it is given.
- "Go to date" (SCR-044) — E11-S15 owns the paging it triggers; the dialog is E15's surface.
- Indicator-scale merging visuals — E13.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Labels decimate instead of colliding
  Given a chart zoomed so that 400 bars span 1200 px
  When the time axis renders
  Then no two labels overlap and every retained label keeps at least 1.5 label-heights of clear space
  And the retained set is a stable subset as the user pans — a label does not blink on and off between adjacent frames

Scenario: Hairlines are crisp at fractional DPR
  Given devicePixelRatio is 1.25
  When gridlines and the axis rule are drawn
  Then each is snapped to a device pixel and a golden image shows a single-pixel line with no grey fringe

Scenario: The price axis rescales by keyboard
  Given the price axis has keyboard focus
  When the user presses Up five times and then Home
  Then the price range compresses one step per press with each new range announced politely at most twice per second
  And Home restores auto-fit and announces "Price scale: auto"

Scenario: The time axis is the master clock for every pane
  Given a three-pane chart
  When the time axis is dragged to expand bar spacing
  Then all three panes change bar spacing together in the same frame
  And no pane lags by a frame

Scenario: Tick labels are present in the accessibility tree
  Given a screen reader inspects a chart pane
  When it navigates the DOM mirror
  Then the current price-axis tick values and time-axis tick labels are exposed as a readable list
  And the values match the labels drawn on the canvas for that frame

Scenario: The last-price label never hides behind a tick
  Given the last price falls within one label height of a regular tick
  When the axis renders
  Then the regular tick label is suppressed and the last-price label is drawn in full
```

## Technical notes / design
Tick generation is "nice number" selection: for a target of `plotHeight / (2.5 × labelHeight)` ticks, choose the step from `{1, 2, 2.5, 5} × 10^n` closest at or above the ideal step, then emit ticks at multiples of that step, quantised to `tickSize`. Log mode anchors at decades and inserts 2× and 5× intermediates only while they clear the overlap test.

Time granularity ladder: 1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m, 30 m, 1 h, 4 h, 1 d, 1 w, 1 M — pick the smallest whose spacing is >= the minimum label gap. Boundary ticks (day starts, session anchors) get priority 0 and are never decimated away before ordinary ticks.

Stability rule (what stops flicker): decimation operates on a **priority-ordered** candidate list, never on "every other label". Zooming changes which candidates exist but not their relative priority, so retained labels are a monotone subset as you zoom out.

Gutter measurement uses a cached text-measure per (format, font, magnitude class). Re-measuring per frame was measured as a real cost in comparable engines and is explicitly avoided; `LAYOUT` dirty is the only trigger.

Snapping: in the vertex shader for GL-drawn rules, positions are rounded to the device-pixel grid after the transform; for the 0.5-px offset convention, half-pixel offsets are applied in device space, not CSS space, which is why the DPR (E11-S10) must be exact.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: nice-number step selection across three orders of magnitude and for `tickSize` 0.01/0.5/1; time granularity ladder selection for spans from 10 s to 5 years; decimation stability (a label retained at zoom z is retained at every zoom >= z for the same range); gutter cache invalidation.
- **Golden image** (SwiftShader, <=0.1 % diff): price axis linear/log, time axis at 5 granularities, DPR 1 / 1.25 / 2, both themes, plus the last-price-label collision case.
- **Interaction/E2E**: axis drag rescale, double-click auto-fit, keyboard rescale, master-clock sync across 3 panes.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the chart route; DOM-mirror tick list matches the drawn labels (assertion compares the mirror text against the frame's tick model); announcement throttling <=2/s.
- **Perf**: axis rendering <=0.5 ms per axis per frame; one draw call per axis text batch (§4).
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-188/CMP-189 a11y contracts are the acceptance bar:
- Axis tick labels are materialised into the DOM mirror as a real list (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1) — windowed to the visible ticks, not all of them.
- Drag-to-rescale has a full keyboard equivalent (focus axis, arrows nudge, `Home` resets) — required because `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids drag-only functionality.
- Keyboard pan/zoom on the time axis is registered in the global hotkey table (E10) so it appears in the shortcuts help.
- Rescale announcements go through the polite region, throttled to <=2/s per §6.2 — a per-step announcement at key-repeat speed would flood.
- Each axis is a focusable element with a visible focus ring (CMP-004 FocusRing) and an accessible name ("Price axis, logarithmic, locked").
- Design source: **E11-D02** (chart chassis hi-fi incl. axis treatment) signed off >=2 sprints earlier.

## Performance notes
Axis text is one batched SDF draw call per axis (§4 draw-call table) — falling back to per-label draw calls would blow the <=18/pane budget on its own. Gutter measurement is cached. Contributes to budget #1; measured inside B1/B5. Label decimation runs only on `LAYOUT`/`TRANSFORM` dirty frames and is O(candidate ticks), which is bounded by plot height / label height (tens), never by bar count.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.axis.ticks_drawn{axis}`, `engine.axis.labels_decimated{axis}`, `engine.axis.gutter_remeasures`. A sustained high `gutter_remeasures` is the signature of a formatter thrashing and is visible in SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S05** — per-mode tick candidates.
- **E11-S11** — the SDF text pipeline that draws the labels; axes are its first consumer.
- **E11-S10** — exact DPR for device-pixel snapping (delivered in the same sprint; the snapping helper is imported from S10).
- **E11-D02** — chassis hi-fi design.
- Blocks **E11-S07** (crosshair axis labels), **E11-T08** (golden-image harness uses axes as its primary fixtures).

title: Show a synced crosshair with an OHLCV readout and a bar-close countdown
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-008` (Must) — *"I want a crosshair with a precise data readout and a bar-close countdown, so that I always know exactly what I am looking at"* — with the NFR **"readout updates within one frame; live-region announcements throttled to <=2/s to avoid screen-reader flooding"**.

Three catalogue components carry the contract. **CMP-190 Crosshair**: synced across all panes and linked charts, props `position`, `syncGroupId`, and the binding a11y rule that "keyboard-driven crosshair movement is the accessible path — mouse-hover crosshair is the pointer-only convenience layer". **CMP-197 ChartTooltip**: the floating readout, explicitly `aria-hidden` because the same information is always available through the DOM mirror, preventing duplicate announcement. **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: text, never a bare progress ring, 1 Hz updates, `aria-live="off"` by default, and the warn state "adds a word, not just a colour".

The readout must include the values of visible indicators (`US-CHART-008` first scenario), so it is built as a composable field list that E13 extends rather than a fixed OHLCV struct.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/overlays/Crosshair.ts` (**CMP-190**): vertical + horizontal lines drawn in the `foreground` layer, snapping to bar centre horizontally, free or snapped vertically per magnet mode, plus price and time labels drawn on the respective axes.
- **Magnet modes**: `off` (free), `weak` (snap to the nearest OHLC value within 8 px), `strong` (always snap to the nearest OHLC value) — mode is a chart option and is announced when changed.
- `ChartEvents["crosshair"]` payload `{ time, price, barIndex, cell? }` emitted **edge-triggered** (only when the resolved bar/price cell changes), never per pointer-move.
- Readout field model: an ordered list of `{ label, value, unit, colorToken }` produced by asking each visible series/overlay for its value at the focused bar — OHLCV and delta from the bar store in this Epic, indicator values appended by E13 through the same interface.
- **CMP-197 ChartTooltip** in `apps/web`: DOM-rendered (crisp text, and it can carry real markup), positioned to avoid the pointer and to flip at viewport edges, `aria-hidden="true"`.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: seconds to bar close for time-based intervals, updating at 1 Hz, turning amber **and adding the word "closing"** in the final 10 s (`US-CHART-008` second scenario + the component's "adds a word, not just a colour" rule). Hidden for non-time bar types with an explanatory title.
- **Keyboard crosshair**: `<-/->` step the data cursor by a bar, `Up/Down` step by price level, `Shift+<-/->` by 10 bars; the readout for the focused bar is announced through the throttled polite live region.
- Sync-group broadcast: the crosshair position is published once per frame to the pane's sync group (consumed by E11-S09).

## Out of scope
- The sync-group *mechanism* and cross-chart linking — E11-S09 (this story publishes and subscribes; S09 owns group membership and propagation).
- Footprint-cell tooltips and per-cell values — E18 (the `cell?` field of the crosshair payload is defined here and populated there).
- Indicator value fields — E13 supplies them through the field interface defined here.
- The full DOM-mirror structure and the data-table alternative — E11-S13 / E11-S14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The readout is precise and complete
  Given the crosshair moves over a bar that has an indicator drawn on its pane
  When the readout renders
  Then it shows open, high, low, close, volume, delta, the bar time in the active timezone, and each visible indicator's value at that bar
  And the values match the DataModel exactly, not an interpolation between bars

Scenario: The countdown warns with a word, not only a colour
  Given a 1-minute interval with 8 seconds to bar close
  When the countdown renders
  Then it shows the remaining seconds with an amber token and the word "closing"
  And a colour-blind simulation of the frame still conveys the warning

Scenario: The keyboard crosshair announces without flooding
  Given the chart pane has focus
  When the user holds -> so that 30 bars are traversed in 3 seconds
  Then the crosshair steps bar by bar and the visual readout updates every frame
  And the live region announces at most 6 times, each carrying the latest bar's summary

Scenario: The tooltip does not double-announce
  Given a screen reader is active and the pointer hovers a bar
  When the tooltip appears
  Then it is aria-hidden and is not announced
  And the same values are reachable through the DOM mirror for the focused bar

Scenario: Crosshair events are edge-triggered
  Given the pointer moves 200 px within one bar's width
  When crosshair events are counted
  Then exactly one crosshair event is emitted for that bar
  And the vertical price component still updates the readout each frame without emitting an event

Scenario: Magnet mode snaps predictably
  Given magnet mode is "strong" and the pointer is 12 px from the bar's high
  When the crosshair resolves
  Then it snaps to the high and the readout labels the snapped value as "High"
```

## Technical notes / design
Edge-triggering is a message-traffic rule from §6 ("pick results posted only when the picked object changes") and applies to crosshair resolution too: the worker resolves `(barIndex, priceLevel)` every frame but posts only on change. The *visual* crosshair still follows the pointer at full frame rate inside the worker — the throttle is on the message, not the rendering.

Bar-centre snapping uses `screenToIndex` (O(1), E11-S03), then re-projects the bar centre with `indexToScreen` so the line lands exactly on the centre rather than under the raw pointer x.

Countdown maths: `msRemaining = barCloseTime - serverNow`, where `serverNow` is the WS-clock-corrected time (offset supplied by the app layer from E17's heartbeat) — using the local clock makes the countdown wrong by the client's clock skew, which traders notice immediately. Below 10 s the component re-renders at 1 Hz still, not faster; sub-second precision is not useful and costs a re-render per frame.

The readout field list is rebuilt only when the focused bar changes or a visible series changes — not per frame — and is a pooled array to keep the hot path allocation-free.

Tooltip positioning: offset 12 px from the pointer in the quadrant with the most space, flipped at pane edges, and clamped inside the chart container; it never covers the last-price label (SCR-030's "labels must never obscure the last price" rule).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: bar-centre snapping across bar spacings; magnet resolution for each mode at boundary distances; countdown formatting and warn threshold; clock-skew correction; edge-trigger logic; field-list assembly with 0/1/3 indicators.
- **Golden image**: crosshair + labels at DPR 1/2, both themes; tooltip at all four edge-flip positions; countdown normal/warning/closed.
- **Interaction/E2E**: pointer crosshair, keyboard crosshair including `Shift` multiples, magnet mode switching, tooltip flip at edges, countdown reaching zero and rolling to the next bar.
- **A11y**: live-region announcement assertions (content and <=2/s cadence); `aria-hidden` verified on the tooltip (axe rule); countdown default `aria-live="off"`; contrast of crosshair lines against both themes.
- **Perf**: readout update within one frame (`US-CHART-008` NFR); CMP-197's catalogue test "performance (update cost during rapid crosshair movement)" — <=0.3 ms/frame during a 1000 px/s pointer sweep.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
This story is one of the two places (with E11-S13) where the chart's accessibility is actually decided.
- **Keyboard is the primary path**, per CMP-190: mouse hover is the convenience layer. Everything reachable by hover is reachable by `<-/->/Up/Down` with the same fidelity.
- **Announcement throttling** at <=2/s with latest-value semantics (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 and the `US-CHART-008` NFR) — the region is pre-rendered and only its text content is swapped, never the node.
- **Tooltip is `aria-hidden`** (CMP-197) so the mirror is the single announcement source; axe asserts it.
- **Countdown** (CMP-226) is text, `aria-live="off"` by default with opt-in announcement, and its warn state adds the word "closing".
- Crosshair lines meet the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement against both themes; the readout never relies on colour alone to distinguish up/down (sign is text).
- Design source: **E11-D02**; a11y review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
`US-CHART-008` NFR: readout updates within one frame. Crosshair rendering is 2 lines + 2 DOM labels = 1 GL draw call (§4 table). The tooltip is DOM, so its cost is main-thread layout — it is positioned via `transform` only (no layout-triggering property writes) to stay off the critical path. Contributes to the <=1 ms overlay stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.

## Observability
`a11y` worker->main message carrying `cursorSummary` (the text the live region announces). Counters: `engine.crosshair.events_emitted`, `engine.crosshair.announcements`, `engine.countdown.clock_skew_ms`. A persistent large skew is surfaced in SCR-046 because it usually indicates a WS heartbeat problem, not a chart problem.

- **E17** (via the app layer) — server-clock offset for the countdown.

title: Pick chart objects in under 1 ms via structural and uniform-grid indices
body:
## Context
Hard requirement **R5** in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1: "200 drawings + 50 order/position lines with hit-testing in <=1 ms". Everything interactive in the product depends on it — selecting a drawing (E14), dragging an order line (E31), hovering a footprint cell (E18), clicking a ladder row (E21) — and it runs inside the input stage of the frame, which has <=1 ms total (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3).

§3.9 specifies two complementary indices maintained incrementally in the worker: a **structural index** exploiting the fact that the chart is a regular grid (bar index and price level computed analytically in O(1)), and an **object index**, a uniform 64 px grid over drawings, order lines, position lines, alert lines and bubbles. The budget is met by never doing a linear scan over objects.

This story builds both indices and the picking pipeline. The objects that populate the object index arrive with later epics; the index and its contract ship now so those epics register rather than invent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/hit/StructuralIndex.ts`: `screenToIndex`/`screenToPrice` from E11-S03 wrapped into `pickStructural(pt) -> { barIndex, priceLevel, paneId }` in O(1). Covers crosshair, footprint-cell hover, ladder rows and profile rows.
- `src/hit/ObjectIndex.ts`: uniform grid of 64 px buckets storing object ids, maintained **incrementally** — an object insert/move/remove touches only the buckets it spans, never a rebuild.
- Query algorithm per §3.9: take the bucket under the cursor plus a 1-bucket ring, test candidates precisely (distance-to-segment for lines, rect containment for boxes, radius for bubbles), sort by `zIndex` then proximity, return the front-most.
- Tolerances: grab handles use an enlarged **10 px** tolerance; **touch input uses 16 px** (§3.9) — resolved from the pointer type, not hard-coded to mouse.
- `pickAt` command (worker inbound, §6) for explicit picks, plus continuous hover picking that posts `pick` messages **edge-triggered** when the picked object changes.
- Registration API for later epics: `registerPickable({ id, kind, bounds, zIndex, paneId, hitTest })` with `kind  in  'drawing'|'order-line'|'position-line'|'alert-line'|'bubble'|'cell'|'axis'`, and an `indexShift` subscriber so a `prepend` (E11-T03) rebases bar-anchored bounds.
- Invalidation: a viewport change marks the object index `TRANSFORM`-dirty and bounds are re-projected lazily on the next query, not eagerly on every pan frame.

## Out of scope
- The drawings, order lines, bubbles and cells themselves — E14, E31, E22, E18, E21. This story ships the index and the contract they register through.
- Drag/resize behaviour after a pick — E14/E31 own the interaction; this story returns what was picked.
- Multi-select and marquee selection — E14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Picking meets the hard budget at the specified density
  Given a pane with 200 drawings and 50 order/position lines
  When 1 000 picks at random screen positions are timed
  Then the p95 pick time is at most 1 ms (requirement R5, benchmark B8)
  And no pick performs a linear scan over all registered objects

Scenario: The front-most object wins
  Given three overlapping drawings at the cursor with zIndex 1, 5 and 3
  When a pick is performed
  Then the drawing with zIndex 5 is returned
  And when two objects share a zIndex, the closer one by distance is returned

Scenario: Touch gets a larger tolerance than mouse
  Given an order line 13 px from the pointer position
  When the pointer type is touch
  Then the line is picked (16 px tolerance)
  And when the pointer type is mouse, nothing is picked (10 px handle tolerance)

Scenario: Pick messages are edge-triggered
  Given the pointer moves 300 px while staying over the same drawing
  When pick messages are counted
  Then exactly one pick message is posted for that drawing
  And one further message is posted when the pointer leaves it

Scenario: A history prepend does not misplace objects
  Given a drawing anchored at barIndex 120 and 2 000 bars are prepended
  When the drawing is picked after the splice
  Then it is found at its unchanged time/price anchor
  And the object index reports no stale bucket entries

Scenario: Panning does not rebuild the index
  Given 250 registered objects
  When the chart is panned continuously for 5 s
  Then no full index rebuild occurs and bucket membership is recomputed lazily per query
  And picking remains within budget throughout
```

## Technical notes / design
Bucket size 64 px is from §3.9 and is a deliberate trade: small enough that a bucket rarely holds more than a handful of objects, large enough that a long trend line spans few buckets. Long lines are stored in every bucket their bounding segment crosses (a DDA walk), not in a bounding-box fill, so a diagonal line across the pane costs O(cells along the line), not O(w×h cells).

Precise tests: distance-to-segment (with the segment's `width/2 + tolerance` as the threshold) for lines and rays; rect containment with an edge band for boxes so both the fill and the border are pickable; radius for bubbles; analytic grid maths for cells.

Anchors are stored in **world space** (time + price) and projected lazily on query using the current viewport, so a pan never invalidates stored geometry — only the cached screen-space bounds, which are recomputed per query batch (once per frame at most).

Handle picking takes priority over body picking: when a pointer is within 10 px of a control point *and* inside the object body, the handle is returned, because dragging a handle is the more specific intent.

Determinism: ties in both `zIndex` and distance are broken by registration order, so pick results are reproducible in tests (§14 determinism aids).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: bucket assignment for horizontal/vertical/diagonal segments; DDA walk correctness; distance-to-segment against hand-computed cases; tolerance resolution by pointer type; zIndex/proximity/registration-order tie-breaking; `indexShift` rebasing.
- **Property** (fast-check, 10 000 cases): for random object sets and random query points, the grid query returns exactly the same object as a brute-force linear scan — this is the test that makes the optimisation safe.
- **Perf**: B8 (200 drawings, drag one, p95 frame <=12 ms, **pick <=1 ms**); a dedicated micro-benchmark at 1 000 objects to show the margin.
- **Integration**: pick -> `pick` message -> main-thread selection state, edge-trigger counting.
- Coverage >=90 % (pure geometry).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
Picking is the **pointer** path; the keyboard path is focus traversal of the DOM mirror (E11-S13), and the two must agree — an object that can be picked must be focusable in the mirror, and the mirror node's bounding box must match the pickable bounds so that pointer and keyboard users select the same thing. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires the surrogate to be "sized to match the visual target for pointer users using it too"; this story exposes the projected bounds that make that alignment possible, and a test asserts mirror-node rects match pickable bounds within 1 px.

Target size: the 10 px (mouse) / 16 px (touch) tolerances are what let small chart objects satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) via the spacing exception; the tolerance values are therefore an a11y control, not only an ergonomic one.

## Performance notes
Hard requirement R5 (<=1 ms for 200 drawings + 50 lines) and the <=1 ms input stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3. Benchmark B8 gates it. Edge-triggered messaging keeps worker->main traffic low, protecting the main thread for the DOM mirror and React.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.pick.duration_us` (histogram), `engine.pick.candidates_tested`, `engine.pick.index_rebuilds`, `engine.pick.objects_registered{kind}`. A rising `candidates_tested` is the early signal that bucket sizing needs revisiting; it is shown in SCR-046's detail view.

- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies

- Blocks **E11-S13** (mirror/pick alignment), **E14** (drawings), **E31** (order-line dragging), **E18**/**E21**/**E22** (cell, ladder and bubble picking).
