title: Stack panes on a shared time axis and sync range, crosshair and levels
body:
## Context
Multi-pane is structural, not cosmetic: the volume sub-pane of `US-CHART-002`, the CVD/OI/funding panes of R2 (E23/E24) and the indicator panes of E13 are all `Pane` instances stacked under one shared time axis. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1 fixes the tree and §3.5 fixes the rule that makes it coherent: **"panes in one chart share `timeStart/timeEnd` by construction"**, while charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, "propagated once per frame after input integration (never re-entrantly)".

**CMP-196 MultiChartLinker** is the non-visual coordinator for that: props `groupId`, `linkedPanes`, `syncModes {crosshair, levels, scale}`, with the a11y requirement that sync-state changes are "announced once via a shared status region (*Panes linked: crosshair, levels*)".

The re-entrancy rule is the trap. A naive implementation where pane A's crosshair sets pane B's, which broadcasts back to A, produces either an infinite loop or a one-frame oscillation that looks like jitter. The design forbids it explicitly; this story implements the forbidding.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Pane stacking in the layout engine: N panes in one chart, vertical order fixed by insertion, per-pane `heightRatio` (`Pane.setHeightRatio`, §8) normalised so ratios always sum to 1, with a minimum pane height below which a pane collapses to a labelled stub rather than rendering illegibly.
- Drag-to-resize splitters between panes, with a **keyboard equivalent** (focus the splitter, `Up/Down` adjust by 2 % steps, `Home` restores equal ratios) — required by the no-drag-only rule.
- Shared time axis: one `TimeAxis` per chart (CMP-189's "master clock" role), rendered once in the bottom gutter; every pane's x-mapping derives from it by construction, so time can never drift between panes.
- Per-pane price scales that are independent by default, with an opt-in "link scale" per sync mode.
- `src/sync/SyncGroup.ts` (**CMP-196**): group registry keyed by `groupId`, membership add/remove, and per-mode propagation of `timeRange`, `crosshair` and `level`.
- **Single-phase propagation**: input is integrated, then the group publishes once per frame; subscribers apply without re-publishing (an `origin` token on the sync message suppresses echo). Re-entrant propagation is impossible by construction, and a test asserts it.
- Sync-state status region: joining/leaving a group or changing modes announces once ("Panes linked: crosshair, levels") through a shared polite status region.
- `sync` message wiring (main->worker, §6) so multiple chart instances sharing the worker propagate without a main-thread round-trip.

## Out of scope
- Grid **layouts** (1/2/3/4/6 charts), workspace save/load, and the colour-coded sync-group UI — E15 (`US-LAY-*`). This story ships the engine mechanism and the API E15 drives.
- The multi-chart grid panel screen **SCR-049** — E15.
- Indicator panes and their placement rules — E13.
- Symbol propagation across linked charts — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Panes in one chart cannot drift in time
  Given a three-pane chart (price, volume, CVD)
  When the chart is panned and zoomed for 10 s
  Then all three panes show the identical time range on every frame, asserted from frame stats, not visually
  And only one TimeAxis is rendered, in the bottom gutter

Scenario: Sync propagates once per frame with no echo
  Given two charts in sync group "A" with crosshair sync enabled
  When the crosshair moves in chart 1
  Then chart 2's crosshair updates on the same frame
  And chart 1 receives no inbound sync message originating from its own broadcast
  And instrumentation shows exactly one propagation per frame

Scenario: Splitters are operable without a mouse
  Given the splitter between the price and volume panes has focus
  When the user presses Down three times and then Home
  Then the price pane shrinks by 6 % in three steps and Home restores equal ratios
  And each change is announced once, not per frame

Scenario: A pane too small to read collapses honestly
  Given a pane is dragged below its minimum height
  When it renders
  Then it collapses to a labelled stub naming the pane and offering restore
  And it does not render a squashed, illegible chart

Scenario: Sync state is announced once
  Given the user enables level sync for a group of three panes
  When the change applies
  Then a single polite announcement says "Panes linked: crosshair, levels"
  And no further announcement occurs while the state is unchanged

Scenario: Four synced charts stay within budget
  Given four synchronised charts with benchmark B5 content at half density
  When B6 runs
  Then the aggregate p95 frame time is at most 16.7 ms and shared-worker CPU is at most 70 % of one core
```

## Technical notes / design
Propagation order inside the frame (§3.5): integrate input -> apply local viewport/crosshair changes -> **publish** to the group -> subscribers apply with `applyingSync = true` -> collect/render. Subscribers set a flag that suppresses publication for that frame; the `origin` token is belt-and-braces for cross-worker cases.

Height ratios are normalised on every mutation so floating-point drift cannot make panes sum to 0.999 and leave a gap. The minimum pane height is `max(48 px, 3 × axis label height)` — below that, axis labels cannot be drawn and the pane is meaningless.

Level sync ("drawing a level on one pane reflects on linked panes", CMP-196) propagates the *price* only; it deliberately does not propagate the drawing object, because linked charts may be different symbols where the same price means something different. Cross-symbol level sync is off by default and flagged in the UI (E15's concern).

The shared time axis derives each pane's x-mapping from one `Viewport.time` instance; panes hold only their own price mapping. There is no per-pane time state that could diverge — this is "shared by construction" rather than "kept in sync".

Sync groups are identified by string ids created by the app (E15 assigns colours to them); the engine never invents or persists a group id.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ratio normalisation and minimum-height collapse; splitter keyboard steps; group membership add/remove/dispose; echo suppression (a subscriber applying a sync must not publish); propagation ordering with `TestClock`.
- **Integration** (CMP-196's catalogue requirement): sync propagation across 2–4 panes and across 2 chart instances, asserting same-frame application and exactly-once propagation.
- **Golden image**: 2-, 3- and 4-pane stacks with correct gutters and a single time axis; collapsed-stub state.
- **Interaction/E2E**: splitter drag and keyboard resize; enabling/disabling each sync mode; announcement fired once.
- **Perf**: B6 (4 synchronised charts — aggregate p95 <=16.7 ms, shared-worker CPU <=70 % of one core). This is also the test that proves the "one rAF per page" rule from E11-S01 holds.
- **A11y**: axe-core on a multi-pane chart; splitter has `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` and an accessible name; status region announces once.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` and a name identifying the panes they divide; keyboard resize is mandatory (drag-only is forbidden by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6).
- Each pane is an `aria-label`led region so a screen-reader user can tell which pane the data cursor is in; moving the cursor between panes announces the pane name once.
- Sync-state changes announce **once** through a shared polite status region (CMP-196's contract) — not per frame and not per pane.
- Collapsed stubs carry a text label and a keyboard-operable restore control; a collapsed pane is never a silent disappearance.
- Design source: **E11-D02** (pane chrome, splitters, collapsed state).

## Performance notes
Budget #1 with the B6 worst case as the gate, and the §4.4 degradation rule that under the stress scenario background panes may be capped to candles+profile with an explicit, **non-colour-only** "reduced live detail" indicator. This story implements the focused/background pane distinction the ladder needs; the shedding policy itself is E11-S12. Draw-call target <=40 for a 3-pane chart (§4).

## Observability
Counters: `engine.sync.propagations_per_frame` (must be <=1 per group — an alerting condition if exceeded), `engine.sync.group_members`, `engine.panes.collapsed`. Frame stats are reported per chart instance so B6 attribution is per-chart, not aggregate-only.

- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

- **E11-T02** — the `sync` message.
- Blocks **E15** (layouts/workspaces drive these APIs), **E13** (indicator panes), **E23**/**E24** (CVD/derivatives panes).

title: Render device-pixel-correct at any DPI and survive resize and monitor changes
body:
## Context
A trading chart is judged on hairlines. If the backing store is not sized at `devicePixelRatio` and coordinates are not snapped to the device-pixel grid, gridlines shimmer, axis text blurs and a 1 px crosshair becomes a 2 px smear — precisely the "boring parity" work `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 warns must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

The reference machine runs **2560×1440 at 125 % scaling**, so a fractional DPR (1.25) is the *default* case, not an edge case. Owners commonly drag a window between a laptop panel and an external monitor, which changes DPR mid-session with no reload.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backing store sized `cssPx * dpr`, canvas CSS size left to layout; all engine math in CSS pixels with a single `dpr` uniform applied at the vertex stage.
- **DPR cap for the heatmap layer at 2** per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4 — a 3× DPR display must not triple heatmap texture memory for no perceptual gain.
- Hairline snapping helper: `snapHairline(vCssPx, dpr)` -> aligns 1-device-pixel strokes to the half-pixel grid so gridlines, axis rules and the crosshair are crisp at any DPR.
- `ResizeObserver` on the container, debounced to one frame, forwarded as the `resize` message (E11-T02) with `{ width, height, dpr }`.
- DPR-change detection via a `(resolution: <dpr>dppx)` media query re-armed after each change (the reliable cross-browser idiom), triggering re-size plus **SDF atlas size-class re-selection** (E11-S11).
- Zero-size and hidden-container handling: a `0×0` or `display:none` container suspends the render loop instead of throwing or allocating a degenerate framebuffer.
- Framebuffer reallocation policy: grow in 128 px steps and never shrink during an interactive drag, to avoid reallocation storms while a user drags a splitter.

## Out of scope
- Pane layout and splitters — E11-S09.
- Printing/export rasterisation — E15 (screenshot export).
- The axis label typography itself — E11-S06/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hairlines are crisp at fractional DPI
  Given the chart is rendered at devicePixelRatio 1.25
  When gridlines, the axis rule and the crosshair are drawn
  Then each is exactly one device pixel wide with no anti-aliased fringe
  And the golden image matches the reference at <= 0.1 % pixel difference

Scenario: Moving to a different-DPI monitor re-renders correctly
  Given a chart rendered on a 1x display
  When the window is moved to a 2x display and devicePixelRatio changes to 2
  Then the backing store is resized, the SDF atlas size class is re-selected
  And the next frame is sharp with no stretched or stale texture

Scenario: Heatmap layer is capped at 2x
  Given a display reporting devicePixelRatio 3
  When the heatmap layer allocates its textures
  Then it allocates at an effective ratio of 2 while other layers use 3
  And heatmap texture memory stays within its 20 MB secondary gate

Scenario: A zero-size container does not crash or burn CPU
  Given the chart container is resized to 0x0 or hidden with display:none
  When a frame would be scheduled
  Then the render loop suspends and allocates nothing
  And it resumes with a correct frame within one frame of the container regaining size

Scenario: Dragging a splitter does not cause reallocation storms
  Given the user drags a pane splitter continuously for 2 seconds
  When framebuffers are inspected
  Then reallocation occurs at most once per 128 px growth step and never shrinks mid-drag
  And p95 frame time during the drag stays within budget #1
```

## Technical notes / design
Transform: world -> CSS px (E11-S03) -> device px by `* dpr` in the vertex shader, so all JS-side hit-testing, layout and drawing math stays in CSS pixels and there is exactly one place DPR is applied.

```ts
// half-pixel alignment: a 1-device-px line centred on a device-pixel boundary blurs;
// centred on a device-pixel *centre* it is crisp.
const snapHairline = (vCssPx: number, dpr: number): number =>
  (Math.round(vCssPx * dpr - 0.5) + 0.5) / dpr;
```

DPR-change detection must re-arm after every change because the media query is DPR-specific:

```ts
function onDprChange(cb: (dpr: number) => void): () => void {
  let mq: MediaQueryList;
  const arm = () => {
    mq = matchMedia(`(resolution: ${devicePixelRatio}dppx)`);
    mq.addEventListener("change", handle, { once: true });
  };
  const handle = () => { cb(devicePixelRatio); arm(); };
  arm();
  return () => mq.removeEventListener("change", handle);
}
```

Resize is debounced to exactly one frame (not a timer) so a drag produces one resize per frame, matching the <=1 message/frame rule of the worker protocol.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: `snapHairline` across dpr  in  {1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3} with property tests asserting the result always lands on a device-pixel centre; framebuffer growth-step policy; zero-size suspension and resumption; DPR listener re-arm (asserting the listener is re-registered after each change).
- **Golden image** (E11-T08, SwiftShader): grid + axes + crosshair at dpr 1, 1.25, 2; heatmap-cap verification at dpr 3.
- **Integration**: simulated DPR change mid-session asserting atlas re-selection and a sharp next frame.
- **Perf**: splitter-drag scenario asserting <=1 reallocation per 128 px and in-budget p95.
- **Chaos**: container hidden/shown repeatedly (E11-Q04 charter) asserting no leak and no exception.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- Crisp hairlines and text are a **low-vision requirement**, not a polish item: blurred 1 px rules at fractional DPI are the single most common legibility complaint on high-DPI Windows setups.
- Browser zoom up to 200 % (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.4) manifests as a DPR/size change and must be handled by the same path — verified in E11-Q05.
- Resizing must not move keyboard focus or reset the data cursor position (E11-S13); the cursor is expressed in world coordinates, not pixels, specifically so this holds.

## Performance notes
Resize and DPR changes are rare events, but a reallocation storm during a drag is a realistic budget #1 violation, hence the growth-step policy and its explicit test. The heatmap DPR cap directly protects budget #14's texture-memory secondary gate (<=20 MB, `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 B4).

## Observability
`frame` stats carry `dpr` and `backingStorePx` so any perf report is attributable to a resolution. Counter `engine.resize.reallocations` and event `engine.dpr.changed` (from -> to) logged at info level.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

title: Render all chart text from an SDF glyph atlas with instanced, batched draws
body:
## Context
Footprint cells are the densest text surface in the product — 2,500 visible cells with two numbers each, roughly **12,500 glyphs per frame** — and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7 therefore makes text a first-class engine subsystem rather than a convenience. Canvas 2D `fillText` cannot reach that density at 60 fps, and per-glyph textured quads blow the draw-call budget.

The answer is a signed-distance-field atlas: glyphs are rasterised once from the design-system font, converted to an 8-bit SDF, packed into a 1024×1024 atlas and drawn as a **single instanced draw call per batch**, crisp at any scale with an optional outline pass that keeps numbers legible over saturated cell fills.

E11-K01 closes open item **O2** (exact glyph set and atlas size for the chosen design-system font) and hands this Story a measured, fixed answer rather than a guess.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/text/SdfGenerator.ts` — rasterise the glyph set to an offscreen 2D canvas, then a **two-pass Felzenszwalb EDT** to produce the signed distance field; 8-bit single channel.
- `src/text/ShelfPacker.ts` — shelf packing into a 1024×1024 atlas (size confirmed by E11-K01), emitting a `uvRect` per glyph plus per-glyph metrics (advance, bearing, size).
- Glyph set per §3.7: digits, `.` `,` `-` `+` `%` `×` `K` `M` `B`, and `A`–`Z` / `a`–`z` for labels — the exact final set is E11-K01's output.
- **IndexedDB cache** keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, sizeClass, hash(glyphSet))`; generation costs ~40 ms once, cached launches are instant (benchmark **B9** gates "SDF atlas from cache <=5 ms").
- `src/text/TextBatcher.ts` — instanced rendering with per-instance attributes `vec2 posPx`, `vec2 sizePx`, `vec4 uvRect`, `vec4 colour`; one draw call per batch.
- Fragment shader: `alpha = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, sdf)` with `w = fwidth(sdf)`; optional **outline variant** at a second threshold for legibility over saturated fills.
- **Pre-computed glyph runs**: numbers are formatted on data update and cached as offsets into the atlas — never formatted per frame. A format change (e.g. compact `1.2K`) invalidates only the run cache.
- Batch budget: all cell text in a pane is one draw call, axis labels a second, drawing labels a third; **target <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame**.
- `degraded-2d` fallback path: Canvas 2D `fillText`, with footprint limited to L2/L3 (implemented in E11-T05, seam provided here).

## Out of scope
- The footprint cell renderer itself and its number semantics — **E18**. This Story ships the text machinery those cells draw with.
- Rich text, bidirectional text, CJK or emoji — the glyph set is Latin + symbols by design; a future non-Latin need is a new spike, not a silent widening.
- DOM tooltips and legends (CMP-197, CMP-199) — those are real DOM and use real fonts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dense cell text renders within its measured budget
  Given a pane containing 2,500 footprint-style cells with two numbers each (~12,500 glyphs)
  When a frame is rendered
  Then all cell text is emitted in a single instanced draw call
  And CPU batching costs <= 2.0 ms total, meeting the B3 secondary gate

Scenario: Text stays crisp at every scale
  Given the same label is rendered at font size class 0, 1 and 2 and at devicePixelRatio 1, 1.25 and 2
  When the golden images are compared with the reference
  Then each differs by <= 0.1 % of pixels with no visible blur or aliasing fringe

Scenario: Atlas generation is cached across launches
  Given the atlas for the design-system font has been generated once
  When the application is relaunched
  Then the atlas is restored from IndexedDB in <= 5 ms
  And benchmark B9 cold-init-to-first-frame stays <= 900 ms

Scenario: Numbers stay legible over saturated fills
  Given a cell filled with the most saturated colour in the delta ramp
  When its numbers are drawn with the outline variant
  Then the text meets a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against that fill
  And the check is automated over every LUT endpoint, not spot-checked

Scenario: A corrupt cached atlas is detected and regenerated
  Given the IndexedDB-cached atlas fails its stored checksum
  When the engine initialises
  Then the cache entry is discarded and the atlas is regenerated from the font
  And ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID is logged once, with no visible text corruption

Scenario: Formatting is not per-frame work
  Given a static viewport of formatted cells
  When 60 consecutive frames are rendered
  Then zero number-to-string formatting calls occur in the frame path
  And the allocation counter reports zero allocations in that path
```

## Technical notes / design
**EDT.** Felzenszwalb's exact Euclidean distance transform is O(n) per row/column: run it over the inside set and the outside set, subtract, normalise to `[0,255]` with a spread of 4 px (the spread is what allows the outline pass; it is a stored atlas property, not a magic number in the shader).

**Shader** (fragment, single channel atlas):

```glsl
float d = texture(uAtlas, vUv).r;
float w = fwidth(d);
float a = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, d);
// outline variant: a second, wider threshold composited underneath
float ao = smoothstep(0.5 - uOutline - w, 0.5 - uOutline + w, d);
outColor = mix(vec4(uOutlineColor.rgb, ao * uOutlineColor.a), vColor, a);
```

**Glyph runs.** A run is `{ atlasIds: Uint16Array, advances: Float32Array }` computed when the underlying value changes. The frame path walks runs and writes instance attributes into a pre-allocated `Float32Array` — no string work, no allocation.

**Cache integrity.** The IndexedDB record stores `{ atlasBytes, metrics, checksum }` where `checksum` is a FNV-1a hash of `atlasBytes`; a mismatch (corruption, a partially-written record, a tampered origin store) discards the entry and regenerates. This is also the Tampering control named in the STRIDE model (E11-X01).

**Size classes.** Three classes (small/medium/large) matched to the density modes of E11-T04; a DPR change (E11-S10) re-selects the class, which may trigger a regeneration — hence the cache key includes `sizeClass`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: EDT correctness against a brute-force reference on small bitmaps; shelf packer produces non-overlapping rects and reports occupancy; glyph-run construction and invalidation on format change; cache key derivation; checksum rejection.
- **Property** (fast-check): for random strings from the glyph set, run advances sum to the measured string width within 0.5 px.
- **Golden image**: every glyph at each size class, at dpr 1/1.25/2, plus the outline variant over the LUT endpoints.
- **Contrast test**: automated over all LUT endpoint fills with the outline variant, asserting >=4.5:1.
- **Perf**: B3's text sub-gate (batching <=2.0 ms, <=2 text draw calls) and B9's cached-atlas <=5 ms.
- **Allocation**: zero allocations and zero `toFixed`/template-literal calls in the frame path over 60 frames.
- **Robustness**: corrupt cache entry; IndexedDB unavailable (private mode) must fall back to in-memory generation, never fail the chart.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**; the atlas contains rendered glyph shapes, no user content.

Residual STRIDE surface (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — the SDF atlas is cached in IndexedDB, which is same-origin-writable, so a poisoned entry could in principle render misleading numbers (a "9" drawn as a "0" is a *trading-relevant* integrity failure, not a cosmetic one). Control: the stored checksum is verified before use and any mismatch forces regeneration from the font. **Denial of service** — atlas generation is bounded by a fixed glyph set and a fixed 1024×1024 atlas, so no input can make it allocate unboundedly.

No `eval`, no dynamic shader source: the shader is a compile-time string constant and glyph data only ever becomes texture bytes and numeric attributes. `security` label applies (cache integrity), reviewed under E11-X03.

## Accessibility notes
- Text crispness is a direct **low-vision** requirement; SDF rendering is what makes the smallest legible size class actually legible.
- The **outline variant exists for contrast**, not decoration: it is the mechanism by which numbers over saturated delta fills meet 4.5:1, and the automated contrast test above is the proof.
- Text rendered into the canvas is invisible to assistive technology by construction — every number drawn here must also exist in the DOM mirror (E11-S13) and the SCR-045 table (E11-S14). This Story does not create an accessible surface; it must not be mistaken for one.
- Minimum legible cell-text height (>=11 px per §3.6) is the threshold at which E11-S12 degrades footprint text to colour-only, and it is defined here.

## Performance notes
Gate **B3** text sub-budget: <=2.0 ms CPU batching and <=2 text draw calls for the 12,500-glyph case; measured ~0.9 ms CPU / ~0.4 ms GPU on the reference machine, so the gate has headroom by design. Gate **B9**: cached atlas <=5 ms within a <=900 ms cold-init budget. Atlas memory 1024×1024×1 B = **1.0 MB** of the ~116 MB per-instance model (§7). Target <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.text.glyphs_per_frame`, `engine.text.draw_calls`, `engine.text.batch_ms`, `engine.atlas.occupancy_pct`, `engine.atlas.cache_hit`. Errors: `ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID`, `ENGINE_ATLAS_GENERATION_FAILED` (the latter falls back to `degraded-2d` text rather than failing the chart). Atlas generation time logged once per launch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-K01** — closes open item O2: the exact glyph set and atlas size for the design-system font. Without it this Story would guess at the atlas budget.
- **E11-S03** — the transform that positions text in world space.
- **E11-S10** — DPR/size-class re-selection.
- **E05** — the design-system font choice and type scale that fix the glyph set and the three size classes. (Runtime theme/density switching arrives with **E11-T04** in Sprint 06; this Story reads the font metrics directly, so it does not wait on it.)
- Blocks **E11-S06** (axis labels), **E18** (footprint cell text), **E19**/**E21** (profile and heatmap labels).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-sdf-text` · 2 PRs (generator + packer + cache; batcher + shaders), each <=400 LOC; generated atlas binaries excluded from the LOC count but reviewed by the code owner.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`

title: Select LOD with hysteresis and decimate candles without losing spikes
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-001` requires that at 100,000 bars zoomed to fit, "rendering stays at or above 55 fps using level-of-detail aggregation, **and the aggregation level is indicated**". That last clause is the honesty requirement: a trader must never be shown a decimated chart that silently pretends to be the full one.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 makes the correctness rule explicit: candle decimation at L2 is **min/max preserving** — per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close — "so spikes never disappear — a correctness requirement, not a cosmetic one". A naive stride-sample would drop the exact wick that a stop sat behind.

This Story also owns the **degradation ladder** of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4: when frames go over budget, the engine steps down detail deliberately and visibly, rather than dropping frames randomly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/lod/LodSelector.ts` — the candle ladder of §3.6: `barSpacing >= 3 px` -> **L0** (full OHLC bodies + wicks); `>= 1.5 px` -> **L1** (bodies only); else **L2** (min/max column strip, one column per pixel).
- **±15 % hysteresis dead band** on every threshold so slow zooming cannot flicker between levels (gate **B2**: <=6 LOD changes over the full 0.1->50 px/bar zoom sweep).
- `src/lod/Decimator.ts` — min/max-preserving reduction producing `(minLow, maxHigh, firstOpen, lastClose)` per pixel column, computed incrementally against the columnar stores of E11-T03.
- Extension seams (thresholds registered, implementations owned elsewhere): footprint L0–L3, profile row merging below 2 px, bubble clustering <=500 instances, heatmap column aggregation; drawings are **never** decimated.
- **Automatic step-down** after **3 consecutive over-budget frames**, one level at a time, with a matching step-up only after sustained headroom (asymmetric, to avoid oscillation).
- The §4.4 **degradation ladder order**, applied in this sequence and no other: (1) reduce non-focused panes to candles+profile, (2) drop footprint cell text, (3) coarsen heatmap, (4) reduce bubble count — trading-critical overlays (order/position lines, SL/TP) are **never** shed.
- **Aggregation indicator**: a non-colour-only chip ("Aggregated — 12 bars per column") surfaced through the engine's state so SCR-030's "low-GPU degraded" state and the DOM mirror can both report it.
- `lodBias` from the density mode (E11-T04) folded into the thresholds.
- Manual override: `chart.setLod(level | "auto")` for diagnostics and for the benchmark harness.

## Out of scope
- Footprint/heatmap/profile decimation *implementations* — E18/E19/E21 register against the seams defined here.
- The memory-pressure step-down (a different trigger with a different policy) — E11-S15's `MemoryGovernor`, which calls into this Story's step-down API.
- Bar aggregation for a *requested interval* (1m -> 7m) — that is a bar-builder concern in E12; LOD is a purely visual reduction that never changes the underlying series.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Spikes survive decimation
  Given a 100k-bar series containing a single one-bar spike of 10x the surrounding range
  When the chart is zoomed to fit so that ~200 bars map to each pixel column
  Then the spike's high and low are both still visible in the rendered column strip
  And a property test over 10,000 random series confirms per-column min-low and max-high are always preserved

Scenario: No LOD flicker while zooming slowly
  Given the user performs the B2 wheel-zoom sweep from 0.1 to 50 px per bar
  When LOD transitions are counted
  Then at most 6 LOD changes occur across the whole sweep
  And p95 frame time stays <= 14 ms

Scenario: The aggregation level is always disclosed
  Given the chart is rendering at L2
  When the chart state is inspected
  Then an aggregation indicator reports the level and the bars-per-column ratio as text, not colour alone
  And the DOM mirror and the SCR-045 data table report the same ratio

Scenario: Over-budget frames trigger a deliberate, ordered step-down
  Given three consecutive frames exceed the 16.7 ms budget
  When the degradation ladder runs
  Then exactly one level is shed, following the 4.4 order, and ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN is logged with the reason
  And no order line, position line, SL or TP is ever shed

Scenario: Recovery is asymmetric and does not oscillate
  Given the engine has stepped down and frame times return to budget
  When headroom is sustained for 2 seconds
  Then the engine steps back up one level
  And a workload oscillating around the budget produces at most one transition per 2 seconds

Scenario: Drawings are never decimated
  Given 200 drawings are present at the most aggregate LOD
  When a frame is rendered
  Then every drawing is drawn at full fidelity
  And picking against them still completes within 1 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
**Hysteresis.** Thresholds are asymmetric by construction so the transition point differs by direction:

```ts
// stepping DOWN in detail requires crossing below t * (1 - 0.15);
// stepping UP requires crossing above t * (1 + 0.15).
const shouldDemote = (spacing: number, t: number) => spacing < t * 0.85;
const shouldPromote = (spacing: number, t: number) => spacing > t * 1.15;
```

**Decimation.** Per pixel column `c` covering bar index range `[i0, i1)`:

```
minLow(c)    = min(low[i0..i1))
maxHigh(c)   = max(high[i0..i1))
firstOpen(c) = open[i0]
lastClose(c) = close[i1-1]
```

Computed with a striding scan over the columnar `Float32Array`s (E11-T03) into a pre-allocated output buffer sized to the pane's pixel width — so the cost is O(visible bars) with **zero allocation**, and the output buffer is reused across frames. Incremental update: appending bars only dirties the trailing column.

**Step-down state machine.** `Nominal -> Degraded(1..4) -> Floor`. Trigger: 3 consecutive frames over budget. Recovery: 2 s of sustained headroom. The ladder order is data, not code branches — a frozen array of shed actions — so E18/E19/E21 register their action at the right rank and the order is reviewable in one place.

**Config keys**: `lod.mode` (`auto` | `l0` | `l1` | `l2`), `lod.hysteresisPct` (default 15), `lod.stepDownFrames` (default 3), `lod.recoveryMs` (default 2000).

## Test plan
- **Property** (fast-check, >=10,000 cases): decimation preserves per-column min-low and max-high for arbitrary series incl. monotonic, constant, and spike-heavy inputs; the first-open/last-close pair always comes from the correct end bars.
- **Unit**: threshold selection at every boundary and inside both dead bands; asymmetric promote/demote; step-down state machine incl. oscillation resistance with a `TestClock`; ladder ordering; assertion that trading-critical overlays are absent from the shed list.
- **Golden image**: the same series at L0, L1 and L2, and at each density mode, confirming the spike is visible at every level.
- **Perf**: **B2** (<=14 ms p95, <=6 LOD changes over the sweep) and **B5** (combined scene <=16.7 ms) as required checks; allocation-counter test asserting zero allocations in the decimation path.
- **Integration**: forced over-budget frames (via a synthetic stall) asserting the ladder runs in order and logs each step.
- **A11y**: the aggregation indicator's text is present in the DOM mirror and announced once on change, not per frame.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**.

The security-relevant property here is **integrity of what the user sees**, which is why min/max preservation is specified as a correctness requirement and tested as a property rather than by example. A decimation bug that hides a wick is indistinguishable to the user from a data-feed bug and could lead to a real trading loss — it is treated as a P0 correctness defect, not a rendering nicety.

**Denial of service** (E11-X01): the decimation output buffer is bounded by the pane's pixel width, so no zoom level or data volume can make it allocate unboundedly; the step-down ladder is itself the engine's DoS mitigation against pathological workloads. No secrets, no I/O, no `eval`.

## Accessibility notes
- **Non-colour-only disclosure**: the aggregation indicator is text ("Aggregated — 12 bars per column"), satisfying `05-accessibility-standard.md` and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 1. SCR-030's degraded state ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells") is the screen-level rendering of this same signal.
- The DOM mirror (E11-S13) must report the *same* LOD level as the canvas — a mirror claiming full detail while the canvas shows a column strip is a desync defect, explicitly never acceptable per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4.
- LOD changes announce **once** in a polite live region, never per frame.
- Degradation must never shed a trading-critical overlay, because for a keyboard/screen-reader user those overlays are the only positional cue available.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the mechanism by which budget **#2** (30 fps floor under the B6 worst case) is met. Gates: **B2** <=14 ms p95 with <=6 LOD changes; **B5** <=16.7 ms p95 with <=40 draw calls; **B6** aggregate <=16.7 ms. Decimation is O(visible bars) with zero allocations. The engine must degrade rather than drop frames — a dropped frame is invisible and unaccountable, a step-down is logged and disclosed.

## Observability
Events `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN` / `ENGINE_LOD_STEPUP` with `{ from, to, reason, frameTimeP95 }`; counters `engine.lod.level`, `engine.lod.bars_per_column`, `engine.lod.transitions_per_minute` (an oscillation alarm above 30), `engine.degradation.rung`. All surfaced on SCR-046 and included in the copied diagnostics snapshot.

## Definition of Done

title: Expose the chart to AT via a windowed DOM mirror and keyboard data cursor
body:
## Context
A WebGL canvas is, by default, an empty node in the accessibility tree: no DOM, no semantics, nothing for a screen reader to read. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 calls this "the highest-risk area" of the whole product and mandates **three complementary layers, all of them, not either/or**. §6.1 goes further and states that the engine's public API must expose a "current visible window + current focused unit" query surface **as an explicit chart-engine-design requirement, not an afterthought bolted on later** — which is why this Story sits inside E11 rather than in a later a11y clean-up Epic.

This Story ships layers 1, 2 and 4: the windowed DOM mirror, the throttled live regions, and the `role="img"` canvas fallback label. Layer 3 (the data-table alternative, SCR-045) is E11-S14.

`US-CHART-008` requires the keyboard crosshair as a first-class path — "when I focus the chart and press arrow keys, the crosshair steps bar by bar and the readout is announced in a live region" — and CMP-190 states plainly that **keyboard-driven crosshair movement is the accessible path; mouse hover is the pointer-only convenience layer**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/a11y/DomMirror.ts` (main thread) — a visually-hidden (`clip-path`, **never** `display:none`) DOM structure mirroring the currently-relevant data: visible bar range with OHLCV, the focused bar, the focused footprint cell's values, the focused heatmap cell. **Windowed/virtualised**: only currently-visible/focusable units are materialised, so 100k bars never become 100k nodes.
- The **canvas control surrogate** pattern: one `tabindex`-able, ARIA-labelled element per logical unit, positioned to align with the visual target it represents so it satisfies target-size and focus-visible rules simultaneously. Focus ring via **CMP-004 FocusRing**.
- `src/a11y/DataCursor.ts` (worker-side state, main-thread surface) — keyboard data cursor: `<-/->` step bar, `Up/Down` step price level, `Home`/`End` first/last bar, `PageUp`/`PageDown` page, `+`/`-` zoom, `Alt+T` opens the data table (E11-S14). The cursor is stored in **world coordinates**, so resize, zoom and pan never lose it.
- The engine query surface §6.1 requires, frame-synchronous with rendering: `chart.getVisibleWindow()` and `chart.getFocusedUnit()`, plus the `a11y` worker->main message (`{ cursorSummary }`) from the §6 protocol.
- `src/a11y/LiveRegions.ts` — pre-rendered, never-recreated containers whose **text content only** is swapped (region hygiene, §6.2):
  - `aria-live="polite"` for ambient values, throttled to the configured cadence (default 1 update / 2 s per field, user-configurable), always presenting the **latest** value rather than queuing intermediate ticks. `US-CHART-008` caps announcements at <=2/s.
  - `role="alert"` reserved for discrete, low-frequency events (context lost/restored, data stale, LOD step-down) — never throttled, announced once in full.
- Layer 4: canvas `role="img"` with a rolling `aria-label` ("BTCUSDT 1 minute, last 64 011, up 0.4 %, delta +200") updated on data change (CMP-180), so no silent empty node exists in the tree.
- A "reduce announcements" master toggle and per-class politeness routing surfaced as engine options for the Settings -> Accessibility panel to bind to.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-045 data-table alternative — **E11-S14** (layer 3).
- The Settings -> Accessibility UI itself — E10/E15 chrome; this Story exposes the options it writes.
- Footprint-cell and DOM-ladder mirror *content* — E18/E21 register their focusable unit types against the mirror's extension point defined here.
- Manual NVDA/VoiceOver certification passes — **E11-Q05**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The chart is fully operable without a mouse
  Given a chart pane has keyboard focus and 500 bars are visible
  When the user presses Right arrow ten times, then End, then Home
  Then the data cursor steps one bar per press, jumps to the last bar, then the first
  And each stop updates the focused surrogate element and the polite live region

Scenario: Announcements are throttled and never flood
  Given a live feed producing 20 ticks per second
  When the ambient live region is observed for 10 seconds
  Then at most 2 announcements per second are emitted per field
  And each announcement carries the latest value, not a queued backlog

Scenario: Discrete events are announced once, in full, unthrottled
  Given the WebGL context is lost
  When the alert region fires
  Then "Graphics context lost - restoring" is announced exactly once
  And it is not coalesced with or delayed by ambient throttling

Scenario: The mirror is windowed, not complete
  Given a 100,000-bar series is loaded
  When the accessibility tree is inspected
  Then only the currently visible and focusable units are materialised as DOM nodes
  And the node count stays under 500 regardless of series length

Scenario: The mirror never desyncs from the canvas
  Given the engine is rendering at LOD level L2 with 12 bars aggregated per column
  When the focused unit is queried from the DOM mirror and from the renderer in the same frame
  Then both report the same bar, the same values and the same aggregation level
  And a property test over random pan/zoom sequences finds no frame where they disagree

Scenario: The canvas is never a silent empty node
  Given assistive technology reaches the canvas element directly
  When its accessible name is read
  Then role="img" is present with a current summary label naming symbol, interval, last price and delta
  And the label updates when the underlying data changes

Scenario: Focus survives resize and zoom
  Given the data cursor is on bar 4,200
  When the window is resized and the chart is zoomed twice
  Then the cursor remains on bar 4,200 and keyboard focus is not lost
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why world coordinates.** The cursor is `{ time: number, price: number }`, not `{ x, y }`. Every pixel-space event (resize, DPR change, zoom, pan, LOD step) would otherwise invalidate it. This one decision is what makes the "focus survives resize" scenario trivially true rather than a pile of special cases.

**Windowing.** The mirror materialises `visibleUnits  intersect  focusableWindow`, where the focusable window is the visible range clamped to a hard cap (default 500 nodes). At LOD >= L1 the mirror mirrors **columns**, not bars, and its label says so ("12 bars aggregated") — this is how mirror and canvas stay in agreement at every LOD, satisfying the desync scenario.

**Throttling.** A per-field latest-value cell plus a single timer:

```ts
class ThrottledField {
  private latest: string | null = null;
  set(v: string) { this.latest = v; }            // called at tick rate
  flush() {                                       // called at the throttle cadence
    if (this.latest !== null && this.latest !== this.rendered) {
      this.node.textContent = this.latest;        // text swap only, node preserved
      this.rendered = this.latest;
    }
  }
}
```

The node is never destroyed or recreated — §6.2's region-hygiene rule, and the single most common cause of "the screen reader stopped announcing" defects.

**Frame synchrony.** The `a11y` message is emitted by the worker in the same frame as the `viewport`/`pick` messages it derives from, so the main thread applies mirror updates from a consistent snapshot rather than interleaving two frames' state.

**Config keys**: `a11y.announceCadenceMs` (default 2000), `a11y.reduceAnnouncements` (bool), `a11y.mirrorNodeCap` (default 500), `a11y.politenessByClass` (map).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cursor stepping at range boundaries; world-coordinate persistence across resize/zoom/LOD; windowing cap; throttle latest-value semantics with a `TestClock`; node-preservation assertion (same DOM node identity before and after an update); politeness routing.
- **Property** (fast-check): over random pan/zoom/LOD sequences, mirror focused unit == renderer focused unit, every frame.
- **Integration**: keyboard-only traversal of a full chart with `@testing-library` — no pointer events dispatched at all.
- **A11y automation**: axe-core zero violations on every chart route; assertions that the canvas has `role="img"` with a non-empty, updating label; live-region presence-on-load assertions.
- **Manual** (feeds E11-Q05): NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS passes over pan, zoom, crosshair stepping, LOD change and context loss.
- **Perf**: mirror maintenance <=1 ms per frame; asserted under the B5 scene so the a11y layer cannot silently consume the frame budget.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — the mirror exposes prices and volumes that are already on screen. It introduces no new data to a new surface.

One real consideration: the mirror is real DOM containing formatted values, so it is subject to the app's CSP and XSS posture like any other DOM. Control: values are written with `textContent`, **never** `innerHTML`, so a malformed or hostile symbol name or number string cannot become markup. This is an explicit test assertion, not a convention.

No secrets, no credentials, no account identifiers. Reviewed under E11-X03.

## Accessibility notes
This Story **is** the accessibility contract of the chart engine. Binding requirements from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6:
- §6.1 layer 1 — windowed offscreen DOM mirror using the canvas-control-surrogate pattern, visually hidden by `clip-path` and never `display:none` (which would remove it from the accessibility tree entirely).
- §6.2 layer 2 — pre-rendered live regions with text-content-only swaps; polite for ambient, `role="alert"` for discrete; ambient throttled to a user-configurable cadence with a "reduce announcements" master toggle.
- §6.4 layer 4 — canvas `role="img"` with a rolling summary label.
- §3.1.6 — no hover-only and no drag-only functionality: the keyboard crosshair is the **primary** path (CMP-190), pointer hover is the convenience layer.
- Focus is visible via CMP-004 FocusRing and focus order follows the visual order of panes.
- WCAG 2.2 AA throughout; axe-core zero violations is a merge gate; NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist in E11-Q05.
- Design source: **E11-D07** (a11y design review) and **E11-D02** (chart chassis).

## Performance notes
The mirror must cost <=1 ms per frame under the B5 scene, and node count is hard-capped at 500 — an unwindowed mirror of 100k bars would blow both the accessibility tree and the frame budget, which is exactly why §6.1 specifies windowing. Announcement throttling is a *performance* control for screen readers as much as a usability one: an unthrottled 20 Hz feed makes a screen reader unusable. Mirror updates are batched into one DOM write per frame, never one per unit.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.a11y.mirror_nodes`, `engine.a11y.announcements_per_minute` (per politeness class), `engine.a11y.mirror_update_ms`, `engine.a11y.desync_detected` (must remain 0 — an alerting condition, since desync is never acceptable per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4). Analytics events owned by the app layer: `chart.data_cursor_used`, `a11y.reduce_announcements_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S07** — the crosshair/readout state the cursor and announcements are derived from.
- **E11-S08** — hit-testing supplies the focused-unit resolution used by both pointer and keyboard paths.
- **E11-S12** — the LOD level the mirror must report to stay in sync.
- **E11-D07** — the a11y design review must be signed off before this Story starts (design-ahead rule).
- Blocks **E11-S14** (the data table consumes the same query surface) and every later canvas Epic (E18, E19, E21), which register unit types against the mirror.

title: Ship the SCR-045 data-table alternative as an equal-status chart view
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-014` (Must) requires a tabular, readable alternative to the canvas so that "chart content is not lost to me", and its NFR is emphatic: **"this view is treated as an equal-status alternative, not a degraded fallback."** `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 repeats the point — the table "is not a stripped-down compliance minimum; it exposes the **same data fidelity** as the visual cell so a screen-reader/keyboard-only user is not second-class" — and SCR-045 makes it a sign-off criterion that the table is "reachable from the chart panel header, not hidden in settings — equal status verified".

This is layer 3 of the three-layer canvas strategy. Layers 1, 2 and 4 ship in E11-S13.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-045** — chart data-table alternative, opened by `Alt+T` from any chart and from a control in the chart panel header (not from settings).
- A real semantic `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` headers and the price/time cell as `<th scope="row">` — not a `div` grid with ARIA bolted on.
- Column set for the chart table: **time, open, high, low, close, volume, delta, CVD**, plus an expandable per-bar footprint cell list (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag) — the footprint sub-rows are populated by E18; this Story ships the expandable row mechanism and renders "—" until then.
- Interactions per SCR-045: arrow keys move, `Enter` expands a bar's cells, `Ctrl+C` copies the selection as TSV, per-row actions (create alert here, replay from here, add note) exposed as extension points registered by E40/E26/E41.
- **Tri-state sort** on activating a column header (`Enter`/`Space`): ascending -> descending -> natural default order, announced via `aria-sort`; sort state persists while the table is open and resets when the focused bar/level changes.
- **Filter toolbar** above the table for filter-only columns; filters narrow rows, never remove columns; active-filter state announced via a live region ("Showing 6 of 40 rows, filtered by: Bid-stacked").
- **Live sync, not a snapshot**: the table reads the same windowed query surface as the DOM mirror (E11-S13). On each throttled tick, **row values are patched in place** — cell text updated, row DOM identity preserved — so screen-reader focus and active sort/filter survive live updates.
- **Stale banner**: if the focused bar/level scrolls out of view, show "Data is for bar X, no longer in view — press Alt+T to refresh to current" rather than going silently stale.
- **Bidirectional crosshair sync** (`US-CHART-014` scenario 3): moving the crosshair moves the table's focused row, and moving the table's focused row moves the crosshair.
- **Summary announcement**: a "request summary" action announcing a concise description of the visible range (trend, range, notable flags).
- Virtualisation: 100k rows without jank, <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame, reading the in-memory series so **no extra fetch is issued**.
- Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell sub-row **content** — E18 (this Story ships the expandable mechanism and the column contract).
- The profile and DOM-ladder table variants of §6.3 — E19 and E21 respectively; they reuse the table shell built here.
- "Create alert here" / "replay from here" / "add note" **implementations** — E40, E26, E41 register against the row-action extension point.
- CSV/TSV export beyond `Ctrl+C` of the current selection — E15's export work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The table is reachable as an equal-status view
  Given a chart pane is focused
  When the user presses Alt+T
  Then the data table opens showing the currently visible bars
  And an equivalent control is present in the chart panel header, not buried in settings

Scenario: The table carries the same data fidelity as the canvas
  Given a visible range of 480 bars is rendered on the canvas
  When the table is opened and its rows are compared to the rendered series
  Then every bar present on the canvas is present in the table with identical time, OHLC, volume and delta
  And an automated parity test asserts this over random ranges, not by spot check

Scenario: Live updates preserve focus, sort and filter
  Given the table is open, sorted by delta descending, filtered to flagged rows, with row 12 focused
  When three live update ticks arrive
  Then the values in place are updated and row 12 still has focus
  And the sort and filter are still applied, with no row node destroyed or recreated

Scenario: Sorting is tri-state and announced
  Given the table is in its natural order
  When the user activates the "delta" column header three times
  Then the order goes ascending, descending, then back to natural
  And aria-sort on that header reports "ascending", "descending", then "none"

Scenario: Crosshair and table stay in sync both ways
  Given the table is open with row 100 focused
  When the user moves the chart crosshair to bar 250
  Then the table's focused row moves to bar 250
  And when the user then arrows to row 251 in the table, the crosshair moves to bar 251

Scenario: A scrolled-away focus shows a banner, never silent staleness
  Given the table is showing data for bar X
  When the user pans the chart so bar X is no longer in the visible range
  Then a banner states the data is for bar X and is no longer in view, with a refresh instruction
  And the stale values are not presented as if they were current

Scenario: 100k rows scroll without jank
  Given a 100,000-bar series is loaded
  When the table is scrolled continuously
  Then scripting stays <= 8 ms per scroll frame
  And no additional network request is issued, because the table reads the in-memory series
```

## Technical notes / design
**Row identity is the whole design.** Rows are keyed by bar open time, and updates patch `textContent` on the existing cells. Destroying and rebuilding rows is what breaks screen-reader focus, and it is the defect this design exists to prevent — asserted by a DOM-node-identity test, not left to review.

**Virtualisation with real table semantics.** A naively virtualised `<table>` breaks row/column relationships for screen readers. The implementation renders a windowed `<tbody>` while declaring the full row count via `aria-rowcount` on the table and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row, so AT reports "row 4,200 of 100,000" correctly — the WAI-ARIA grid pattern for virtualised tables.

**Bidirectional sync without loops.** Both surfaces subscribe to a single focused-unit store (the E11-S13 query surface). Neither writes to the other directly; each writes to the store and re-renders from it. Echo suppression is therefore structural — there is no cycle to suppress.

**Summary generation.** `summariseRange(visible)` -> "480 bars, 13:00 to 21:00 UTC, range 63,800 to 64,300, closed up 0.4 %, 3 bars flagged". Deterministic and unit-tested, so the announcement is reviewable text rather than an ad hoc string built at the call site.

## Test plan
- **Parity test** (the headline test): over random visible ranges, every bar rendered on the canvas appears in the table with identical values — this is the automated form of "equal status".
- **Unit**: tri-state sort cycling and `aria-sort` values; filter narrowing plus its live-region message; stale-banner trigger; `summariseRange` output; TSV serialisation of a selection.
- **DOM-identity test**: row nodes survive N live updates (asserting `===` node identity before/after).
- **Integration**: bidirectional crosshair<->row sync; `Alt+T` open/close and focus placement/restoration.
- **A11y**: axe-core zero violations; `aria-rowcount`/`aria-rowindex` correctness under virtualisation; NVDA/JAWS table-mode navigation (Ctrl+Alt+arrows) manual pass in **E11-Q05**; header-cell scope correctness.
- **Perf**: 100k-row scroll with <=8 ms scripting per frame; assertion that zero network requests are issued while the table is open.
- Coverage >=80 % (this is `apps/web` code, not engine package code).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**.

Two controls worth naming. First, all cell values are written with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`, so no formatted value can become markup. Second, `Ctrl+C` TSV export writes to the clipboard only on an explicit user gesture and copies **only the current selection** — it is not a path by which a page script can silently exfiltrate the whole series.

The row-action extension points (alert, replay, note) cross into Epics that do mutate state; the contract defined here passes an opaque bar reference and performs no privileged action itself. RBAC for those actions belongs to E09 and the registering Epic, and is explicitly not weakened by exposing the action here — a `viewer` sees the table, and the actions they lack permission for are simply not registered.

## Accessibility notes
This Story is the **normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030** and is verified in every a11y test pass (SCR-045's own wording). Requirements:
- Real `<table>` semantics with `<th scope="col">` and `<th scope="row">`; standard screen-reader table-mode navigation works.
- `aria-sort` on sortable headers, tri-state, announced.
- Filter state announced via a live region with counts ("Showing 6 of 40 rows").
- Fully keyboard-navigable grid: arrows, `Enter` to expand, `Ctrl+C` to copy; `Alt+T` to open from anywhere on the chart.
- Equal status is a **sign-off criterion**: reachable from the panel header, same data fidelity, not a degraded fallback.
- Delta signs are shown as text `+`/`-`, never colour-only; imbalance flags are text labels, never icon-only; `(estimated)` markers carry the literal word.
- Live updates preserve focus and do not flood — the table shares E11-S13's throttle cadence.
- Design source: **E11-D04** (table / empty / error hi-fi).

## Performance notes
SCR-045's budget: virtualised rendering of 100k rows with **<=8 ms scripting per scroll frame** and no extra fetch, since it reads the same in-memory series as the canvas. Live patching is O(visible rows), not O(series). Opening the table must not perturb the canvas frame budget — asserted by running the B5 benchmark with the table open.

## Observability
Analytics: `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (per SCR-045). Counters: `a11y.table.rows_rendered`, `a11y.table.patch_ms`, `a11y.table.stale_banner_shown`. The parity test result is published as a CI artefact so "equal status" is evidenced, not asserted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S13** — the windowed query surface, focused-unit store and throttle cadence the table reads from.
- **E11-D04** — hi-fi design for the table, empty and error states, signed off >=2 sprints earlier.
- **E05** — CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker from the design system.
- Blocks **E11-T09** (API freeze) and is extended by **E18** (footprint sub-rows), **E19**, **E21**.

## Branch

title: Govern chart memory with a budget, eviction and days-to-load estimates
body:
## Context
Requirement **R7** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` caps a chart instance at **600 MB** of GPU + JS heap at full load; §7 models the 100k-bar / 4 h-heatmap case at ~116 MB, leaving headroom that a careless paging policy would happily consume.

`US-CHART-010` (Must) turns that budget into a user-facing contract: setting a lookback shows **the estimated memory footprint**; a request that would exceed the configured client memory budget **warns with the estimate and requires confirmation before loading**; and each view type (chart, footprint, profile, replay) has its own default lookback. Its NFR fixes the accuracy bar: the estimate must be **accurate within ±20 %**, and **loading never blocks the UI thread**.

This Story is the engine half of that contract — the governor, the eviction policy, the paging trigger and the estimator — feeding SCR-044 ("Go to date") and SCR-047 (empty/no-data).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/memory/MemoryGovernor.ts` — samples usage **every 5 s** (§7) across the columnar stores, GPU buffers, textures and the SDF atlas; steps down when usage exceeds **70 %** of `memoryBudgetMb` by calling E11-S12's step-down API; emits `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE` at the threshold.
- **Eviction policy** per §7: footprint cells and heatmap columns outside a **3× viewport window** are dropped from GPU buffers while retained in CPU stores; under continued pressure, CPU stores are dropped too and re-fetched from the backend on demand.
- `src/memory/Estimator.ts` — the §7 formula table made executable: given `{ barCount, cellsPerBar, heatmapColumns, priceRows, panes, dpr, viewportPx }` it returns a byte estimate broken down per item (BarStore, GPU candle buffers, FootprintStore, glyph runs, heatmap rings, atlas, framebuffers). Must be within **±20 %** of measured, verified by a calibration test.
- `visibleRangeNeedsData` paging callback (the engine's request-for-more-history signal): emitted when the visible range approaches the loaded edge, debounced, cancellable, and never issuing I/O itself — the app layer performs the fetch (the engine does no I/O, `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16).
- Per-view-type default lookbacks (`chart`, `footprint`, `profile`, `replay`) as engine config consumed by the settings UI.
- Over-budget confirmation flow: the estimate and the budget are exposed so the app can render the warning and require confirmation **before** the load starts.
- Hard ceilings `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` enforced at every ingest point, so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.
- Config keys: `memory.budgetMb` (default 600), `memory.sampleIntervalMs` (5000), `memory.stepDownPct` (70), `memory.viewportWindowMultiplier` (3), `memory.defaultLookbackDays` (per view type).

## Out of scope
- Fetching history — the app/data layer and **E17**/**E12**; the engine only signals need.
- The SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog UI and SCR-047 empty-state UI — E15/E10 chrome consuming this Story's estimates and signals.
- Backend-side retention and disk budget — **E16**.
- Heatmap ring-buffer implementation — E21 (its memory is accounted for here, its rendering is not built here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The memory estimate is shown before loading and is accurate
  Given the user sets a 30-day lookback on a 1-minute chart
  When the estimate is computed
  Then a per-item breakdown and a total are returned before any data is requested
  And the total is within 20 % of the memory actually consumed once loaded

Scenario: Exceeding the budget requires explicit confirmation
  Given the configured client memory budget is 600 MB
  When the user requests a lookback whose estimate is 780 MB
  Then the load does not start
  And the estimate and the budget are surfaced for confirmation, and loading proceeds only after the user confirms

Scenario: Memory pressure steps down detail rather than crashing
  Given usage crosses 70 % of the budget during a live session
  When the governor samples at its 5 second interval
  Then ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE is emitted and one degradation rung is shed
  And GPU buffers outside the 3x viewport window are evicted while CPU stores are retained

Scenario: Evicted data is transparently re-fetched when needed again
  Given footprint cells for a range were evicted under pressure
  When the user pans back to that range
  Then visibleRangeNeedsData fires for exactly that range
  And the chart shows a loading affordance for the missing range rather than drawing a silent gap

Scenario: Loading never blocks the UI thread
  Given a 100k-bar load is in progress
  When the main thread is sampled during the load
  Then no main-thread task exceeds 50 ms
  And pan and zoom remain responsive throughout

Scenario: A malformed length field cannot exhaust memory
  Given a data message declares a bar count above maxBars
  When it reaches the ingest path
  Then it is rejected with ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and no allocation of that size occurs
  And the existing scene continues rendering unaffected

Scenario: A 30-minute soak shows no runaway growth
  Given benchmark B10 runs a 30-minute live feed
  When peak memory and the growth trend are measured
  Then peak stays <= 600 MB and growth does not exceed 5 % over the 30 minutes
```

## Technical notes / design
**Estimator.** A direct encoding of the §7 table, so the document and the code cannot drift:

```ts
const estimate = (p: LoadParams) => ({
  barStore:      p.barCount * (8 + 4 * 4 + 4 + 4),
  candleGpu:     p.barCount * 28,
  footprintStore:p.fpBars * p.cellsPerBar * 18,
  glyphRuns:     p.fpBars * p.cellsPerBar * 12,
  heatFine:      2048 * p.priceRows * 2,
  heatCoarse:    p.heatmapColumns * p.priceRows * 2,
  atlas:         1024 * 1024,
  misc:          8 * 1024 * 1024,
  framebuffers:  p.viewportPx.w * p.viewportPx.h * 4 * Math.min(p.dpr, 2) ** 2 * FB_COUNT,
});
```

A **calibration test** loads each modelled case, measures actual usage via `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` where available and GL buffer accounting otherwise, and fails if any estimate is off by more than 20 % — which is how the ±20 % NFR becomes enforceable rather than aspirational.

**Sampling, not hooking.** The governor samples every 5 s rather than instrumenting every allocation: allocation hooks would themselves cost frame time, and pressure is a slow-moving condition. The trade-off is up to 5 s of latency before a step-down, which is acceptable because the LOD ladder (E11-S12) already handles fast-moving frame-time pressure on a 3-frame horizon. The two mechanisms are deliberately complementary: **frame time reacts in frames, memory reacts in seconds.**

**Eviction.** `3 × viewport` window, evicting GPU first (cheap to rebuild from CPU stores) and CPU second (requires a re-fetch). Eviction is never partial within a bar: a bar's cells are all present or all absent, so no half-drawn bar can appear.

## Test plan
- **Calibration test** (the headline test): estimate vs measured for each §7 modelled case, failing above ±20 %.
- **Unit**: estimator arithmetic per item; threshold crossing at 70 %; eviction window boundaries; `visibleRangeNeedsData` debouncing, cancellation and exact-range emission; `maxBars` rejection; per-view default lookbacks.
- **Integration**: pressure -> step-down -> eviction -> pan-back -> re-fetch, as one sequence.
- **Perf**: **B10** 30-minute soak (peak <=600 MB, growth <=5 %); main-thread task duration <=50 ms during a 100k-bar load; **B9** cold init <=900 ms with paging active.
- **Fuzz**: malformed length fields, negative counts, `NaN` bar counts — all rejected at the boundary, none reaching an allocator.
- **Chaos** (E11-Q04): repeated pressure cycles asserting no leak and no oscillation between evict and re-fetch.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**; no PII, no credentials.

STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in **E11-X01**): **Denial of service** is the primary one. An attacker-controlled or corrupted frame declaring an enormous length is the classic path to memory exhaustion in a binary-protocol client, and the whole point of hard `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings enforced **at the ingest boundary** is that no downstream code ever sees a value it could act on. **Tampering**: typed arrays are bounds- and value-validated (no `NaN`/`Infinity` prices) before indexing, so a corrupt frame cannot become an out-of-bounds read or poison the viewport.

Controls: ceilings enforced before allocation, not after; rejection emits `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR` and leaves the existing scene intact (fail-closed for the bad frame, not for the chart); fuzz tests over the ingest path are part of this Story's test plan, not a later hardening Epic. `security` label applies; reviewed in **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
- The over-budget warning is **text stating the estimate and the budget**, with a real confirmation control — never a colour-coded gauge alone (SCR-047's "empty state is a heading + paragraph + action, not an icon alone" convention applies).
- A range that is loading or was evicted must be announced as such in the DOM mirror ("loading 3 hours of history"), so a screen-reader user is never shown a silent gap.
- Memory-pressure step-downs announce once, politely, reusing E11-S12's aggregation-indicator channel — not per sample.
- Design source: **E11-D04** (empty/error states) and **E11-D03** (scale/date menus, which host the days-to-load control).

## Performance notes
Requirement **R7**: <=600 MB GPU + JS heap per chart instance; the §7 model is ~116 MB for the 100k-bar case. Gate **B10**: 30-minute soak, peak <=600 MB, no monotonic growth beyond 5 %/30 min. Governor sampling costs <=0.2 ms every 5 s — deliberately off the frame path. `US-CHART-010` NFRs: estimate within ±20 %, loading never blocks the UI thread (<=50 ms main-thread tasks).

## Observability
Counters: `engine.memory.used_mb` (broken down per store), `engine.memory.budget_mb`, `engine.memory.evictions`, `engine.memory.refetches`, `engine.paging.requests`. Errors: `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`. All surfaced on **SCR-046** (GPU memory estimate, buffer uploads/s) and included in the copied diagnostics snapshot, so a user reporting "it got slow" ships the memory trace with the report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-T03** — the columnar stores whose memory is governed and evicted.
- **E11-S12** — the step-down API the governor calls under pressure.
- **E17**/**E12** — supply the history that paging requests; the engine signals need and never fetches.
- Feeds **SCR-044** and **SCR-047** (E15/E10 chrome) and **E21**'s heatmap ring budgets.

## Branch

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility: DOM mirror, live regions, table alternative)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` 7 (CMP-180..199), `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041..049)
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §7 (memory budget table, eviction, MemoryGovernor), §13 B9/B10, R7
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-010 (Must, ±20 % estimate, non-blocking load)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-044, SCR-046, SCR-047
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 (memory budgets)
