title: Create packages/chart-engine with the public API surface and thin React bindings
body:
## Context
Every later chart ticket compiles against this surface, so it is written **first and frozen early** (interface-first rule, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10). `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 already contains the complete TypeScript API sketch — `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin` — this task transcribes it into a real package with compiling types and stub implementations, not new design.

`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 makes the package **framework-free**: no React, no application store, no `fetch`/XHR/WS client, no Bybit-specific type. The React ergonomics shown in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 (`<Chart><Pane><CandleSeries/></Pane></Chart>`) live in `apps/web`, are deliberately thin, and are the only place where React and the engine meet. E12/E13/E14/E18/E21 all register through the seam created here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New workspace package `packages/chart-engine` (pnpm workspace member from E02), `"type": "module"`, ESM + types build via `tsup`, `sideEffects: false`, TS `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
- `src/index.ts` exporting exactly the §8 surface and nothing else: `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `PriceScale`, `TimeScale`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesDataMap`, `SeriesDeltaMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `OrderLine`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `OverlayPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin`, `Unsubscribe`, `createChart(opts: ChartOptions): Chart`.
- Data shape types exactly as §8: `CandleData`, `FootprintData`, `HeatmapColumnData`, `FootprintOptions`, `HeatmapOptions` — prices as `Int32Array` ticks with `priceOrigin`/`tickSize`, times as `Float64Array` µs epoch.
- Stub `createChart` that mounts a canvas, fills it with `color.chart.background` and emits `frameStats`; real subsystems land in E11-S01/S02.
- `packages/chart-engine/README.md`: the package contract (framework-free, no I/O, transferable typed arrays in, pixels + events out) and a usage example.
- React bindings in `apps/web/src/chart/`: `<Chart>`, `<Pane>`, `useChartApi()`, `useCrosshair()`. Bindings own React lifecycle + option diffing only; they contain no rendering logic.
- CI boundary check: `eslint-plugin-import` `no-restricted-imports` + a `depcruise` rule failing the build if `packages/chart-engine` imports `react`, `react-dom`, any `apps/*` path, `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`/`WebSocket` usage, or any symbol whose name matches `/bybit/i`.
- `tsd` type tests asserting the exported surface is stable and that `packages/protocol` types are structurally assignable to the engine data shapes.

## Out of scope
- Any real rendering, scene graph, worker or GL code — E11-S01, E11-S02, E11-T02.
- Series/indicator/overlay plugin *implementations* — E12/E13/E14/E18/E19/E21. This task ships the interfaces only.
- Publishing the package to any registry; it is workspace-internal for the whole plan horizon.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The package builds and exports the designed surface
  Given packages/chart-engine is built with tsup and tsc --noEmit
  When the emitted .d.ts is compared against the API sketch in 26-chart-engine-design.md §8
  Then every named export in §8 exists with a matching signature
  And no symbol outside §8 is exported from the package root

Scenario: The framework-free boundary is enforced, not just documented
  Given a developer adds `import { useState } from "react"` inside packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs the boundary check
  Then the build fails naming the forbidden import and the rule (CONSTITUTION.md C-2.16)
  And the same happens for an import of fetch, WebSocket, or an apps/* path

Scenario: A chart mounts and reports frame stats through the stub
  Given createChart({ container, theme }) is called in apps/web
  When the component mounts
  Then a canvas sized to the container appears filled with color.chart.background
  And a frameStats event carrying renderProfile is delivered to the subscriber within 1 s

Scenario: Protocol types are assignable without adapters
  Given packages/protocol emits the generated WS payload types
  When the tsd contract test compiles
  Then a protocol BarsBatch payload is assignable to CandleData without a hand-written mapper
```

## Technical notes / design
Transcribe `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 verbatim; where the sketch is ambiguous, prefer the narrower type and record the choice in the README rather than widening the surface.

Precision rule (§3.3, non-negotiable and easy to get wrong): **prices are integer ticks** (`Int32Array`) relative to a per-symbol `priceOrigin`, never float prices. Float32 loses precision at BTC price magnitudes; the GL side subtracts `priceOrigin` in a uniform. Times are `Float64Array` microseconds since epoch.

`createChart` returns the facade object directly (no async) and resolves capability detection lazily so React bindings need no Suspense.

Directory layout, fixed here so later tickets do not relitigate it:
```
packages/chart-engine/
  src/index.ts        public surface only (re-exports)
  src/api/            facade: chart.ts, pane.ts, scales.ts
  src/scene/          (E11-S01)      src/gl/        (E11-S02)
  src/model/          (E11-T03)      src/worker/    (E11-T02)
  src/viewport/       (E11-S03)      src/text/      (E11-S11)
  src/interaction/    (E11-S04)      src/a11y/      (E11-S13)
  bench/              (E11-T06)      test/golden/   (E11-T08)
```

## Test plan
- **Unit** (Vitest): `createChart` mounts/disposes cleanly; `dispose()` is idempotent; `subscribe` returns a working `Unsubscribe`; option diffing in the React binding does not recreate the chart on an unrelated prop change.
- **Type/contract**: `tsd` assertions for each §8 export; `tsc --noEmit` across the workspace; a snapshot test of the emitted `.d.ts` public surface so an accidental export widening shows up in review.
- **Boundary**: a fixture file importing `react` is expected to fail lint; asserted in CI as a negative test.
- Coverage target >=85 % on the package (mostly type-level here; the stub paths are fully covered).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
`getDomMirrorRoot(): HTMLElement` (CMP-180's a11y contract anchor) is part of the API from day one, and the visible-window/focused-unit query surface required by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 is included in the frozen surface — it is an engine-design requirement, "not an afterthought bolted on later". The React binding renders the mirror root as a real DOM child of the container so focus can land in it.

## Performance notes
No runtime budget yet. Two structural budget guards: the package must tree-shake (`sideEffects: false`) and the initial engine chunk counts against budget #9 (<=8 MB gzipped initial bundle, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2) — record the stub's gzipped size as the baseline the later tickets are measured against.

## Observability
`frameStats` event shape wired end-to-end (even from the stub) so E11-T07's SCR-046 feed has a stable contract. Engine errors use the `ChartEvents["error"]` channel with stable string codes; the code table is owned by E11-S02.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E02** — pnpm workspace, TS config, lint/test tooling and the `import-linter`/dep-cruiser harness this task adds a contract to.
- **E06** — the spike's ADR must have confirmed the custom-engine path before the package exists.
- **E10** — `apps/web` and the Electron shell provide the mount point and theme provider the React bindings attach to.
- Blocks every other E11 ticket and all of E12/E13/E14/E18/E21.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-package` · one PR, ~350 LOC (mostly type declarations) + config. Review by the `packages/chart-engine` code owner and the Architect (interface-first change).

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

title: Implement the OffscreenCanvas render worker, protocol and inline fallback
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 splits the engine across two threads and the split is the reason the frame budget is reachable: the main thread keeps React, DOM overlays, accessibility and input capture; **everything with a per-frame cost** — decode, model updates, culling, batching, GL calls — runs in a render worker against an `OffscreenCanvas`. Input is captured on the main thread, coalesced, and forwarded as compact messages so pan/zoom never waits on React.

§2 also mandates a **supported, tested** fallback: where `OffscreenCanvas` is unavailable (older WebView2), the identical worker code runs on the main thread behind the same facade as `RunMode.inline` — "only throughput changes, not behaviour". Shipping the fallback as an afterthought is how it rots, so it is built here with the worker.

§6 fixes the message tables in both directions; this task implements them exactly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/worker/render-worker.ts` — the worker entry, bundled same-origin (no `blob:` URL, so the Electron CSP from E10 needs no widening).
- `src/worker/host.ts` — the main-thread host: canvas `transferControlToOffscreen()`, worker lifecycle, message dispatch, backpressure, `terminate()` on `dispose()`.
- Main->worker messages per §6: `init` `{canvas, dpr, theme, chartConfig}`, `resize` `{width,height,dpr}` (debounced one frame), `input` `{kind: pointer|wheel|key|touch, coalesced[]}` (<=1/frame), `data` `{store, op: append|patch|prepend|replace, buffer}` (transferred, up to 20/s per store), `command` `{setViewport|setSeriesOptions|addDrawing|setTheme|setLod|pickAt|export}`, `sync` `{groupId, timeRange, crosshair}` (<=1/frame).
- Worker->main per §6: `ready` (capability report + selected `RenderProfile`), `frame` (`FrameStats`, sampled 1 Hz, full in bench mode), `pick` (edge-triggered), `viewport` (<=1/frame), `a11y` `{cursorSummary}`, `error` `{code,message,recoverable}`.
- `RunMode` selection: `'worker'` when `OffscreenCanvas` + `transferControlToOffscreen` exist, else `'inline'`; overridable via `ChartOptions.runMode` for tests. The inline path runs the *same* modules behind a synchronous message bus — no second implementation.
- **One rAF per worker**: N chart instances on a page share one worker and one rAF, rendering into their own canvases in sequence (§3.2 rule 1). The host registers/deregisters instances with the shared worker.
- Transferable discipline: every `data` message transfers its `ArrayBuffer`; a test asserts `buffer.byteLength === 0` on the sender afterwards (proof of zero-copy).
- Validation at the worker boundary: unknown message kind -> `error` with code `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, never a throw that kills the worker; buffer length must match the declared element count.
- Worker crash recovery: `onerror`/`onmessageerror` -> emit `error`, tear down, re-init from the retained `DataModel` snapshot request, max 3 attempts with 1/2/4 s backoff, then surface SCR-048.

## Out of scope
- The shared **WS client** worker that decodes wire frames (§9) — that is E17 plus the `apps/web` data layer. This task defines the port the decoded typed arrays arrive on; it never opens a socket.
- The `DataModel` stores the `data` messages mutate — E11-T03.
- GL work inside the worker — E11-S02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rendering runs off the main thread
  Given a chart mounted in a browser supporting OffscreenCanvas
  When a 2 s artificial main-thread block is injected during a continuous pan
  Then the canvas keeps panning and rendering throughout the block
  And RunMode reported in the ready message is "worker"

Scenario: Inline fallback is behaviourally identical
  Given ChartOptions.runMode = "inline"
  When the interaction test suite for pan, zoom, crosshair and resize is run
  Then every assertion that passes in worker mode also passes in inline mode
  And the only permitted difference is throughput, recorded in the benchmark report

Scenario: Data buffers are transferred, never copied
  Given a 3.2 MB CandleData batch is handed to SeriesHandle.setData
  When the data message reaches the worker
  Then the sender's ArrayBuffer byteLength is 0
  And no structuredClone of the payload appears in a heap snapshot taken after the send

Scenario: A malformed message cannot kill the worker
  Given a message with kind "data", store "bars" and a buffer 3 bytes shorter than its declared element count
  When the worker processes it
  Then the message is rejected with an error event carrying code ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and recoverable=true
  And the worker continues to render the previous frame contents

Scenario: Worker death is recovered
  Given the render worker is killed externally mid-session
  When the host observes the termination
  Then it re-initialises the worker and restores the scene within 2 s, retrying at most 3 times
  And if all retries fail, SCR-048 shows the error state with a copyable correlation id
```

## Technical notes / design
Message envelope (structured-cloneable, no JSON on the hot path):
```ts
type ToWorker =
  | { t: 'init'; id: ChartId; canvas: OffscreenCanvas; dpr: number; theme: ThemeLut; config: ChartConfig }
  | { t: 'resize'; id: ChartId; width: number; height: number; dpr: number }
  | { t: 'input'; id: ChartId; kind: 'pointer'|'wheel'|'key'|'touch'; events: Float32Array }
  | { t: 'data'; id: ChartId; store: StoreId; op: 'append'|'patch'|'prepend'|'replace'; layout: BufferLayout; buffer: ArrayBuffer }
  | { t: 'command'; id: ChartId; cmd: Command }
  | { t: 'sync'; groupId: string; timeRange: [number, number]; crosshair: number | null };
```
`input` events are packed into a `Float32Array` (`[type, x, y, buttons, modifiers, dt] × n`) rather than an object array — object-array cloning at 240 Hz trackpad rates was the measured cost the design is avoiding.

**Shared worker vs dedicated**: one *dedicated* worker per page shared by all chart instances (not a `SharedWorker`) — Electron renderer isolation makes `SharedWorker` lifetime awkward and the design only requires one rAF per page. The WS client separately uses a shared worker (E17), outside this scope.

Error codes owned here: `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, `ENGINE_WORKER_LOST`. Codes for GL failures are owned by E11-S02.

Backpressure: the host keeps at most 2 unacknowledged `data` messages per store; beyond that, `append` payloads are conflated (last-wins for `patch`/`replace`, concatenated for `append`) before sending. The feed is already conflated upstream, so this is a second guard, not the primary one.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (Vitest): message encode/decode round-trip for every kind in §6; conflation logic under a 3× overrun; length-mismatch rejection; `RunMode` selection matrix (OffscreenCanvas present/absent × explicit option).
- **Integration**: the whole interaction suite is parameterised over `runMode: ['worker','inline']` and must pass in both — this is what keeps the fallback honest.
- **Robustness/fuzz**: 10k randomly corrupted messages (truncated buffers, wrong store ids, NaN coordinates, unknown `t`) must produce zero unhandled rejections and zero worker terminations.
- **Perf**: B7 (live update storm, 20 msg/s × 6 stores) — decode + dispatch p95 <=4 ms, zero dropped messages.
- **E2E**: main-thread block test above, in Playwright and in the Electron driver.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. Threats from `04-security-program.md` mapped to this boundary:
- **Tampering / memory safety**: the worker boundary is the engine's only untrusted-input surface. Every `data` message is validated before any typed-array view is created: declared element count × stride must equal `buffer.byteLength`, `store` must be a known id, and offsets must be within range. Failure yields a recoverable `error`, never an exception across the boundary.
- **Denial of service**: bounded queue depth (2 unacked per store) plus conflation; a hostile producer cannot grow the queue. `maxBars`/`memoryBudgetMb` ceilings are enforced downstream by E11-S15.
- **Supply chain / CSP**: the worker is bundled from a same-origin asset URL — no `blob:` worker, no `eval`, no data-derived code. This keeps the E10 Electron CSP strict (`worker-src 'self'`).
Requires the `security` label; reviewed as part of the E11-X01 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
The `a11y` worker->main message (`{cursorSummary}`) is implemented here — it is the transport the live-region layer (E11-S13) consumes. Throttling to <=2 announcements/s (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2) is applied on the **main-thread** side, not the worker, so the worker never becomes the throttle authority. In `inline` mode announcements must arrive on exactly the same schedule; asserted by the shared interaction suite.

## Performance notes
Serves budget #1 directly: the main thread must stay free for React and the DOM mirror (<=1 ms of the 16.6 ms frame per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3). Targets: postMessage overhead <=0.2 ms per frame for the input batch; zero structured-clone of any data payload; B7 decode p95 <=4 ms. `inline` mode is expected to lose throughput and is exempted from B5/B6 gates but must still hold 30 fps on B1 — recorded, not gated.

## Observability
`frame` stats at 1 Hz (full rate in bench mode) carrying `renderProfile` and `runMode`. Counters: `engine.worker.messages_dropped`, `engine.worker.conflated`, `engine.worker.restarts`. `Performance.mark()` pairs around post->receive so the SCR-046 overlay can show the transport slice of the frame.

title: Implement columnar typed-array data stores with append/patch/prepend mutations
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 specifies the engine's data model as **columnar, typed-array based, append-optimised, with stable indices**. It is the M2 "data plane" milestone (§15) and the reason the memory budget in §7 closes at ~116 MB for the 100k-bar case against a 600 MB ceiling (requirement R7).

Stable indices matter beyond memory: drawings anchor to `barIndex` *and* `time` (§3.10), hit-testing computes bar index analytically (§3.9), and paging splices history at the front (`prependHistory`) without invalidating anything already on screen. A store that renumbers on mutation would break all three.

This task ships the stores and their mutation API. The series that read them ship in E12; the footprint/heatmap stores are declared here but only the bar store is exercised, because E18/E21 own their semantics.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/model/BarStore.ts` per §3.3: `time: Float64Array` (µs), `open/high/low/close: Int32Array` (ticks from `priceOrigin`), `volume/delta: Float32Array`, head/tail ring indices, capacity grown by doubling.
- `src/model/FootprintStore.ts`: parallel arrays sorted by `(barIndex, priceLevel)` — `barIndex: Uint32Array`, `priceLevel: Int32Array`, `bidVol/askVol: Float32Array`, `tradeCount: Uint16Array`, `offsets: Uint32Array` prefix sums mapping `barIndex -> first cell index`.
- `src/model/HeatmapRing.ts`: descriptor only (ring width 2048 columns × 512 price rows, `writeCol` cursor) — the texture itself is uploaded by E21.
- Mutation API returning **affected index ranges** so the batch builder can do `bufferSubData` on a sub-range instead of re-uploading: `append(data) -> {from,to}`, `patch(index, data) -> {from,to}`, `prepend(data) -> {from,to, indexShift}`, `replace(data) -> {from:0, to:n}`.
- `BarView` read facade (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 `IndicatorPlugin.compute`) giving bounds-checked, allocation-free access to a bar range.
- Index maps: monotone `index -> time` and a binary-search `time -> index` (`timeToIndex`, used by drawings and Go-to-date), both O(log n), both covered by property tests.
- Capacity policy: doubling growth up to `ChartOptions.maxBars` (default 200 000); at the ceiling, oldest bars are evicted from the front and `indexShift` is reported so anchors can be rebased.
- Snapshot/replace semantics (§9): a `replace` keeps the previous contents renderable until the new store is fully built, so there is **no blank flash**.

## Out of scope
- GPU buffer management and `bufferSubData` calls — E11-S02 consumes the returned ranges.
- Footprint and heatmap *semantics* (imbalance, price grouping, column cadence) — E18 and E21.
- Any fetching or paging policy — E11-S15 decides *when* to ask; this task only splices what arrives.
- Persistence: stores are in-memory only and are rebuilt from the backend on reload.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Appending a bar touches only the new range
  Given a BarStore holding 100 000 bars
  When append() adds one bar
  Then the returned range is {from: 100000, to: 100001}
  And no existing element is written and no reallocation occurs while capacity remains

Scenario: Prepending history preserves on-screen anchors
  Given a BarStore of 5 000 bars with a drawing anchored at barIndex 120 / time T
  When prependHistory splices 2 000 older bars
  Then indexShift is 2000 and timeToIndex(T) returns 2120
  And the drawing resolves to the same time and price as before the splice

Scenario: Prefix sums address footprint cells in O(1)
  Given a FootprintStore of 20 000 bars × up to 40 cells each
  When cells for bar 12 345 are requested
  Then they are returned as a subarray view between offsets[12345] and offsets[12346]
  And no copy is allocated

Scenario: Hostile values are rejected at the store boundary
  Given an append payload containing NaN in close and Infinity in volume
  When the mutation is applied
  Then the payload is rejected with ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and the store is left byte-identical to before
  And a counter engine.model.rejected_mutations is incremented

Scenario: The bar ceiling evicts instead of growing without bound
  Given maxBars = 200000 and a full store
  When 1 000 more bars are appended
  Then the store still holds 200 000 bars, the oldest 1 000 are evicted
  And indexShift = 1000 is reported so every anchor can be rebased
```

## Technical notes / design
Precision (§3.3 note, the single most error-prone decision in the engine): OHLC are **integer ticks** in `Int32Array` relative to `priceOrigin`; float prices are never stored. Float32 at BTC magnitudes loses sub-tick precision, which shows up as candle wicks jittering during zoom.

Ring buffer: `head`/`tail` indices over a power-of-two capacity with masked indexing; logical index `i` maps to `(head + i) & (cap - 1)`. Growth doubles capacity and re-linearises (one copy, amortised O(1)). Eviction moves `head` — it never memmoves.

`prepend` cannot use the ring's front cheaply when capacity is tight, so it reallocates with the new bars leading, and returns `indexShift` so consumers rebase. Consumers that store indices (`drawings`, `hitIndex`, `picks`) subscribe to `indexShift` events; the design deliberately makes shifts explicit rather than hiding them.

Allocation discipline (§3.2 rule 4): mutations must not allocate in the hot path. Subarray views are cached per store; formatting caches are invalidated by range, not rebuilt. A dedicated allocation-counter test asserts zero GC-triggering allocations across a 1 000-mutation run.

Validation contract: `Number.isFinite` on every float column, `priceLevel` within `INT32` bounds, `time` monotonically non-decreasing for `append` (out-of-order -> reject and count, do not sort silently — silent sorting hides feed bugs).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring wrap at capacity boundary; doubling growth; eviction with `indexShift`; prefix-sum construction and lookup; `timeToIndex` on exact/between/before/after; rejection matrix (NaN, Infinity, non-monotone time, length mismatch).
- **Property** (fast-check, must hold over 10 000 cases): for any random bar series and any sequence of append/patch/prepend, `timeToIndex(indexToTime(i)) === i`; the multiset of `(time, ohlcv)` after a prepend equals the union of the two inputs; `offsets` is non-decreasing and `offsets[n] === cellCount`.
- **Perf micro-bench**: 1 M appends <=120 ms; allocation-counter test asserting zero hot-path allocations.
- **Integration**: store + worker transport against a recorded fixture session — snapshot then deltas then a sequence-gap replace, asserting no blank frame.
- Coverage >=90 % (this is pure logic; the higher bar is cheap and the blast radius is the whole engine).

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. This is the engine's **memory-safety chokepoint** — every hostile value entering from the decoder is stopped here.
- **Tampering**: bounds- and finiteness-validated before any indexed write; `priceLevel`/`barIndex` range-checked against the store's declared extent; a corrupt `offsets` array (non-monotone) is rejected wholesale rather than partially applied.
- **Denial of service**: `maxBars` and per-store byte ceilings cap allocation; growth is doubling-with-ceiling, never proportional to an attacker-declared length field. A declared element count larger than the ceiling is rejected before allocation, not after.
- **Information disclosure**: none — nothing here is persisted or logged beyond counters.
Requires the `security` label; covered by E11-X01 and by the fuzz corpus in E11-X02.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI surface — this ticket ships engine internals. Two binding constraints still apply from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1, and the reviewer must check them:
- The public query surface for "current visible window + current focused unit" that the DOM mirror (E11-S13) consumes must exist and be frame-synchronous; it may not be bolted on later.
- Nothing here may make the DOM mirror unable to stay in sync with what is drawn (desync is called out explicitly as never acceptable in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4).

## Performance notes
Serves budget #7 (frontend memory) and the §7 memory table: BarStore 3.2 MB, FootprintStore 14.4 MB, glyph runs 9.6 MB for the 100k-bar/4 h case. Hard requirement: mutation application stays inside the **4 ms/frame** data-mutation drain of §3.2 rule 3 — anything not drained waits for the next frame. Micro-benchmarks recorded in the B7 report.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.model.rejected_mutations{reason}`, `engine.model.evictions`, `engine.model.reallocations`, `engine.model.bytes{store}`. `bytes` feeds the `gpuMemoryMbEstimate` field of `FrameStats` and hence SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-T02** — stores live inside the render worker and are mutated by `data` messages.
- **E17** (via `packages/protocol`) — the decoded payload shapes the stores ingest.
- Blocks **E11-S15** (memory governor/paging), **E11-S08** (hit index), **E12** (series read these stores).

title: Ingest design-system theme tokens, colour LUTs and density modes into the engine
body:
## Context
The engine draws in GL, where a colour is four floats, while the product's source of truth for colour, type and spacing is the design-system token set shipped by **E05** (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`). Without a single ingestion path every renderer would hard-code colours, themes would drift and the high-contrast theme would be impossible to verify.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 additionally fixes three non-negotiable rules that this Task makes structurally enforceable rather than a review convention: colour is never the sole carrier of meaning, estimated data carries a hatch pattern plus an "(estimated)" label, and **density modes (`comfortable` | `compact` | `dense`) change cell padding, font size class and LOD thresholds together as one coherent switch** — not three independent settings a caller can desynchronise.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/theme/ThemeIngest.ts` — maps the E05 token JSON (`color.chart.*`, `color.surface.*`, `color.text.*`, `font.mono`, `elevation.*`, spacing scale) into a flat, frozen `EngineTheme` of premultiplied `Float32Array` RGBA plus scalar metrics. Resolution happens **once per theme change**, never per frame.
- `src/theme/ColorLut.ts` — generates 256-entry `Uint8Array` RGBA lookup textures for continuous encodings (delta ramp, heatmap intensity, imbalance intensity). Consumers sample the LUT; they never compute a colour in a shader from a token.
- `src/theme/Density.ts` — the `DensityMode` switch: one enum drives cell padding, font size class **and** the LOD thresholds of E11-S12 together (§5 rule 5). Exposed as `chart.setDensity(mode)`.
- `setTheme` command wired through the E11-T02 worker protocol; the whole scene is marked dirty and redrawn within one frame (SCR-031's "styling is a uniform/shader change, not a data reload" requirement).
- Three themes supported from day one: `dark` (default), `light`, `high-contrast`.
- Hatch/pattern registry for the `(estimated)` encoding (CMP-227's engine-side counterpart) so later Epics (E20, E22, E25) attach a pattern id rather than inventing one.
- Config keys: `theme.name`, `theme.density`, `theme.reducedMotion`, `theme.colorBlindSafePalette`.

## Out of scope
- Authoring the tokens themselves — **E05**; this Task consumes them.
- The settings UI that switches theme/density (SCR-031 Appearance tab) — E15/E10 chrome; this Task exposes the engine API it calls.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection — open item **O5** of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16, due at M8, validated by the accessibility pass; this Task only proves a palette can be swapped without code changes.
- Heatmap-specific LUT tuning — E21.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch is a uniform change, not a reload
  Given a chart with 100k bars and an active crosshair in the dark theme
  When chart.setTheme("light") is called
  Then every layer redraws in light-theme colours within one frame
  And no data is refetched and no GPU vertex buffer is re-uploaded

Scenario: Density is one coherent switch
  Given density is "comfortable"
  When chart.setDensity("dense") is called
  Then cell padding, the font size class and the LOD thresholds all change together
  And no API exists that can change one of the three without the others

Scenario: High-contrast theme meets the contrast floor
  Given the high-contrast theme is active
  When every foreground/background token pair used by the engine is measured
  Then each pair meets at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for non-text UI components
  And a token pair failing the floor fails the CI contrast test

Scenario: Unknown token fails loudly at ingest, never at frame time
  Given a theme payload missing "color.chart.crosshair"
  When ThemeIngest resolves it
  Then it throws a descriptive ENGINE_THEME_INVALID error naming the missing key
  And no partially-resolved theme is ever installed into the scene
```

## Technical notes / design
`EngineTheme` is a frozen object of typed arrays so the frame path performs zero allocation and zero string lookups:

```ts
interface EngineTheme {
  readonly name: "dark" | "light" | "high-contrast";
  readonly density: DensityMode;
  readonly rgba: Readonly<Record<ThemeSlot, Float32Array>>; // premultiplied, length 4
  readonly luts: Readonly<Record<LutId, Uint8Array>>;       // 256 * 4 bytes
  readonly metrics: Readonly<{ cellPadPx: number; fontSizeClass: 0|1|2; hairlinePx: number }>;
  readonly lodBias: number; // folded into E11-S12's thresholds
}
```

LUT generation interpolates in **OkLab**, not sRGB, so a diverging delta ramp has perceptually even steps and no muddy mid-band; the result is converted back to sRGB bytes once at generation time. LUTs are uploaded as `LUMINANCE_ALPHA`-free `RGBA8` 256×1 textures and bound to a dedicated texture unit reserved by the GL backend (E11-S02).

Density -> LOD coupling: `Density.apply(mode)` returns `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` and E11-S12 adds `lodBias` to its `barSpacing` thresholds, so `dense` steps down later (more detail retained) and `comfortable` earlier. The coupling lives in one function so there is exactly one place to reason about it.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: token -> `Float32Array` mapping incl. premultiplication; missing-key rejection; LUT monotonicity and endpoint exactness; OkLab round-trip; density triple-coupling (asserting the three values change together); frozen-object immutability.
- **Contrast test** (CI, automated): every foreground/background slot pair used by the engine measured against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text) for all three themes — a failing pair fails the build.
- **Golden image** (via E11-T08): axes + crosshair + grid rendered in `dark`, `light` and `high-contrast`, and in all three density modes.
- **Perf**: assert `setTheme` costs <=1 frame and allocates zero bytes in the frame path afterwards (allocation-counter test).
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes

title: Provide a degraded-2d Canvas fallback when WebGL2 is unavailable
body:
## Context
Requirement **R9** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`: the engine "runs in a `degraded-2d` mode (candles + axes + lines only) if WebGL2 is unavailable". SCR-048 makes the user-facing half explicit — the "WebGL-unavailable fallback message names the fallback path" — and the Epic's acceptance criteria are blunt about the failure mode to avoid: the user is "told which capabilities are reduced and why, **never shown a blank canvas**".

This is not hypothetical. WebGL2 is disabled by policy on some managed Windows fleets, blocked by GPU driver blocklists, and unavailable in software-rendering fallbacks after a driver crash. The owner runs the terminal through an Electron shell on Windows, so a driver blocklist hit is a realistic Tuesday, not a corner case.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/render/Canvas2dBackend.ts` implementing the same `RenderBackend` interface as the WebGL2 backend (E11-S02), so the scene graph, viewport, layout, LOD and interaction layers are entirely unaware which backend is active.
- Supported in `degraded-2d`: **candles, axes, gridlines, crosshair, line series, order/position lines and drawings**. Text via Canvas 2D `fillText` (§3.7 fallback). Footprint limited to **L2/L3** (coloured cell or hidden, no cell text).
- Not supported and explicitly disclosed: heatmap, bubbles, profile shading, any GPU-only effect.
- **Capability probe** (built in E11-S02) selects the `RenderProfile`; this Task adds the `degraded-2d` profile and the selection rules: no WebGL2 -> `degraded-2d`; WebGL2 present but a required extension missing -> `degraded-gl`; otherwise `full`.
- **Capability disclosure UI contract**: the engine reports `{ profile, reducedCapabilities: string[], reason }` so SCR-048 can name what is reduced and why, and SCR-118 (renderer settings) can offer a manual override.
- Manual override `renderer.forceProfile` for support and for testing — the same switch QA uses in E11-Q07's GPU matrix.
- Frame budget in this mode is deliberately relaxed to **>=30 fps at 20k bars**; it is a usable-degraded mode, not a parity mode, and saying so prevents a pointless optimisation effort later.

## Out of scope
- WebGPU backend — an explicit future seam only (§3.4), not built.
- Bringing footprint cell text, heatmap or bubbles to Canvas 2D — out of scope by design; those surfaces are disclosed as reduced.
- The SCR-048 error-state UI itself — E10/E15 chrome, consuming this Task's capability report.
- Context-loss recovery within WebGL2 — E11-S02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No WebGL2 degrades instead of failing
  Given a runtime whose capability probe reports no WebGL2 support
  When a chart is mounted
  Then the degraded-2d profile is selected and candles, axes, gridlines and lines render through Canvas 2D
  And no blank canvas and no thrown error is ever presented to the user

Scenario: Reduced capabilities are named, not merely implied
  Given degraded-2d is active
  When the capability report is surfaced on SCR-048
  Then it names each reduced capability and the reason in plain language
  And a link to renderer settings offers a manual override

Scenario: The backend swap is invisible to the rest of the engine
  Given the same scene, viewport and interaction sequence
  When it is executed against the WebGL2 backend and the Canvas 2D backend
  Then both produce the same viewport state, the same pick results and the same DOM-mirror content
  And no code outside src/render branches on the active backend

Scenario: Footprint degrades to colour-only rather than disappearing
  Given footprint is enabled and degraded-2d is active
  When a frame is rendered
  Then cells render at L2 as coloured cells with no text
  And the aggregation and reduced-detail disclosure states that cell text is unavailable in this mode

Scenario: The degraded mode remains usable
  Given degraded-2d with 20,000 bars loaded
  When the user pans continuously for 10 seconds
  Then the frame rate stays at or above 30 fps
  And pan, zoom, crosshair and the keyboard data cursor all behave identically to the full profile
```

## Technical notes / design
The `RenderBackend` interface is the whole design, and it is defined in E11-S02 before either implementation exists precisely so the 2D path is a peer rather than a bolt-on:

```ts
interface RenderBackend {
  readonly profile: RenderProfile;          // "full" | "degraded-gl" | "degraded-2d"
  readonly capabilities: Capabilities;      // what this backend can actually draw
  resize(w: number, h: number, dpr: number): void;
  beginFrame(theme: EngineTheme): void;
  drawBatch(batch: DrawBatch): void;         // batches are backend-agnostic
  endFrame(): FrameStats;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

`DrawBatch` is expressed in primitives both backends can honour (quads, lines, polylines, text runs); GPU-only batch kinds declare `requires: Capability[]` and are skipped with a disclosure entry rather than silently dropped — a skipped batch with no disclosure is the exact failure mode ("silently wrong chart") this design forbids.

Canvas 2D performance technique: batch by style to minimise state changes, use a single `Path2D` per style bucket, and draw candle bodies as a single `fill()` per colour bucket rather than per candle. That is what makes 20k bars at 30 fps achievable in 2D at all.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: profile-selection rules for each probe outcome; capability-report contents; batch `requires` filtering and disclosure emission.
- **Cross-backend equivalence** (the headline test): the same scripted scene and interaction sequence run against both backends must agree on viewport state, pick results and DOM-mirror content.
- **Golden image**: candles, axes, grid, crosshair and lines in `degraded-2d` for each theme, compared to a `degraded-2d` reference (not to the WebGL reference — the two are legitimately different renderings).
- **Integration**: WebGL2 forcibly disabled (`--disable-webgl2` / stubbed `getContext`) asserting a usable chart and a correct SCR-048 disclosure.
- **Perf**: >=30 fps at 20k bars panning for 10 s.
- **E2E**: manual override via `renderer.forceProfile` round-trips, used as the mechanism for **E11-Q07**'s GPU matrix.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- The degraded mode must be **fully equivalent in accessibility**: the DOM mirror, keyboard data cursor, live regions and the SCR-045 table are main-thread DOM and are entirely unaffected by which backend draws pixels. This is asserted by the cross-backend equivalence test, so an a11y regression cannot hide in the fallback path.
- Capability disclosure is **text**, not an icon or a colour: SCR-048's `role="alert"` region with plain-language copy and a copyable correlation id.
- A blank canvas is the worst possible outcome for every user and a completely silent one for a screen-reader user — hence the "never a blank canvas" acceptance criterion.

## Performance notes
Deliberately relaxed: >=30 fps at 20k bars, versus >=60 fps at 100k bars for the full profile. This mode is excluded from the B1–B10 gates (which assume WebGL2) and has its own single benchmark, so a machine without a GPU cannot fail the main perf gate and a slow 2D path cannot hide behind it either.

## Observability
`ready` message carries `{ profile, capabilities, reason }`. Errors: `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2` (informational, recoverable — it selects the fallback rather than failing). Counter `engine.render.profile` reported in `frame` stats and on SCR-046, so every perf report states which backend produced it. Analytics `chart.render_profile_selected` owned by the app layer.

title: Make the engine benchmark harness a required CI check with enforced baselines
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §13 names the single mitigation that makes E11 survivable as a critical-path Epic: "**benchmark harness in CI from day 1 so regressions surface same-day**". Performance in a render engine is not a feature you add at the end; it is a property you lose one 3 % regression at a time, and the only defence is a gate that fails the build.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 already specifies the harness completely: benchmarks live in `packages/chart-engine/bench`, run headless on a **dedicated CI runner**, replay a **deterministic fixture** for 20 s, report p50/p95 frame time, draw calls, uploaded bytes and peak memory, and are **required checks on PRs touching the package**. This Task builds it and, critically, turns it on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/bench` — the harness: Playwright + Chromium with a fixed GPU flag set, deterministic fixtures from `packages/fixtures`, 20 s per scenario, **3 repetitions** with the median of p95 taken as the result (a single run of a GPU benchmark is noise).
- Scenarios implemented in this Task — the ones whose subject matter exists by Sprint 07: **B1** (100k candles, pan at 1000 px/s, <=12 ms, <=8 draw calls), **B2** (zoom sweep 0.1->50 px/bar, <=14 ms, <=6 LOD changes), **B5** (combined scene, <=16.7 ms, <=40 draw calls), **B6** (4 synchronised charts, <=16.7 ms aggregate, shared-worker CPU <=70 % of one core), **B9** (cold init to first frame, <=900 ms, atlas from cache <=5 ms), **B10** (30-min memory soak, peak <=600 MB, growth <=5 %).
- Scenario **stubs with registered gates** for B3, B4, B7, B8 — owned by E18, E21, E17 and E14 respectively; registering them here means those Epics inherit a working harness instead of building one each.
- **Baseline storage and update policy**: baselines committed as JSON; a regression **>10 %** against the stored baseline fails the check (§13); baselines are updated **only** by an explicit reviewer-approved commit that states the cause. The Epic applies a tighter **5 %** working threshold for hard budgets per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §8 — the harness enforces the tighter of the two.
- **Required-check wiring**: GitHub branch protection on `packages/chart-engine` paths; a dedicated, pinned CI runner (shared runners have unusable GPU variance, and saying this in the ticket prevents a well-meaning "let's just use the standard runner" PR).
- Per-stage attribution using the nine frame stages of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, so a regression report names the stage, not just the total.
- Artefact output: JSON results, a trend chart and a PR comment table (before/after/delta per scenario).

## Out of scope
- Backend API/WS load testing (k6/Locust) — E46 and the platform Epics; this is the **frontend engine** harness only.
- The benchmark **fixtures** themselves beyond the seeded synthetic generator — extended from **E06**'s M0 harness, which this Task builds on rather than replaces.
- Perf sign-off as a QA activity — **E11-Q03**; this Task provides the numbers, Q03 interprets and signs off on them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The benchmark check blocks a regressing PR
  Given a stored baseline for scenario B5 of 15.0 ms p95
  When a PR raises B5 p95 to 16.0 ms, a 6.7 % regression
  Then the required check fails and the PR cannot merge
  And the PR comment names B5, the before and after values, the delta and the worst-regressing frame stage

Scenario: Results are stable enough to gate on
  Given the harness runs on the dedicated runner
  When scenario B1 is executed three times in a row with no code change
  Then the median-of-p95 values vary by less than 3 %
  And that variance figure is published so the gate threshold is demonstrably above the noise floor

Scenario: A deliberate baseline change is possible but never silent
  Given an intentional change trades 8 % of B2 frame time for a correctness fix
  When the author updates the baseline
  Then the update is a separate, explicitly reviewed commit stating the cause
  And an unexplained baseline change is rejected in review

Scenario: Every gate from the design document is enforced or explicitly deferred
  Given the harness configuration is inspected
  Then B1, B2, B5, B6, B9 and B10 are enforced with their primary and secondary gates
  And B3, B4, B7 and B8 are registered as stubs naming the Epic that will enable them

Scenario: Benchmarks are deterministic
  Given the same fixture and the same commit
  When the harness runs on two different days
  Then the same bars, trades and timestamps are replayed
  And no wall-clock time, random seed or network call influences the result
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why median-of-p95 over three runs.** GPU benchmarks have a fat right tail from driver scheduling and thermal effects. A single p95 varies by 5–10 % run to run — more than the thing we are trying to detect. Three runs and a median collapses that to under 3 %, which is what makes a 5–10 % gate meaningful. The stability scenario above exists to prove this claim continuously rather than assume it.

**Determinism.** Fixtures are pre-recorded, time is driven by a virtual clock, and the harness injects frames rather than waiting on `rAF` wall time. No network, no randomness without a fixed seed, no wall-clock branches.

**Runner pinning.** A dedicated runner with a fixed GPU, fixed driver version and fixed Chromium build, pinned in the workflow. The driver version is part of the baseline record, so a driver upgrade invalidates baselines explicitly instead of appearing as a mysterious 20 % regression across every scenario at once.

**Per-stage attribution** uses the `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` spans placed at the §4.3 stage boundaries (decode, model update, layout, viewport, cull, decimate, batch, GL submit, present), so the PR comment can say "batch stage +1.2 ms" instead of "B5 got slower".

## Test plan
- **Self-test**: the harness is tested against a deliberately regressed build (a synthetic 10 % stall injected) asserting the check fails; and against an unchanged build asserting it passes — a gate that has never been seen to fail is not a gate.
- **Stability test**: 3× repeat run reporting variance, published as an artefact each run.
- **Determinism test**: identical results across two runs on different days from the same commit.
- **Unit**: baseline comparison arithmetic, threshold selection (tighter of 5 %/10 %), PR-comment rendering, stage attribution parsing.
- Coverage >=85 % on the harness's own code — the harness is production code for the purposes of the coverage gate.

## Security notes
Data classification: **synthetic fixture data only** — no real account data, no credentials, no PII ever enters a benchmark fixture, and this is asserted by a fixture-content check so nobody "temporarily" records a real session into `packages/fixtures`.

Supply-chain note: the harness pins Playwright, the Chromium build and the GPU driver version; those pins are covered by Dependabot and npm audit like any other dependency. CI artefacts (JSON results, trend charts) contain only timing data and are safe to publish on PRs.

The dedicated runner executes repository code, so it is subject to the same untrusted-fork restrictions as any other self-hosted runner: benchmarks run on PRs from forks only after maintainer approval. Reviewed in **E11-X02**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the harness itself — it produces numbers, not UI. Two adjacent requirements are worth stating so they are not lost: the benchmark scenarios must run with the DOM mirror **active** (so its <=1 ms/frame cost is inside the measured budget rather than excluded from it), and the a11y automated checks (axe-core) are a separate required check owned by **E11-Q05**, not folded into this one.

## Performance notes
This Task **is** the performance gate. It enforces budgets #1 and #2 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and gates B1/B2/B5/B6/B9/B10 from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13. Regression threshold: the tighter of 5 % (Epic working threshold, §8 of the perf standard) and 10 % (§13). The harness itself must complete a full run in under 25 minutes so it can plausibly be a required check on every PR; scenarios run in parallel across runner slots where the GPU allows.

## Observability
Results published as CI artefacts and as a PR comment table. A long-run trend series (per scenario, per commit) is retained so slow drift — the regression pattern that no single PR gate catches — is visible; a 15 % drift over 20 commits triggers a review even though no individual PR crossed the threshold. Runner GPU/driver/Chromium versions recorded in every result record.

title: Feed the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay with telemetry and a copy snapshot
body:
## Context
When the owner reports "the chart felt slow around 14:30", the difference between a one-hour investigation and a five-minute one is whether the report arrives with numbers attached. **SCR-046** is that mechanism: a `Ctrl+Shift+D` overlay showing FPS, frame-time p50/p95, draw calls, GPU memory, buffer uploads/s, WS message rate, dropped frames, and a **"copy diagnostics" button used in bug reports**.

The engine already computes all of this for the benchmark harness (E11-T06). This Task exposes the same numbers at runtime, under a strict cost ceiling — SCR-046 requires the overlay itself to cost **<=0.5 ms per frame** and to sample at **2 Hz, not per frame**, because a diagnostics panel that perturbs the thing it measures is worse than none.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Extend the `frame` worker->main message (E11-T02, §6) to a full stats payload: `fps`, frame time p50/p95, draw calls, triangles, uploaded bytes/s, LOD levels per layer, GPU memory estimate, render profile, dropped-frame count, decode p95, and **WS->pixel latency** (the end-to-end number SCR-046 calls for).
- Sampling: **1 Hz in production, 2 Hz when the overlay is open, full per-frame in bench mode** — three modes, one code path, selected by a flag.
- Per-stage timings from the nine `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 stages, so the overlay attributes cost to a stage rather than showing one opaque total.
- **`copyDiagnostics()`** producing a structured, pasteable snapshot: engine version, commit SHA, render profile, capability report, theme/density, symbol/interval, visible bar count, the full stats block, the last 20 engine error events with codes, and the backend **correlation id** carried on the WS envelope.
- Correlation with the backend: the WS envelope's span id is included so a client-side slow frame can be joined to a backend trace.
- Threshold colouring **paired with text** ("below budget") per SCR-046's sign-off checklist — never colour alone.
- Overlay hidden by default, enabled from SCR-118 (renderer settings), toggled with `Ctrl+Shift+D`.
- Components: CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.

## Out of scope
- The overlay's visual design — **E11-D02**'s diagnostics section; this Task supplies the data contract it binds to.
- Backend system-health data (`system` topic) — E10/E44 own the `SystemHealthTile` data source; the overlay composes both.
- Uploading diagnostics anywhere — copy-to-clipboard only, by explicit user action. The engine performs no I/O.
- Prometheus/Grafana metrics — backend observability, E44/E46.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The overlay costs less than it measures
  Given the diagnostics overlay is open during the B5 benchmark scene
  When frame time is compared with the overlay open and closed
  Then the overlay adds at most 0.5 ms per frame
  And it samples at 2 Hz, not once per frame

Scenario: A copied snapshot is sufficient for triage without follow-up questions
  Given a user presses "copy diagnostics" during a slow period
  When the clipboard contents are inspected
  Then they contain engine version, commit SHA, render profile, capabilities, symbol, interval, visible bars, the full stats block, the last 20 error events and the backend correlation id
  And pasting it into an issue requires no further information to begin investigation

Scenario: Thresholds are never colour-only
  Given frame time exceeds its budget
  When the overlay displays it
  Then the value is accompanied by the text "above budget"
  And the meaning is fully available to a user who cannot distinguish the colours

Scenario: Sampling mode follows context
  Given the overlay is closed in a production build
  Then stats are sampled at 1 Hz
  And when the overlay is opened sampling rises to 2 Hz, and in bench mode it is per-frame

Scenario: Client and backend traces can be joined
  Given a frame rendered from a WS message carrying span id X
  When the diagnostics snapshot is copied
  Then it contains span id X
  And the backend trace for X can be retrieved without correlating by timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
Stats are accumulated in a **pre-allocated ring buffer** in the worker (600 samples ~ 10 s at 60 fps) and reduced to percentiles at the sampling cadence, so per-frame cost is a few array writes and nothing else. Percentiles come from the ring, not from a growing array — that is what keeps the "measuring costs nothing" property true.

```ts
interface FrameStats {
  fps: number; frameMsP50: number; frameMsP95: number;
  drawCalls: number; triangles: number; uploadedBytesPerSec: number;
  lod: Record<LayerId, number>; gpuMemoryMb: number;
  profile: RenderProfile; droppedFrames: number;
  decodeMsP95: number; wsToPixelMsP95: number;
  stages: Record<StageId, number>;   // the nine 4.3 stages
}
```

**WS->pixel latency** is measured by carrying the message's receive timestamp through the decode -> model -> batch -> present path and differencing at present. It is the only number here that crosses the worker boundary in both directions, and it is the one that actually answers "is it the network or the renderer".

`copyDiagnostics()` returns Markdown, because its destination is a GitHub issue.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring-buffer percentile correctness against a reference implementation; sampling-mode selection; snapshot serialisation completeness (asserted field by field against the SCR-046 required list); Markdown escaping of symbol names.
- **Perf**: overlay open vs closed during B5, asserting <=0.5 ms delta; assertion that stats accumulation allocates zero bytes per frame.
- **Integration**: WS->pixel latency measured against a fixture with known injected delays, asserting the reported figure tracks the injected one.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the overlay; assertion that values update **politely**, not assertively (SCR-046's explicit requirement, since an assertive diagnostics panel would flood a screen reader); assertion that every threshold indication has a text equivalent.
- **E2E**: `Ctrl+Shift+D` toggle, pin-open behaviour, copy-to-clipboard round-trip.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **diagnostic telemetry**. The relevant threat, named in the Epic's STRIDE surface, is **information disclosure**: SCR-046 is designed to be screenshotted and pasted into issues, so its contents become as public as the issue tracker.

Controls: the snapshot contains **no account identifiers, no API keys, no order or position data, no user identity** — only engine timing, capability and error information plus an opaque correlation id. The correlation id is opaque by construction (a random span id, not an encoding of anything). A test asserts the snapshot's field set matches an allowlist, so a future contributor cannot casually add "current account" to a payload designed to be pasted in public.

Copy happens only on explicit user gesture; nothing is transmitted anywhere. Reviewed under **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-046's own a11y requirements, which this Task's data contract must support:
- The overlay is a **text panel, not a canvas**, and can be pinned open and read as a static table.
- Values update **politely** so a screen reader is not flooded — the 2 Hz cadence is an accessibility control as much as a performance one.
- **Threshold colouring is paired with text** ("below budget" / "above budget"); colour is never the sole carrier.
- The copy control is a real, keyboard-operable button with a confirmation announcement ("Diagnostics copied").
- Design source: **E11-D02**.

## Performance notes
Hard ceiling from SCR-046: **<=0.5 ms per frame** for the overlay, sampled at **2 Hz**. Stats accumulation in the worker is allocation-free and costs <=0.05 ms per frame. Production sampling at 1 Hz is cheap enough to leave permanently on, which is what makes the numbers available when a user reports a problem rather than only when someone thought to enable them.

## Observability
This Task *is* the observability surface for the engine. It exposes the counters and error codes defined across E11: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN`, `ENGINE_FRAME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, `ENGINE_THEME_INVALID`, `ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID`. Analytics: `diagnostics.overlay_toggled`, `diagnostics.snapshot_copied` (per SCR-046).

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies

title: Build a deterministic golden-image regression harness running on SwiftShader
body:
## Context
Unit tests prove a transform returns the right number; they cannot prove a chart looks right. Rendering defects — a half-pixel axis offset, a gridline drawn under instead of over, text baseline drift after a font change, a theme token wired to the wrong slot — are invisible to every other test layer and obvious in a pixel diff.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §14 requires golden-image tests per layer and per theme at **<=0.1 % pixel difference**. The engineering problem is determinism: real GPUs produce different pixels on different drivers, so goldens captured on a developer's RTX 3060 will never match CI. The answer is **SwiftShader**, Chromium's software rasteriser, which is bit-identical across machines — the standard trade of absolute fidelity for absolute reproducibility.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/test/golden` — the harness: Playwright + Chromium launched with `--use-gl=swiftshader --disable-gpu-sandbox --deterministic-mode`, fixed viewport, fixed DPR per case, virtual clock.
- Golden coverage required by §14: **axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD, `degraded-2d`**, each in **`dark`, `light` and `high-contrast`** themes and in all three density modes.
- Comparison with a perceptual threshold (`pixelmatch` at <=0.1 % differing pixels) plus a **diff artefact** (before/after/diff triptych) attached to the PR on failure — a golden test that fails without showing you the image is a test people learn to ignore.
- Update workflow: `pnpm golden:update` regenerates, and the regenerated images must be reviewed **as images** in the PR. An update commit touching more than 5 goldens requires an explanatory note, so a "just update the goldens" reflex cannot quietly absorb a real regression.
- Deterministic inputs: fixed fixture, fixed seed, virtual clock, fonts loaded from a pinned local file rather than the system font stack (system fonts differ per machine and are the most common source of spurious diffs).
- Runs as a **required check** on PRs touching `packages/chart-engine`.
- Shares the Playwright infrastructure and fixture plumbing with the benchmark harness (E11-T06).

## Out of scope
- Benchmarking — **E11-T06**; goldens run on SwiftShader where performance is meaningless by design.
- Visual regression of the React chrome (toolbars, dialogs) — the design-system Storybook/Chromatic pipeline in **E05**.
- Cross-browser and real-GPU rendering verification — **E11-Q07**'s exploratory GPU matrix, which is a human activity precisely because it cannot be made deterministic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Golden images are reproducible across machines
  Given the golden suite is run on a developer machine and on the CI runner
  When the produced images are compared
  Then they are byte-identical, because SwiftShader rasterises deterministically
  And no golden is captured from a hardware GPU

Scenario: A rendering regression fails the check with visible evidence
  Given a change shifts the price axis by half a pixel
  When the golden suite runs
  Then the check fails on the axis goldens
  And a before/after/diff triptych is attached to the PR for each failing case

Scenario: Every layer, theme and density is covered
  Given the golden manifest is inspected
  Then axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD and degraded-2d are covered
  And each appears in dark, light and high-contrast themes

Scenario: Golden updates are reviewed as images, not rubber-stamped
  Given an intentional visual change updates 7 goldens
  When the PR is opened
  Then the regenerated images are rendered in the PR for review
  And the update carries an explanatory note because it exceeds the 5-golden threshold

Scenario: The suite is fast enough to gate every PR
  Given the full golden suite runs in CI
  Then it completes within 10 minutes
  And it runs in parallel with the unit suite rather than after it
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why SwiftShader and not a real GPU.** A hardware GPU gives fidelity but not reproducibility: driver versions, vendor extensions and even GPU temperature change the last bit of a blend. SwiftShader gives reproducibility but not fidelity — it will not catch a driver-specific bug. Both properties are needed, so they are split across two mechanisms: SwiftShader goldens as a **deterministic gate** (this Task), and a human **GPU matrix exploratory** (E11-Q07) for driver reality. Stating the split here prevents the recurring "why don't the goldens catch GPU bugs" question.

**Determinism checklist**, all of which must hold or diffs become noise: fixed viewport and DPR per case; fonts from a pinned local file (never the system stack); virtual clock (no animation captured mid-flight); fixed fixture and seed; animations disabled or advanced to a fixed frame; `prefers-reduced-motion` forced on during capture.

**Threshold.** `pixelmatch` with `threshold: 0.1` per-pixel and a failure at >0.1 % of pixels differing — tolerant of a single anti-aliased edge pixel, intolerant of a half-pixel layout shift.

The manifest is data (`golden.manifest.ts`), so adding a case is a data change, and coverage of the §14 matrix is verifiable by reading one file.

## Test plan
- **Self-test**: inject a deliberate 1 px offset and assert the harness fails; run unchanged and assert it passes — the same "has this gate ever fired" discipline as E11-T06.
- **Determinism test**: same commit, two runs, byte-identical output.
- **Manifest-coverage test**: assert the manifest covers every (layer × theme × density) combination required by §14; a missing combination fails the build rather than being noticed a year later.
- **Unit**: diff-threshold arithmetic; triptych generation; update-workflow guard rails (the 5-golden note requirement).
- Runtime assertion: full suite <=10 minutes.

## Security notes
Data classification: **synthetic fixture data only**; goldens are images of generated market data and contain no real account, order or user information — asserted by the same fixture-content check as E11-T06.

Supply chain: Playwright, Chromium and `pixelmatch` are pinned and covered by Dependabot/npm audit; the SwiftShader build ships with pinned Chromium rather than being fetched separately. Golden PNGs are committed binaries, so the review requirement ("reviewed as images") doubles as a control against a binary being swapped for something unrelated. Reviewed under **E11-X02**.

## Accessibility notes
Golden images are how the **high-contrast theme** stops being a claim and becomes a verified artefact: it is a first-class golden dimension, so a token change that quietly breaks high-contrast fails CI. The automated contrast-ratio test in E11-T04 checks the token pairs; the goldens check that the pairs actually reach the pixels. Neither substitutes for the manual screen-reader and low-vision passes in **E11-Q05**.

## Performance notes
Not a performance gate (SwiftShader timings are meaningless). The only performance requirement is on the harness itself: <=10 minutes for the full suite, parallelised across runner slots, so it can be a required check on every PR without becoming the reason people stop opening PRs.

## Observability
Diff artefacts (triptychs) published on every failure; a golden-count and manifest-coverage summary published on every run so drift in coverage is visible. Failures name the layer, theme and density of each failing case, not just the file name.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

- Shares Playwright/fixture infrastructure with **E11-T06** and is consumed by **E11-S10**, **E11-S11**, **E11-S12**, **E11-T05** for their visual assertions, and inherited by **E18**/**E19**/**E21**.

title: Freeze the public engine API, document it and amend the ADR for open item O2
body:
## Context
Six Epics compile against `packages/chart-engine` — E12 series, E13 indicators, E14 drawings, E15 layouts, E18 footprint, E21 DOM/heatmap — and they start in R1 and R2 with no opportunity to absorb churn in a shared interface. `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10's interface-first rule made the API a **first** deliverable (E11-T01); this Task makes it a **finished** one: frozen, documented and versioned, so downstream Epics build against a contract rather than a moving target.

It also closes the Epic's documentation obligations: `26-chart-engine-design.md` must describe what shipped rather than what was proposed, and open item **O2** (SDF atlas size and glyph set), answered empirically by E11-K01 and E11-S11, must be recorded as an **ADR amendment** — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires every spike's decision to land as an ADR, including a decision to defer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **API freeze**: review the surface of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 against what shipped — `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin` — and mark it stable at **v1.0.0** of the package.
- **Semver policy** for the package recorded in its README: a breaking change to the plugin interface is a major bump and requires a migration note plus sign-off from every consuming Epic's lead. Experimental surfaces live under an `unstable_` prefix and are explicitly outside the freeze.
- **API-extract check in CI**: a generated API report (`api-extractor`-style `.api.md`) committed to the repo; any change to the public surface produces a diff in that file, so an accidental public-surface change is impossible to merge unnoticed.
- **TSDoc on every exported symbol**, with a documented example per plugin interface — the plugin interfaces are what E12/E13/E14/E18/E21 implement, so an undocumented one costs five teams.
- **Package README**: architecture overview, quick start, the plugin authoring guide, the config-key reference (every `lod.*`, `memory.*`, `theme.*`, `a11y.*`, `renderer.*` key defined across E11), and the engine error-code table.
- **`26-chart-engine-design.md` reconciliation**: update §3, §6, §7, §8 and §13 to shipped behaviour; where the implementation diverged from the design, record the divergence and its reason rather than silently editing the design to match.
- **ADR amendment for O2**: amend `ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md` with the measured glyph set, atlas size, generation cost and cache strategy from E11-K01/E11-S11, closing the open item in §16.
- Storybook coverage check for the chart-primitive components the Epic ships: CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226.
- Handoff session with the E12/E13/E14/E15/E18/E21 leads walking the plugin seam and the config surface.

## Out of scope
- Publishing the package externally — it is internal to the monorepo; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 explicitly rules out third-party distribution.
- Freezing internal (non-exported) structure — internals stay free to change; that freedom is the point of having a narrow public surface.
- Resolving open items O3, O4 and O5 — owned by M4, M5 and M8 in later Epics (E21, E13, E11-Q05 respectively).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The public surface cannot change without a visible diff
  Given the committed API report for packages/chart-engine
  When a PR adds an exported symbol or changes an exported signature
  Then the API report file shows a diff and the CI check fails until it is committed
  And an unintended public-surface change cannot merge unnoticed

Scenario: The design document matches what shipped
  Given 26-chart-engine-design.md sections 3, 6, 7, 8 and 13
  When each is compared against the implementation
  Then every documented interface, message, budget and benchmark gate matches the code
  And each deliberate divergence is recorded with its reason, not silently edited away

Scenario: Open item O2 is closed by an ADR amendment
  Given E11-K01 and E11-S11 measured the glyph set, atlas size and generation cost
  When ADR-0002 is amended
  Then the amendment records the chosen glyph set, the 1024x1024 atlas decision, the measured generation cost and the cache strategy
  And open item O2 in section 16 is marked closed with a link to the amendment

Scenario: A downstream team can write a plugin from the docs alone
  Given a developer from the E13 indicators team with no prior engine exposure
  When they follow the plugin authoring guide in the package README
  Then they can implement and register a working indicator plugin without asking the engine team a question
  And this is verified by actually doing it during the handoff session

Scenario: Every exported symbol is documented
  Given the public API surface
  When TSDoc coverage is measured
  Then every exported symbol has a description, and every plugin interface has a usage example
  And a missing TSDoc comment on an exported symbol fails lint
```

## Technical notes / design
**The API report is the mechanism, not the policy.** A generated `.api.md` committed to the repo turns "did we change the public API?" from a judgement call in review into a diff. It is the cheapest possible enforcement of an interface freeze and the reason this Task is 3 points rather than a documentation marathon.

**What "frozen" means in practice**, written down so it is not re-litigated per PR:
- Additive changes (new optional option, new event, new plugin hook with a default) — minor bump, no sign-off.
- Breaking changes (removed/renamed export, changed signature, changed semantics) — major bump, migration note, sign-off from every consuming Epic lead.
- `unstable_`-prefixed exports — outside the freeze, may change in any release, and may not be used by another Epic without an explicit note in that Epic's ticket.

**Divergence recording.** Where implementation diverged from design, the doc gets a short "Shipped behaviour differs: … because …" note rather than a rewrite. A design document quietly retrofitted to match the code loses the history of why, which is the main thing a reader six months later needs.

## Test plan
- **CI check**: API report diff detection (self-tested by adding a throwaway export and asserting the check fails).
- **Lint rule**: missing TSDoc on an exported symbol fails.
- **Doc-example compilation**: every code example in the README and in TSDoc is type-checked as part of the build, so examples cannot rot silently.
- **Storybook coverage check**: asserts a story exists for each of CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226.
- **Handoff verification**: the "developer writes a plugin from the docs alone" scenario is executed with a real E13 engineer during the handoff session and its outcome recorded on the ticket.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this Task produces documentation, a version policy and a CI check.

Two security-relevant points to record in the README rather than leave as folklore. First, the engine's **no-I/O invariant** (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16) is part of the public contract — a plugin that performs `fetch`, opens a WebSocket or touches storage violates it, and the framework-free boundary check enforces it. Second, the **plugin seam is a trust boundary in the making**: plugins are first-party TypeScript compiled into the bundle in v1, so they carry the app's privileges. Any future third-party or user-authored plugin would need a sandbox, and the README states this explicitly so nobody later assumes the seam was designed for untrusted code. Reviewed as part of **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
The plugin authoring guide must state the accessibility obligations a plugin inherits, because a plugin that draws to the canvas without registering mirror units is an accessibility regression that no automated check will catch:
- Any plugin rendering a focusable unit **must** register it with the DOM mirror (E11-S13).
- Any plugin encoding meaning **must** use a registered pattern/hatch in addition to colour (E11-T04).
- Any plugin adding a surface with data **must** contribute columns to the SCR-045 table (E11-S14).
These are documented as contract requirements with the rationale, not listed as suggestions.

## Performance notes
The plugin guide documents the frame-path rules every plugin must honour: no allocation in the frame path, no string formatting per frame (use cached glyph runs), batch by style, respect the LOD level supplied by the engine, and stay within the draw-call budget (<=18 per pane). The engine cannot enforce these at runtime without cost, so they are contract plus review plus the benchmark gate — which is why the benchmark harness (E11-T06) is a required check on the package.

## Observability
The engine error-code table is published in the README as the canonical list, so support and the diagnostics overlay share one vocabulary. The API report file doubles as a changelog input for the package.
